area: Menu bar, navigation, project and recovery controls
summary: The five menus are File, Edit, View, Analysis and Help. Analysis is organized into Detect, Curate, Explore this recording, Compare recordings and Export. Analysis home and the launcher provide named routes into the shared Analysis Explorer; Event inspector and Event gallery remain dedicated curation surfaces. Enabled actions depend on the selected source, sample rate, stored results and optional dependencies. The status bar reports cursor/sample-rate context, analysis progress and calibration warnings. This maintained control reference covers reviewed workflows, not an exhaustive census of every dynamically generated control.
opened_by: Menu bar and status bar are always available; on macOS the menu bar is at the top of the screen. Analysis home is available from Analysis and Help. Sources: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py, analysis_catalog.py, analysis_home.py, analysis_explorer.py, build_info_dialog.py; project persistence: nanoscope/core/project.py.
gotchas: Actions are gated by their actual inputs, not one universal detection prerequisite. Noise needs current and a sample rate; I-V needs current/voltage observations; event pages need stored results. Analysis home, Figure Library and Help remain available to explain requirements. Optional ML availability depends on the installed model/runtime.
Native macOS menus may not show action tooltips. Analysis home and the launcher provide visible descriptions and requirements; the Explorer uses the same canonical analysis names.

Edit > Undo has ONE entry but TWO stacks (event tables and the manual-measurement table). Which one a Ctrl+Z acts on is decided by whichever changed most recently, so read the menu label — it spells out exactly what will be undone.

"Undo — nothing on this table; the threshold detector (3 steps) on this channel" does not mean your curation is gone: it means the history lives under the OTHER detector on the same channel. Switch the active detector back and it is there.

Undo cannot reach past File > Close document. Closing a recording takes its detections, curation and undo history with it permanently — that is why closing one with events raises a confirmation naming the counts.
A segment is not a file. It lives only in this session, so closing it (or its parent) without saving a project destroys it and everything detected on it — there is nothing on disk to reopen.

File > Create segment from selection…, View > Centre selection in view and the merge-in-selection command all need the Measure region: turn on Analysis > Measure event (Ctrl+M's companion) and DRAG a region on the trace, or they stay greyed.
Ctrl+M (Add measurement to list) stays enabled even with no region drawn — press it and the status bar names what is actually missing rather than leaving you with a dead key.
Analysis > Batch detect with "Re-run all" wipes existing curation on every recording it re-detects. "Only missing" (the default) is the safe answer.

Substate fitting runs in the background from frozen inputs. Selecting another source does not erase a completed per-source fit; fits are saved in projects. A completed background result is discarded if its source, calibration, event frame or recorded analysis context changed. Cancel preserves the previous valid fit.

Generate Report figures… creates the standard report set from the selected detection, not the styled Explorer canvas. Export current figure exports that canvas; Save figure bundle preserves the image with plotted data, configuration and provenance. Read export success/failure messages before relying on a same-named file.

Calibration warnings must be reviewed, but gain=1 alone does not establish physical validity. Check source units, acquisition gain, offset and reference provenance. Fractional ΔI/I₀ is not a universal workaround: offsets, ambiguous open-pore levels and incompatible references can invalidate its interpretation too.
"rate: unknown · x-axis in samples" in the status bar means the x-axis is samples, not seconds — and it is why Run detection, Batch detect and Noise spectrum are greyed for that recording.

File > Open Project REPLACES the whole session rather than merging into it, and Ctrl+S on a project whose recordings could not all be loaded still keeps the unloadable records — but a project whose segments' parents are closed will warn you and, if you save anyway, keep the title's • so you know work is still only in memory.

Opening a second recording SHOWS only that one; the others stay open but invisible. Tick a channel in the File Manager (or right-click > add to view) to draw them alongside — View > Overlay/Stacked only decides whether comparable channels share a pane.
Cancel in the status bar does not always mean the work stopped: if it reads "Cancelling — the run is finishing in the background", a core is still busy and the result is merely being discarded.

Save Project refuses to silently overwrite a project another window (or program) wrote since this one last read it — a conflict dialog with Cancel as the default offers Save Project As… to keep both versions.
At the per-table undo ceiling the Edit menu says the history was evicted ("…is at its 30-step ceiling — N of your steps have been evicted"), never the never-edited wording.

Project files preserve recording references, calibration notes, supported analytical workspaces, fitted substates and Figure Library snapshots; raw recordings are not embedded. Keep referenced source data accessible.
Recovery is a safety net, not a replacement for explicit project saves. Recover opens unsaved work; Discard permanently removes both recovery generations; Not now preserves the offer.

controls.label: Open…
controls.what_it_does: Opens a file dialog to pick one or more recordings to load. Filters offered: "Recordings (*.abf *.h5 *.hdf5 *.tdms *.csv *.txt)", "Axon ABF (*.abf)", "HDF5 (*.h5 *.hdf5)", "TDMS (*.tdms)", "Text trace (*.csv *.txt)", "All files (*)".
controls.notes: Dialog title is "Open recording(s)"; it reopens in the last folder you used. Files are loaded one at a time through a single queue. Opening a recording SHOWS it and hides every other recording's layers (nothing is closed) — a status message says how many others stay open and that you tick a channel in the File Manager to overlay them. A file already open is never loaded twice. A file over the working sample ceiling raises a "Large file" dialog offering "Load first 15,000,000" (the ceiling, formatted), "Load a range…", "Load all anyway" and "Cancel". You can also drag and drop files onto the window instead.

controls.label: Open Recent
controls.what_it_does: Submenu listing the last 10 recordings you opened, by file name; picking one reopens it. Each entry's tooltip is its full path.
controls.notes: Shows a single disabled item reading "(none)" when the list is empty. Entries whose file no longer exists are dropped when the app starts. Ends with a separator and "Clear recent".

controls.label: (none)
controls.what_it_does: Placeholder shown when no recordings have been opened yet.
controls.notes: Permanently disabled — it is a label, not a command. The same placeholder appears in Open Recent Project.

controls.label: Clear recent
controls.what_it_does: Empties the recent-recordings list.
controls.notes: Only appears when the list is non-empty. Does not touch any file on disk.

controls.label: Open Project…
controls.what_it_does: Reopen a saved .nanoscope project: its documents, calibrations, layers, detections (with curation) and manual measurements are all restored. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: REPLACES the current session — it never merges. If you have unsaved work you get a Save / Discard / Cancel prompt first, and the project file is validated before anything in the current session is touched. Restoring is asynchronous; when it settles the status bar says "Project restored." — unless you cancelled it, in which case it says "Project restore cancelled — N of its recording(s) were not loaded. They are still in the project." and the title KEEPS its •, because the session now holds less than the file does. A cancelled restore, source files that could not be found, source files that were found but the reader refused (each with the reader's own reason), segments whose parent is absent, unusable stored calibrations, and records re-attached by channel name or naming a channel that is gone are all reported in a dismissible banner above the trace rather than blocking the open. If a source file on disk is no longer the one the project was saved from, the banner says so and counts how many restored events now fall past the end of the recording.

controls.label: Open Recent Project
controls.what_it_does: Submenu listing the last 10 .nanoscope projects, by file name; picking one reopens it. Each entry's tooltip is its full path.
controls.notes: Shows a disabled "(none)" when empty. Ends with a separator and "Clear recent projects". Same unsaved-work guard as Open Project….

controls.label: Clear recent projects
controls.what_it_does: Empties the recent-projects list.
controls.notes: Only appears when the list is non-empty.

controls.label: Save Project…
controls.what_it_does: Save the whole analysis to a .nanoscope project file so nothing is lost on relaunch. Re-saves the current project in place once it has a path. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Falls through to Save Project As… the first time (no path yet). Raw signal is NOT stored — file-backed recordings are saved as path references plus the sample range you loaded, and segments as a crop spec re-derived from their parent. A save whose segments have no open parent WARNS first ("N segment(s) cannot be saved in this project", with "Save without them" / "Cancel") and, if you save anyway, deliberately leaves the window still marked dirty. Records from a project you opened that are not open in this session — a source that could not be read, or one whose load you cancelled — are written back out verbatim, never dropped, and the status line says so: "N recording(s) that are not open in this session were kept in the project, not dropped.", plus "N record(s) this project holds but could not be re-attached were kept in it, not dropped." for everything else the restore could not install.

controls.label: Save Project As…
controls.what_it_does: Always prompts for a .nanoscope path and saves the whole analysis there, then adopts that file as the current project.
controls.notes: Typing a name without the .nanoscope suffix still writes (and warns about overwriting) the suffixed file, so "study" over an existing study.nanoscope raises the overwrite prompt rather than silently replacing it. The window title becomes "NanoScope — <file name>".

controls.label: Create segment from selection…
controls.what_it_does: Crop the current on-trace selection (turn on Measure and drag a region) into a new derived recording in the Files list, analysed independently of the parent. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until a recording is selected AND the on-trace Measure region spans at least 2 samples — turn on Analysis > Measure event and drag a region on the trace. It is the twin of the "Segment" button in the File Manager dock; both are enabled and disabled together. Prompts for a name, prefilled as "‹parent name› [t0–t1 s]". A segment exists only in memory: it is not a file, so closing it or its parent without saving the project loses it and everything detected on it. Creating one marks the session unsaved.

controls.label: Close document
controls.what_it_does: Closes the currently selected recording, dropping its layers, calibration and detection results from the session.
controls.notes: DESTRUCTIVE and beyond the reach of Undo — "undo cannot reach past a close". If the recording carries detected events you get a "Close recording" confirmation naming the counts (accepted / rejected / hand-added) with "Close and discard the events" vs "Keep it open" (Keep it open is the default). If segments were cut from it, an earlier dialog asks "Close it and its N segment(s)" / "Close only this recording" / "Cancel". Does nothing when no recording is selected. The File Manager dock's Close button lands on exactly the same guarded path.

controls.label: Quit
controls.what_it_does: Closes the window and exits the application.
controls.notes: With unsaved analysis AND something a save would keep (open recordings, or saved manual measurements), you get an "Unsaved work" prompt — "You have unsaved analysis. / Save your project first?" — with Save (default), Discard and Cancel. A cancelled or failed Save keeps the window open. Window geometry, dock layout and both recent lists are written to settings on the way out; background jobs are asked to stop and given up to 2.5 s.

controls.label: Undo
controls.what_it_does: Walks back the most recent change to an event table or to the manual-measurement table — a re-run detection that replaced your curation, accept/reject decisions, mask edits, a deleted measurement row. The status bar confirms with "Undone: <what>."
controls.notes: THE LABEL CHANGES TO TELL YOU WHAT IT WILL DO, because a greyed menu item cannot explain itself and macOS never renders menu tooltips. Five wordings: "Undo <what>"; "Undo — nothing on this table; the threshold detector (N steps) on this channel" (the history exists but under the other detector); "Undo — this table's history was dropped at the memory ceiling (N step(s) lost)" (the history was real and was thrown away to stay under the 128 MiB session ceiling — the status bar says so at the moment it happens); "Undo — nothing to undo on this event table"; or a plain "Undo". DISABLED when neither table has an undoable step. There is only ONE Undo and two separate stacks (event tables vs the measurement table); which one a press acts on is decided by which changed most recently. Depth is 30 steps PER EVENT TABLE, so curating one recording can no longer evict another recording's history; only the byte ceiling is session-wide. The labels are recomputed every time you open the Edit menu, and any edit that was made without announcing itself is committed at that moment. Safe to press inside the detection form's text and spin boxes — there it undoes your typing. Cannot reach past a closed recording.

controls.label: Redo
controls.shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+Z, plus the platform standard QKeySequence.Redo (Ctrl+Y on Windows)
controls.what_it_does: Re-applies the change you just undid, on whichever table it belonged to. The status bar confirms with "Redone: <what>."
controls.notes: Same self-describing label scheme as Undo ("Redo <what>", "Redo — nothing on this table; …", "Redo — this table's history was dropped at the memory ceiling (N step(s) lost)", "Redo — nothing to redo on this event table", "Redo"). DISABLED when there is nothing to redo. A new edit ends the redo branch of the recordings that edit actually touched — on both stacks — and leaves every other recording's branch alone.

controls.label: Overlay
controls.what_it_does: Draws comparable channels from different recordings on the SAME pane so they sit on top of each other.
controls.notes: Checkable, and mutually exclusive with Stacked (one radio group). The check follows the session, so flipping the mode from the File Manager updates this tick too. Which recordings are drawn at all is controlled by the channel tick boxes in the File Manager, not here.

controls.label: Stacked
controls.what_it_does: Gives each channel its own pane, stacked vertically, instead of overlaying them.
controls.notes: Checkable, mutually exclusive with Overlay.

controls.label: Zoom Back
controls.what_it_does: Return to the previous view — reject an event and keep scanning. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Steps back through the trace's own zoom/pan history; it does not undo any data change.

controls.label: Zoom Forward
controls.what_it_does: Steps forward again through the zoom history after using Zoom Back.
controls.notes: No tooltip is set on this action.

controls.label: Reset zoom
controls.shortcut: Ctrl+0 window-wide; Home while the trace is focused
controls.what_it_does: Zoom all the way back out to the full trace. The Full button below the plot does the same; Home also works while the trace itself has focus. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Home is trace-scoped so it does not steal the normal go-to-first-row action from tables and lists.

controls.label: Centre selection in view
controls.what_it_does: Slide the view (without changing the zoom) so the Measure selection sits in the middle — the keyboard twin of dragging the pan bar under the trace. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until a Measure region exists on the trace (turn on Analysis > Measure event and drag). Unlike Create segment it accepts even a one-sample cursor pair. If you trigger it with nothing selected, the status bar tells you to turn on Measure and drag a region.

controls.label: Drag draws zoom box
controls.what_it_does: On: left-drag frames a region and zooms into it (dive inside an event). Off: left-drag pans. The mouse wheel moves the signal vertically; use −/+ in the Scan strip to change the time scale. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Checkable menu item, ON by default. This is a mouse-behaviour switch, not a view change — nothing on screen moves when you toggle it.

controls.label: Panels
controls.what_it_does: Submenu of checkable items that show or hide the two docks.
controls.notes: Contains exactly two entries, generated from the docks themselves.

controls.label: File Manager
controls.what_it_does: Shows or hides the left-hand File Manager dock, which lists open recordings, their segments and their channels (with the colour swatch, Δt offset and tick boxes).
controls.notes: Checkable; also unticked by clicking the dock's own ✕. The dock is draggable and resizable; on a first launch it opens at 320 px wide, after which your own width is remembered.

controls.label: Inspector
controls.what_it_does: Shows or hides the right-hand Inspector dock, which holds the Calibration, File Info and Analysis tabs.
controls.notes: Checkable; also unticked by the dock's own ✕. Opens at 460 px on a first launch. Several commands re-open and raise this dock for you (the calibration chip, the workflow strip, and turning on Measure event).

controls.label: Detect
controls.what_it_does: Section heading (not clickable) marking the group of commands that make events: Run detection, Batch detect, Load ML model and Run ML detection.
controls.notes: Added with addSection. On some platforms a section heading renders as a plain separator line rather than as text.

controls.label: Run detection
controls.what_it_does: Run the selected classical detector on the selected current channel using the displayed scientific settings.
controls.notes: Requires a known sample rate and a valid reference/processing context. Schmitt and CUSUM operate on the whole recording; use a segment for a separately characterized excerpt. Explicit replacement may replace curation and is undoable. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py and analysis_panel.py.

controls.label: Batch detect (all open recordings)…
controls.what_it_does: Run the current Schmitt detection parameters on every open recording that has a current channel and a known sample rate, in the background. Detect the whole -1000..-200 mV series in one pass, then plot the voltage dependence. (ML detection is not offered here — it is too slow to batch over many full recordings.) (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until at least one open recording has both a current channel and a known sample rate; re-checked every time you open the Analysis menu. If some recordings already have a Schmitt detection it asks "Re-run all of them, or only the ones that are missing one?" with "Only missing" (default), "Re-run all" and "Cancel" — "Re-run all" discards existing curation on those recordings. Progress and Cancel appear in the status bar; when it finishes the status bar reports how many recordings and events were installed, how many were dropped because their recording was closed mid-run, how many were skipped for lack of a current channel/rate, and any failures.

controls.label: Load ML model…
controls.what_it_does: Load a .keras event-detector model to use for ML detection. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Needs no recording and no detection, but DISABLED when TensorFlow is not importable — the same gate the panel's own Load-model button uses — and the tooltip then reads "TensorFlow is not installed, so ML detection is unavailable. Install tensorflow (2.15) to enable it." Otherwise it opens the Analysis panel's own file dialog. Loading a model is what makes "Run ML detection…" available (together with a current channel and a known rate).

controls.label: Run ML detection…
controls.what_it_does: Run the loaded Keras ML detector on the selected current channel over the chosen range (visible view or whole recording). Inference is slow, so it runs in the background with progress and cancel. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED unless all three hold: the selection is a current channel with a known rate, TensorFlow is importable, AND a model has been loaded (from this menu or from the panel). Re-derived every time the Analysis menu opens, so it goes live as soon as a model is loaded. ML events land in the SAME event table, overlays, inspector, plots and exports as Schmitt ones, but on their own undo stack — Edit > Undo will tell you when curation lives under the other detector.

controls.label: Curate
controls.what_it_does: Section heading marking the commands for judging detected events: Event inspector, Measure event, Add measurement to list and Compare baseline estimators.
controls.notes: Added with addSection.

controls.label: Event inspector…
controls.what_it_does: Step through the detected events one at a time: see each event's raw waveform with its baseline/level/boundaries and accept/reject it. Curation flows back to the table, the trace, the summary and the exports. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until the selected recording has a detection result. Opens a single standalone window that re-focuses rather than re-opening. It edits the SAME event table the Analysis tab shows, so accepting/rejecting there updates the trace overlays and the summary immediately, and marks the session unsaved. Also reachable by clicking the CURATE chip on the workflow strip. Ctrl+I opens it from anywhere (the twin of Ctrl+G for the gallery): on macOS the menu that holds both windows is at the top of the screen rather than on the window, and the two surfaces a curator actually lives in had no keys at all.

controls.label: Measure event
controls.what_it_does: Hand-select an event with cursors and measure its dwell, amplitude and full statistics (incl. kurtosis) live; add measurements to a saveable table. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Checkable. DISABLED until a recording is selected — it needs no detection, since it is a hand gesture. Turning it ON also raises the Inspector dock and its Analysis > Measure tab so you can see the readout; turning it OFF leaves the tabs where they are. The tick stays in step with the panel's own toggle. This is the tool whose dragged region also feeds File > Create segment from selection…, View > Centre selection in view, and the merge-in-selection command.

controls.label: Add measurement to list
controls.what_it_does: Append the region currently selected on the trace to the measurement table. Works from any tab — turn on Measure event and drag a region first. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Enabled on the same condition as Measure event (a selected recording), NOT on whether a region is drawn — deliberately, so a press always lands and can name the real blocker in the status bar: "Nothing to measure — select a recording first.", "Measure is off. Turn on Analysis ▸ Measure event, then drag a region on the trace and press Ctrl+M.", or "No region is selected on the trace — drag one across the event you want to measure, then press Ctrl+M." The shortcut lives on the menu so it works from any tab, including while the measurement panel is hidden.

controls.label: Compare baseline estimators…
controls.what_it_does: Show what re-measuring this detection against the configured open-pore estimator would change: old vs new depth per event, the ratio distribution, and how many events have a stamped baseline that moves more than 10 pA. Nothing is re-measured until you say so. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until the selected recording has a detection. Purely a report — opening it changes nothing. The outcome (or the reason it refused) is posted to the status bar by the Analysis panel; the same command is behind the stale-baseline banner's own button.

controls.label: Explore this recording
controls.what_it_does: Section heading for event/distribution, waveform, noise and exploratory report workflows.
controls.notes: The visible routes use the canonical names Distributions, Distribution summaries, Comparison figures, Event waveforms, Event gallery, Noise spectrum and Subpopulations.

controls.label: Distributions…
controls.what_it_does: Open the Distributions page in Analysis Explorer.
controls.notes: Use detected event sources or saved manual measurements. Select source checkboxes, review Data/Analysis settings, and distinguish an existing committed result from unapplied edits. Refresh explicitly when live sources change.

controls.label: Event waveforms…
controls.what_it_does: The signature translocation plots for the current detection: the 2-D dwell-vs-blockage density map (with ECD / charge-deficit as a metric) and the event-ensemble overlay with its mean and median waveform. Needs at least one accepted event. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Gated in four steps, each with its own message on the launcher strip: nothing open, nothing selected in the Files panel, no detection on the selection, or "No accepted events yet — accept at least one in the Event inspector (or tick it in the event table) to fill the density map and the ensemble." Single window; follows the selection.

controls.label: Event gallery…
controls.what_it_does: See every detected event at once as a grid of waveform tiles: sort by dwell or depth, sweep a box over the bad ones and reject them together. The inspector is for one event; this is for a thousand. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until the selected recording has a detection. It curates but is deliberately filed under Explore, not Curate. Ctrl+G opens it from anywhere, and the ▤ Event gallery button on the Analysis launcher row under the workflow strip is its always-visible door — the gallery has no chip of its own on the workflow strip, which is the gap that button fills. Bulk accept/reject from here writes the same shared table as the inspector and the event table, and marks the session unsaved. Double-clicking a tile jumps to that event in the trace and brings the main window forward.

controls.label: Noise spectrum…
controls.what_it_does: Open the current-noise power spectrum for a recording's current channel: the log-log PSD that separates 1/f (flicker), the thermal/white floor and the high-frequency dielectric/capacitance rise, plus band-integrated RMS noise. Pore quality control on the RAW calibrated trace — no detection needed. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Needs NO detection. DISABLED until at least one open recording has a live current channel with a known sample rate; when greyed the reason shown is "Open a recording first — the noise spectrum needs a current channel with a known sample rate (no detection required)." or "No open recording has a current channel with a known sample rate — the noise spectrum needs both." The open window follows your selection.

controls.label: Fit sub-state levels (CUSUM)…
controls.what_it_does: Explicitly fit CUSUM sub-states inside accepted events in a background job, without changing the event table n_levels estimate.
controls.notes: The menu action starts the job directly despite its ellipsis; it does not open a parameter dialog. Cancel is on the main status bar. The result is committed only if the frozen scientific inputs still match. Completed per-source levels and provenance can be saved in the project. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py, _fit_levels.

controls.label: Compare recordings
controls.what_it_does: Section heading marking the two cross-recording surfaces: I-V / Conductance and Voltage dependence.
controls.notes: Added with addSection.

controls.label: I-V / conductance…
controls.what_it_does: Gather (voltage, open-pore current) from every open recording, fit I vs V, and report the pore CONDUCTANCE (slope, in nS) with the leak and R². The classic pore-characterisation plot across your -1000..-200 mV runs. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Needs no detection. DISABLED until at least one open recording has BOTH a current channel and a known applied voltage (a live voltage channel, or a voltage in the file's metadata); the greyed reason names exactly that. Single window that re-gathers its points each time you open it and whenever the session changes.

controls.label: Voltage dependence…
controls.what_it_does: Plot how an event metric (capture rate, dwell, depth, dI/I₀, count) varies with the applied voltage across your detected recordings, and fit the trend (linear or the A·exp(V/V₀) capture-rate model). The classic nanopore voltage series — batch-detect first, then open this. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until at least TWO recordings each have a known applied voltage AND a stored Schmitt detection — one point is not a trend. The greyed reason carries the live count: "Needs at least 2 detected recordings with a known applied voltage — N so far. Open the voltage series and run Analysis ▸ Batch detect."

controls.label: Export
controls.what_it_does: Section heading marking the six export commands at the bottom of the Analysis menu.
controls.notes: Added with addSection.

controls.label: Export events…
controls.what_it_does: Export the current detection's events to CSV (the accepted/curated-in events), for extraction into your own tools. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: DISABLED until the selected recording has a detection. Writes TWO files — the CSV and a <stem>.meta.json provenance sidecar naming the detector, the source file, the open-pore estimator and the CLOCK the table's t_start_s is on (the recording's instrument-clock origin, carrying the same sentence the event table's own column header shows; an explicit null with a note when it is not knowable) — and the overwrite confirmation covers both. Only ACCEPTED events are written; the status bar reports "Wrote N accepted event(s) of M to <csv> (+ provenance <sidecar>)." If the write broke a hard link or followed a symlink, a dialog says so afterwards, exactly as a project save does.

controls.label: Export events for training…
controls.what_it_does: Export the selected source detector table as labelled training regions with review metadata and provenance.
controls.notes: The default is Reviewed decisions (recommended): human positives and negatives. Accepted candidates and All raw candidates are explicit alternatives. Detector acceptance is not itself human review. Reconciled unresolved rows are excluded from reviewed export until adjudicated. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py, _export_training.

controls.label: Export sub-state levels…
controls.what_it_does: Export the fitted sub-state levels (one row per event level, plus a provenance sidecar naming the CUSUM parameters). Enabled once a level fit has been run. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Enabled when the selected source has a valid stored substate fit, including a fit restored from a project. Switching sources selects that source’s fit; it does not erase the previous source’s stored fit. Export includes the per-level numerical table and CUSUM provenance.

controls.label: Export density figure…
controls.what_it_does: Export a separate multi-source 2-D KDE contour figure with marginal distributions.
controls.notes: Choose depth or fractional depth explicitly and retain source-data/metadata files. Dimensionless ΔI/I₀ is not automatically comparable: review offset, physical units, open-pore reference and pore context. This generator is separate from Export current figure in the Explorer.

controls.label: Density figure style…
controls.what_it_does: Contour levels, line width, font scale and the legend (size, position, heading, whether it carries counts). Overlaying several recordings puts the legend on top of the contours it names, so it is adjustable. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: ALWAYS enabled, even with nothing open — it only edits settings. Opens a "Density figure style" dialog with: Contour levels (2-20, default 8), Line width (0.1-5.0, default 0.7), Legend position (upper right / upper left / lower right / lower left / center right / outside right / none — "outside right" lifts the legend clear of the contours entirely; "none" removes it), Legend font size (3.0-20.0, default 6.0), Legend heading (default "molecule", blank = no heading), a "show (n = …) in the legend" checkbox (on by default; the counts stay in the exported source CSV either way) and Font scale (0.5-3.0). Settings are remembered for the session only, not saved into the project.

controls.label: Generate Report figures…
controls.what_it_does: Generate the standard dwell/depth histograms, dwell-versus-depth scatter and trace preview from the current detection.
controls.notes: Writes report figures with source-data sidecars. Does not export the styled Explorer canvas. Use Export current figure… for that, or Save figure bundle… for a frozen image/data/configuration/provenance package. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py, _export_figures.

controls.label: cursor readout
controls.what_it_does: Live time and value under the mouse on the trace, formatted "t = <value> <unit>     y = <value> <units>" — for example "t = 1.2345 s     y = -412.7 pA".
controls.notes: Reads the SELECTED channel when it is drawn. When it is not — nothing selected, or the selection hidden behind an overlay of other recordings — it falls back to the first visible layer and NAMES it, appending "  (<channel name>)" so the number is never mistaken for the selection's. Blank when nothing is drawn. Shows the time only (no y) when the cursor is off the sampled range. Minimum width 320 px.
controls.correction: The status-bar cursor label has no fixed caption; its actual text is "t = <value> <unit>     y = <value> <units>" (f"t = {xax.values[idx]:.6g} {xax.unit}     y = {float(chan.data[idx]):.6g}{units}{whose}"), where {whose} is "  (<channel name>)" whenever the y had to be borrowed from the first visible layer because the selected channel is not drawn, and "" otherwise. It falls back to just "t = <value> <unit>" when the cursor is off the data, and to an empty string when no channel is visible.

controls.label: sample-rate readout
controls.what_it_does: The selected recording's sample rate and where that number came from — the provenance word is printed verbatim (measured / file_meta / filename / unknown), e.g. "250,000 Hz · file_meta". When the rate is unknown it reads "rate: unknown · x-axis in samples" — your trace x-axis is then in samples, not seconds, and dwell times cannot be computed.
controls.notes: Blank when no recording is selected. "rate: unknown" is the condition that greys out Run detection, Batch detect and Noise spectrum.
controls.correction: The permanent right-hand status label reads either "rate: unknown · x-axis in samples" (verbatim, when the recording has no known rate) or "<rate> Hz · <provenance>" (f"{meta.sample_rate_hz:,.6g} Hz · {meta.rate_provenance.value}"); it is blank when nothing is selected.

controls.label: progress bar
controls.what_it_does: Shows how far a background job has got, with a label saying what it is: "Opening <file>…", "Analysing (<module>)…" or "Batch detecting N recording(s)…".
controls.notes: Hidden whenever no job is running. Max width 240 px.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.what_it_does: Stops whichever background job is running — a file load, a single detection, or a batch pass — and discards its result.
controls.notes: Appears only alongside the progress bar, and is only clickable while something genuinely stoppable is in flight. It tells you the truth about what happened: "Cancelled." if the worker actually stopped, or "Cancelling — the run is finishing in the background. Its result is discarded." if it could not be stopped (this happens on uninterruptible calls such as the first TensorFlow import). Nothing is ever force-killed. A multi-file open is ONE gesture, so Cancel also empties the queue behind it and says how much it dropped: " N more queued file(s) were not opened." is appended to whichever of the two sentences applies. Cancelling during a project restore ends the restore — see Open Project….

controls.label: ⚠ Current gain uncalibrated — magnitudes not physical
controls.group: Status bar (far right, permanent) — calibration chip
controls.what_it_does: Show the app’s warning for a current gain still at its default, and open Calibration when clicked.
controls.notes: This is a calibration-review cue, not an independent measurement of validity. Already physical source data may legitimately use unity gain. Resolve gain/offset/units using acquisition provenance before claiming physical amplitudes; fractional depth does not cure an uncertain offset/reference.

controls.label: ✓ Gain set: <detail>
controls.group: Status bar (far right, permanent) — calibration chip
controls.what_it_does: Show that the current-channel gain was explicitly set; click to inspect Calibration.
controls.notes: A green chip is not independent certification that the entered gain, offset, source units or reference are correct.

controls.label: No current channel
controls.group: Status bar (far right, permanent) — calibration chip
controls.what_it_does: Dim/neutral chip meaning the selected recording has no live current channel to calibrate. Tooltip: "This recording has no live current channel to calibrate."
controls.notes: Also the state shown before anything is open. A recording in this state cannot be detected on or used for a noise spectrum.

controls.label: NanoScope
controls.what_it_does: The window title. Plain "NanoScope" with no project open; "NanoScope — <file>.nanoscope" once a project has been saved or opened.
controls.notes: Window opens at 1440x880 and accepts dropped files.

controls.label: • NanoScope — <project>.nanoscope
controls.what_it_does: A leading bullet "• " in the title means there is UNSAVED analysis a project save would keep — a detection, a calibration edit, a curation decision, a manual measurement, a hand-cut segment, or a layer's colour/Δt.
controls.notes: This is the marker the quit prompt is tied to; if it is there, closing the window asks Save / Discard / Cancel. Merely opening or closing a recording does NOT set it unless a project is already open. It deliberately STAYS set after a save that had to drop segments whose parent is closed, so the work is not silently written off.

controls.what_it_does: Dismisses the thin advisory banner that appears under the launcher strip — used for the duplicate-representation notice ("“X” may be another representation of: Y. Both are kept open.") and for the project-restore report: a cancelled restore, sources that could not be found, sources that were found but REFUSED (each one carrying the reader's own sentence, verbatim), unrebuilt segments, unusable calibrations, records re-attached after a channel moved or naming a channel the file no longer has, and a changed source file.
controls.notes: Non-blocking and non-modal; dismissing it does not undo anything. It re-appears on the next event that raises one.

controls.label: <recording file name>
controls.what_it_does: One entry per recently opened recording, showing only the file name (Path(p).name); its tooltip carries the full path. Clicking reopens that file. Up to 10 are kept (_MAX_RECENT), most recent first.

controls.label: <project file name>
controls.what_it_does: One entry per recently opened .nanoscope project, showing only the file name; tooltip is the full path. Clicking reopens that project, which REPLACES the current session (you are asked about unsaved work first). Up to 10 are kept.

controls.label: Recordings (*.abf *.h5 *.hdf5 *.tdms *.csv *.txt)
controls.what_it_does: The file-type filter in the Open dialog. The full list of choices is "Recordings (*.abf *.h5 *.hdf5 *.tdms *.csv *.txt)", "Axon ABF (*.abf)", "HDF5 (*.h5 *.hdf5)", "TDMS (*.tdms)", "Text trace (*.csv *.txt)", "All files (*)". Multi-select is allowed — several recordings can be opened in one go.

controls.label: NanoScope project (*.nanoscope)
controls.group: File ▸ Open Project… (file dialog, titled "Open Project")
controls.what_it_does: The file-type filter in the Open Project dialog; the other choice is "All files (*)".

controls.label: Load first 15,000,000
controls.group: "Large file" dialog (raised by File ▸ Open… when a file exceeds the working ceiling)
controls.what_it_does: Loads only the first 15,000,000 samples of an over-size recording. The dialog appears automatically for any file above the 15,000,000-sample soft ceiling and states how many samples and how many times over the ceiling the file is.

controls.label: Load a range…
controls.group: "Large file" dialog (raised by File ▸ Open… when a file exceeds the working ceiling)
controls.what_it_does: Opens the "Load a sample range" dialog so you pick the exact start/stop sample window to load instead of the first N.

controls.label: Load all anyway
controls.group: "Large file" dialog (raised by File ▸ Open… when a file exceeds the working ceiling)
controls.what_it_does: Loads the entire recording despite the warning. Marked as the destructive choice — this is the option that can consume very large amounts of memory.

controls.label: Start sample
controls.group: "Load a sample range" dialog (from Large file ▸ Load a range…)
controls.what_it_does: First sample of the window to load (0 to the recording's sample count, thousands separators shown). A live hint under the fields shows the resulting "N samples · X s" (seconds only when the sample rate is known).

controls.label: Stop sample
controls.group: "Load a sample range" dialog (from Large file ▸ Load a range…)
controls.what_it_does: Last sample (exclusive) of the window to load; it starts at whichever is smaller of 15,000,000 and the file length. If Stop is not greater than Start the range is treated as empty and nothing is loaded.

controls.label: OK
controls.group: "Load a sample range" dialog (from Large file ▸ Load a range…)
controls.what_it_does: Loads the chosen [Start, Stop) window. Cancel (beside it) abandons the open entirely.

controls.label: Only missing
controls.group: "Batch detect" conflict dialog (raised by Analysis ▸ Batch detect (all open recordings)…)
controls.what_it_does: When some open recordings already have a Schmitt detection, this runs detection only on the ones that do not, leaving existing tables (and their curation) untouched. This is the pre-selected default button.

controls.label: Re-run all
controls.group: "Batch detect" conflict dialog (raised by Analysis ▸ Batch detect (all open recordings)…)
controls.what_it_does: Re-runs detection on every eligible recording, replacing the detections that already exist. Marked destructive — replacing a table discards the curation on it (Edit ▸ Undo can put it back). Cancel abandons the batch.

controls.label: Name for the new segment:
controls.group: "Create segment" dialog (raised by File ▸ Create segment from selection…)
controls.what_it_does: Names the derived recording cut from the current Measure selection; it is prefilled with a default like "<recording> [1.234–5.678 s]" (or "[1000–2000 samp]" when the rate is unknown). Leaving it blank keeps the default. Cancel makes no segment.

controls.label: Contour levels
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: How many KDE contour lines each recording draws in the exported density figure. Range 2–20, default 8.

controls.label: Line width
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Thickness of the contour lines. Range 0.1–5.0, default 0.7.

controls.label: Legend position
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Where the legend sits: "upper right" (default), "upper left", "lower right", "lower left", "center right", "outside right", "none". Its tooltip: "outside right" lifts the legend clear of the contours entirely; "none" removes it.

controls.label: Legend font size
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Point size of the legend text. Range 3.0–20.0, default 6.0 — small on purpose, because the legend sits on top of the contours it names.

controls.label: Legend heading
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Title line above the legend entries (default "molecule"). Empty means no heading — the field shows the placeholder "(no heading)".

controls.label: show (n = …) in the legend
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Adds each recording's event count to its legend entry (on by default). Its tooltip: a legend is sized by its widest entry and the counts are the longest part of one; the counts stay in the exported source CSV either way.

controls.label: Font scale
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Overall text scaling for the density figure. Range 0.5–3.0, default 1.0.

controls.label: OK
controls.group: "Density figure style" dialog (Analysis ▸ Density figure style…)
controls.what_it_does: Stores these settings for the rest of the session — it does NOT export anything; run Export density figure… afterwards. Cancel leaves the previous style untouched. Note this menu item is one of the few that is never greyed out, even with nothing open.

controls.label: depth (pA)
controls.group: "Amplitude measure" dialog (raised by Analysis ▸ Export density figure…)
controls.what_it_does: Plots the density map against absolute blockade depth in pA. This is the pre-selected default. The dialog appears every time the export runs from the menu.
controls.notes: Absolute depth is interpretable only in the recorded signal domain with verified calibration and reference. Read the source metadata; a column named depth_pA is not itself proof that the source was physical pA.

controls.label: fractional ΔI/I₀
controls.group: "Amplitude measure" dialog (raised by Analysis ▸ Export density figure…)
controls.what_it_does: Plot fractional depth using each event’s recorded open-pore current.
controls.notes: A multiplicative factor may cancel in a ratio only under appropriate assumptions. Offset and open-pore ambiguity remain; verify comparability rather than treating this option as a calibration substitute.

controls.label: Reviewed decisions (recommended)
controls.group: "Export events for training" dialog (raised by Analysis ▸ Export events for training…)
controls.what_it_does: Export human-reviewed positive and negative decisions, with unresolved curation conflicts excluded.
controls.notes: Recommended default for supervised-learning data; acceptance by the detector alone is not a reviewed decision. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py, _export_training.

controls.label: All raw candidates
controls.group: "Export events for training" dialog (raised by Analysis ▸ Export events for training…)
controls.what_it_does: Export all rows with their provenance, including unreviewed detector decisions.
controls.notes: Explicitly broader than the recommended human-reviewed export. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py, _export_training.

controls.label: Close it and its <n> segment(s)
controls.group: "Close recording" dialog (segments exist; raised by File ▸ Close document or the Files-dock Close button)
controls.what_it_does: Closes the parent recording together with every segment cut from it. Destructive: a segment lives only in this session, so its detections go with it. The exact text substitutes the number, e.g. "Close it and its 3 segment(s)".

controls.label: Close only this recording
controls.group: "Close recording" dialog (segments exist; raised by File ▸ Close document or the Files-dock Close button)
controls.what_it_does: Closes the parent but leaves its segments open. Be aware the dialog warns those segments can no longer be saved in a project, because a project stores a segment as a crop of a parent that must be open.

controls.label: Close and discard the events
controls.group: "Close recording" dialog (unsaved detection; raised by File ▸ Close document or the Files-dock Close button)
controls.what_it_does: Closes the recording and throws away its detection and every accept/reject decision on it. Destructive and unrecoverable — Undo cannot reach past a close, so save the project first if you want to keep them.

controls.label: Keep it open
controls.what_it_does: Cancels the close. This is the default button and the Escape button, so Enter or Esc keeps the recording.

controls.label: Save without them
controls.group: "Save Project" dialog (segments whose parent is closed; raised by File ▸ Save Project… / Save Project As…)
controls.what_it_does: Writes the project anyway, accepting that the listed segments — and any results on them — will be missing when the project is reopened. Marked destructive; the alternative is to reopen the parent recording(s) and save again.

controls.label: Save
controls.group: "Unsaved work" dialog (raised when quitting, or when opening a project over the current session)
controls.what_it_does: Saves the project first, then continues with the quit or the project open. This is the pre-selected default button; the dialog reads "You have unsaved analysis." / "Save your project first?".

controls.label: Discard
controls.group: "Unsaved work" dialog (quit / Open Project over an unsaved session)
controls.what_it_does: Continues without saving — the analysis in this session is lost. Marked destructive.

controls.label: (no label — the whole main window is a drop target)
controls.what_it_does: Dragging recording files from Finder and dropping them anywhere on the NanoScope window opens them exactly as File ▸ Open… would. Not discoverable from any menu, so it belongs in the manual.

controls.label: Distribution summaries…
controls.what_it_does: Open optional ECDF, empirical-survival, box and violin controls.
controls.notes: Choose sources and Generate; opening does not generate analysis. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Comparison figures…
controls.what_it_does: Open facets, pair matrices and individual-observation plots.
controls.notes: Choose sources/metrics and Generate explicitly. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Reconcile detector results…
controls.what_it_does: Preview and build a separate union, agreement or intersection of overlapping candidates.
controls.notes: Source detector tables and their curation are preserved. Reconciliation is not new independent ground truth. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Event labels…
controls.what_it_does: Define event labels for shared review in the Inspector and gallery.
controls.notes: Labels are annotations, not detector validation or molecular identification. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Mark selection as missed event
controls.what_it_does: Add the Measure selection as a reviewed missed event to the active source detector table.
controls.notes: Ctrl+Shift+M; different from Ctrl+M, which appends to the separate measurement notebook. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Noise spectrum of the measured region
controls.what_it_does: Open noise analysis over the exact Measure selection.
controls.notes: Selection travels as sample indices, avoiding instrument-clock versus recording-relative time confusion. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Generate Subpopulations…
controls.what_it_does: Explicitly generate an exploratory report from accepted event waveforms.
controls.notes: A statistical group is not an identified molecule. Review the report caveats and stability evidence. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Open saved Subpopulations…
controls.what_it_does: Reopen a project-stored report without PCA, clustering, mixture or bootstrap recomputation.
controls.notes: Saved reports may differ from live inputs; inspect their source/status. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Export processed trace…
controls.what_it_does: Export conditioned samples to CSV with a processing metadata sidecar.
controls.notes: Uses the cursor selection when present, otherwise the recording. Requires a current channel, sample rate and a real processing chain; read the gate if disabled. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Figure Library…
controls.what_it_does: Open named frozen figures in this project.
controls.notes: Separate from Event gallery. Save Project to persist newly added snapshots. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Analysis home…
controls.what_it_does: Open the analysis catalogue and input requirements.
controls.notes: Navigation itself does not run a scientific analysis. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Guided first analysis…
controls.what_it_does: Open the optional step-by-step workflow aid.
controls.notes: The guide does not automatically calibrate, preprocess, detect or approve events. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Analysis home…
controls.what_it_does: Open the analysis catalogue.
controls.notes: Specialist workflows remain directly available through Analysis and the Explorer. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: About NanoScope…
controls.what_it_does: Show the running build identity and diagnostics.
controls.notes: Use this to distinguish an installed build from a source checkout or older app. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Copy diagnostics
controls.what_it_does: Copy build/runtime diagnostics for a reproducible support report.
controls.notes: Inspect the copied information before sharing it outside the lab. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Accepted candidates
controls.what_it_does: Export accepted rows without requiring human review.
controls.notes: Explicit legacy mode; not equivalent to reviewed positive/negative training labels. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Recover
controls.what_it_does: Open a validated recovery snapshot as unsaved work.
controls.notes: Save the project explicitly after recovery; recovery is not the normal Save workflow. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Discard
controls.what_it_does: Permanently remove both recovery generations.
controls.notes: Destructive: choose only if the offered unsaved work is no longer needed. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Show in Finder
controls.what_it_does: Reveal the offered recovery artifact.
controls.notes: Does not restore the session or save it as a normal project. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

controls.label: Not now
controls.what_it_does: Dismiss the recovery offer without discarding it.
controls.notes: Also the escape action; does not recover or permanently delete the snapshot. Source: nanoscope/gui/main_window.py; build_info_dialog.py.

area: File Manager, calibration and source identity
summary: File Manager lists recordings, their segments and channels, grouped by nominal voltage. Selecting a recording shows it; channel checkboxes and Add to view provide overlays. Calibration applies calibrated = raw × gain + offset, with explicit target units and channel-kind overrides. Verify acquisition metadata, gain, offset and units before interpreting physical magnitudes. A numerical gain of 1 alone is not proof of either valid calibration or invalid data: already physical traces can legitimately use unity gain, whereas acquisition-specific scale factors may remain unverified.
opened_by: File Manager is the left dock (View → Panels → File Manager). Calibration is the first Inspector tab; File Info and Analysis are adjacent. The status-bar calibration chip also opens Calibration. Sources: nanoscope/gui/file_dock.py, calibration_panel.py, main_window.py; nanoscope/core/sources.py and project.py.
gotchas: Verify the acquisition scale rather than diagnosing it from gain=1 alone. Unity gain is legitimate for an already physical trace; an ABF whose current-channel gain is unverified remains illustrative for amplitudes, ECD, conductance and noise until that provenance is resolved.
Clicking a recording SWITCHES to it — it does not add it. The only ways to get two recordings on the same axes are ticking a channel of each, or right-click ▸ "Add to view (compare)".
Unticking a channel does not throw anything away: the layer keeps its colour and its Δt, and re-ticking brings it back exactly as it was.

Both Apply and Reset to default can DELETE the .npcal.json calibration file next to your raw data, and take any note stored in it with them — Apply does it the moment your typed values happen to equal the defaults, not only when you press Reset.
Calibration notes can be carried in current .nanoscope projects. Sidecar deletion/note-loss warnings still matter: save a project or preserve the notes before explicitly erasing the sidecar.

In the Raw vs calibrated box only the MEDIAN is sampled — read from a stride of at most 20,000 points — while min, max and span are exact over every sample of the channel. The title, the row tooltips and the grey line under the grid say which is which and name the stride and the counts; when the channel holds a NaN or an infinity those three rows read "—" and that line says they are not computable rather than claiming exactness over a dash.

"Command-voltage check" and "Open-pore conductance" are not disabled when unavailable — they vanish completely. A missing box means the recording has no voltage channel (or no live current channel), not that something is broken.
The Segment button stays greyed out until you turn on Measure (Analysis ▸ Measure event) and drag a region on the trace; there is nothing wrong with the button.
The Δt column is dead for files that declare no sample rate — hover it and it tells you "This file declares no sample rate; alignment is unavailable."
A recording shown in italics under a voltage heading had that voltage guessed from its filename; hover it to see "voltage inferred from filename (unreliable)" before you rely on the grouping.
Closing a recording that has segments cut from it can lose those segments — a segment can only be saved while its parent is open.
Gain 0 is refused outright, and so is a gain so tiny it underflows to zero. A negative gain is fine and is honoured — inverting headstages are legitimate.

If a Reset cannot delete the .npcal.json beside your data, the status line says the OLD file is still there and WILL re-apply its values (and any note) when you reopen the recording — the exact opposite of what a failed WRITE says ("will be gone when you reopen"), and until you delete that file by hand the session and the disk disagree.
Signal-domain metadata matters. Normalize changes the numerical domain; do not relabel normalized values as pA. A historic column name ending in _pA does not override recorded units/domain.

A known open-pore current must be signed and calibrated for this recording/channel. Do not substitute a nominal voltage, absolute current magnitude or a synthetic ground-truth value into a real recording.

controls.label: File Manager
controls.what_it_does: The left column listing every open recording, its derived segments and its channels, grouped under headings for the voltage each recording was taken at.
controls.notes: Drag its inner edge to resize; closing it (its ✕ or View ▸ Panels) gives the whole width back to the trace viewer. It never closes a file — closing the panel just hides the list.

controls.label: Overlay
controls.what_it_does: Groups comparable channels into one shared, x-linked pane, so ticked traces are drawn on top of each other.
controls.notes: Tooltip: "Overlay: group comparable channels into one x-linked pane.\nStacked: one pane per channel." Overlay and Stacked are a mutually exclusive pair — one is always pressed in. It only changes how ticked channels are laid out; it does not tick or untick anything.
controls.correction: Both are CHECKABLE toggle buttons in an exclusive QButtonGroup — exactly one is always pressed in, so they behave as a radio pair rather than as two independent buttons. Shared tooltip: "Overlay: group comparable channels into one x-linked pane. / Stacked: one pane per channel."

controls.label: Stacked
controls.what_it_does: Gives every drawn channel its own pane instead of sharing one.
controls.notes: Exclusive with Overlay. Same tooltip as Overlay.
controls.correction: Both are CHECKABLE toggle buttons in an exclusive QButtonGroup — exactly one is always pressed in, so they behave as a radio pair rather than as two independent buttons. Shared tooltip: "Overlay: group comparable channels into one x-linked pane. / Stacked: one pane per channel."

controls.label: Segment
controls.what_it_does: Creates a new derived recording from the current on-trace selection. Tooltip: "Create a new derived recording from the current on-trace selection.\nTurn on Measure (Analysis ▸ Measure event) and drag a region first. The segment is analysed independently of the parent."
controls.notes: DISABLED until there is an active recording AND a live Measure region on the trace — turn on Analysis ▸ Measure event and drag a region to enable it. Twin of the File menu's "Create segment from selection…" (both do exactly the same thing). New segments appear in the tree marked with a ✂ prefix, in italic teal, with a tooltip naming the parent file and the sample range they were cut from.

controls.label: Close
controls.what_it_does: Closes the recording currently selected in the tree. Tooltip: "Close the selected document".
controls.notes: Does nothing if the selected row is a voltage group heading or nothing is selected. Twin of File ▸ Close document (Ctrl+W). If the recording has segments cut from it, closing it is a data-loss decision — a segment can only be saved while its parent is open — so the app raises its own warning before it goes through.

controls.label: Channel
controls.what_it_does: The tick box on every channel row means "this channel is drawn on the trace". Tooltip: "Tick to draw this channel on the trace.\nTicking channels from more than one recording draws them together — that is how you compare two runs.\nUntick to take the channel off the trace."
controls.notes: This is the ONLY way to put two recordings on the same axes — clicking a recording switches to it rather than adding it. Ticking a channel of a recording that is not on screen draws it alongside, it does not switch to it. Unticking keeps the layer's colour and Δt alignment, so re-ticking restores exactly what was there. Ticking, unticking, recolouring and Δt edits all count as unsaved work and will make the app prompt you on quit.
controls.correction: "Channel" is the tree's first COLUMN HEADER (setHeaderLabels(["Channel", "Units", "Colour", "Δt (s)"])), not the label on a checkbox. The tick box sits on each channel row and its visible text is that channel's own name from the file. Its tooltip is the user-facing wording: "Tick to draw this channel on the trace. Ticking channels from more than one recording draws them together — that is how you compare two runs. Untick to take the channel off the trace."

controls.label: Units
controls.what_it_does: Read-only column showing the channel's raw units as recorded in the file, or an em dash when the file does not declare any.
controls.notes: A channel with no usable signal is greyed out and its units read "<units>  ·  dead"; hover the channel name for the reason (e.g. "flagged dead (no signal)").

controls.label: Colour
controls.what_it_does: A small colour chip on each channel row; click it to pick that trace's colour. Tooltip: "Click to change this layer's colour".
controls.notes: The chip is HIDDEN entirely until the channel is ticked — an untick makes it disappear rather than grey out. Opens a colour picker titled "Layer colour". This is how you tell overlaid comparison traces apart.

controls.label: Δt (s)
controls.what_it_does: Slides this trace left or right along the time axis so it lines up with the others. Tooltip: "Shift this layer along the time axis to align it with others".
controls.notes: Six decimal places, range −1,000,000 to 1,000,000 s, arrow step 0.001 s, suffix " s". Value is only committed when you press Enter or leave the box, not on every keystroke. DISABLED until the channel is ticked. Also permanently disabled for files with no declared sample rate, where the tooltip changes to "This file declares no sample rate; alignment is unavailable."

controls.label: Unknown voltage
controls.what_it_does: The bold heading recordings are filed under when the app could not work out what bias they were taken at. Recordings whose voltage is known sit under headings like "-600 mV", sorted high to low, with this group last.
controls.notes: Not clickable — it is a grouping row only. A recording whose voltage was merely GUESSED FROM ITS FILENAME is drawn in italic and its tooltip says "voltage inferred from filename (unreliable)"; do not trust that grouping for analysis.
controls.correction: "Unknown voltage" is a grouping ROW inside the File Manager tree (the last group, for recordings whose voltage could not be determined), not a table.

controls.label: Click a recording to show it · tick channels to draw them together
controls.what_it_does: The dimmed one-line hint under the tree. Its full tooltip spells the rule out: "Opening or clicking a recording displays it on its own; the others stay open.\nTo compare recordings, tick the channel of each one you want drawn — or right-click a recording and choose “Add to view”.\nOverlay/Stacked then decide whether the ticked channels share a pane or get one each."
controls.notes: The line is shortened with an ellipsis when the dock is narrow — hover it to read the whole thing.

controls.label: Show only this recording
controls.what_it_does: Draws this recording on its own; the others stay open and listed. Tooltip: "Draw this recording on its own; the others stay open."
controls.notes: Greyed out when this recording is already the only thing on the trace. It does not close anything — the recordings you switch away from keep their colours, their alignment and their results.

controls.label: Add to view (compare)
controls.what_it_does: Draws every live channel of this recording ALONGSIDE what is already on the trace. Tooltip: "Draw this recording ALONGSIDE what is already on the trace."
controls.notes: Greyed out when this recording is already the only thing shown. This is the coarse version of ticking channels one at a time; use it when you just want "show me both runs".

controls.label: Close recording
controls.what_it_does: Closes the recording you right-clicked.
controls.notes: Same handler as the Close button and File ▸ Close document (Ctrl+W), including the warning about segments cut from it.

controls.label: Calibration
controls.what_it_does: Edits the gain, offset and units for whichever channel is selected in the File Manager, previewing the effect live before you commit it.
controls.notes: First tab of the Inspector dock. Clicking the calibration chip in the status bar raises the Inspector and jumps straight here. The panel follows the File Manager selection — select a channel row to calibrate that channel, or a recording row to land on its first live current channel.

controls.label: No channel selected
controls.what_it_does: The heading at the top of the panel when nothing is selected. With a channel selected it reads "<channel name>   ·   <channel kind>   ·   <raw units>".
controls.notes: When it says "No channel selected" every field and button below it is disabled. It also reverts to this the moment the recording you were calibrating is closed.

controls.label: provenance: <value>
controls.what_it_does: A coloured badge saying where this calibration came from — green "measured", blue "file metadata", amber "filename", grey "unknown" — followed by any advisory note stored with it.
controls.notes: The note is worth reading: for ABF voltage channels it explains whether the app applied the 10× correction ("ABF voltage is stored 10x too large; verify against your protocol") or decided the channel already reads the real bias. Pressing Apply on your own edit sets provenance to "unknown" but keeps the note.
controls.correction: Incomplete: the badge is `provenance: {value}` followed by `  ·  {note}` whenever the calibration carries a note (e.g. the 10× headstage explanation), and the text is colour-coded by provenance — green for measured, blue for file metadata, orange for filename-derived (unreliable), grey for unknown.

controls.label: Gain
controls.what_it_does: The number every sample is multiplied by. Type the amplifier's real conversion factor here to turn raw file values into physical current or voltage.
controls.notes: Text box, accepts scientific notation (e.g. 2.5e3). Press Enter to Apply directly. Everything below updates as you type, before you commit. DISABLED until a real recording's channel is selected. Zero is refused, and so is anything non-finite — the panel says why instead of applying it.

controls.label: Offset
controls.what_it_does: A constant added to every sample after the gain, for removing a baseline shift in the amplifier.
controls.notes: Same rules as Gain: scientific notation allowed, Enter applies, live preview, disabled with no selection.

controls.label: Target units
controls.what_it_does: What to call the calibrated values — e.g. type pA or nA so axes and read-outs are labelled correctly. Placeholder: "raw units unchanged".
controls.notes: Leaving it empty keeps the file's own units. This label is what decides whether the conductance read-out can give you nanosiemens at all: unrecognised current units make the nS figure unavailable.

controls.label: Treat this channel as
controls.what_it_does: Which pane this channel gets and how it is grouped with the others. (Verbatim tooltip: "Which pane this channel gets and how it is grouped with the others. Leave it alone unless the file declared the channel wrongly or not at all.") Entries: "as the file declares" (the default) plus the override kinds.
controls.notes: This is the OTHER half of the same correction the units box makes: answering only the units question relabels the y axis and leaves the pane ordered as whatever the file declared, so a channel corrected to pA still sorted below the voltage and two recordings of one experiment opened with their panes in opposite orders. It changes NO number — it is not part of the calibration fingerprint and reaches no sample, so there is no live preview of it; it decides which pane the channel lands in and which overlay group it shares, and only once Apply commits it. It is also the only way to separate a TDMS whose channels are BOTH raw Volts, which overlay as one (kind, units) group until something says which one is the current. Saved with the project (format v8); a project written by an older build carries no override, which reads as "no override, the header stands" and leaves the sidecar's own value alone.

controls.label: calibrated = raw × <gain> + <offset>
controls.what_it_does: The live formula line, restating exactly what will be done to your data. When the typed values cannot be used it is replaced by the reason.
controls.notes: The three refusal messages you may see here: "gain/offset: enter a number"; "gain/offset: enter a finite number — an infinite one makes every sample infinite"; and "gain 0 would make every sample exactly the offset — that deletes the recording rather than scaling it. Use a small gain, not zero." While any of these show, the Calibrated column stays as dashes and Apply does nothing.

controls.label: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: A two-column table ("Raw" and "Calibrated") showing median, min, max and span of the selected channel, so you can see the effect of the gain before committing it. Two lines underneath: a grey coverage line reading "min / max / span: exact over all 749,651 samples.   median: every 37th sample (20,261 of 749,651).", and "units: raw = … calibrated = …".
controls.notes: The title says which rows are which, because the box used to be titled "(sampled)" over four rows of which only the median was robust to the stride: min, max and span are now computed over EVERY sample (Session.raw_extremes), and the calibrated column is the exact raw extreme through the same float32 arithmetic Apply uses. Only the median is read from the stride, which is robust to it on a stationary trace. Measured before the fix, on the owner's -500 mV recording (12,502,631 samples, every 625th read): strided max -7.63 pA against a true +5.49, min -215.5 against -281.7, span 207.8 against 287.2 — all printed as plain numbers. The Calibrated column shows dashes whenever the typed gain/offset are unusable (including a finite gain that overflows float32 on this channel), and min/max/span read "—" on a channel holding a NaN or an infinity, with the coverage line saying they are not computable.
controls.correction: Title string is verbatim, but it is a QGroupBox holding a grid of read-only labels — nothing in it can be edited or sorted. The box's own tooltip restates the coverage: "min, max and span are exact over all N samples; the median is read from every Kth sample (M of N)."

controls.label: Command-voltage check
controls.what_it_does: Sanity-checks the voltage calibration: it shows "Measured median (raw)", "× gain", "= effective" and "Nominal (grouping)" so you can confirm the calibrated command voltage matches the bias you meant to apply.
controls.notes: The whole box is HIDDEN for recordings with no voltage channel. "Nominal (grouping)" is the voltage the File Manager filed the recording under — if "= effective" and it disagree badly, either the voltage gain is wrong or the filename lied. When the voltage channel is the one selected, the row tracks the gain you are typing; otherwise it uses the voltage channel's committed gain.
controls.correction: The title string is verbatim, but it is a QGroupBox of read-only label rows, not a table — and, critically, the whole box is INVISIBLE unless the selected recording has a voltage channel.

controls.label: Open-pore conductance
controls.what_it_does: The physical reality check: "Open-pore current I₀", "Applied voltage V" and the headline "G = I₀ / V" in nanosiemens, recomputed live as you dial the current gain. Dial the gain until G lands in a physical range for your pore (a 22 nm pore in 1× PBS sits near ~100 nS).
controls.notes: HIDDEN when the recording has no live current channel. It is shown whichever channel you have selected — the gain lives on the current channel but its effect is the point. The caption underneath tells you the unit scaling (e.g. "pA / mV -> nS") and whether V was measured on the command channel or taken from the filename/header; it reads "no applied voltage known for this recording" when neither is available. G shows a dash when the voltage is zero or the current units are not recognised.
controls.correction: Title string is verbatim, but it is a QGroupBox of read-only label rows, not a table, and the whole box is INVISIBLE unless the recording has a live (non-dead) current channel.

controls.label: Reset to default
controls.what_it_does: Puts this channel back to the calibration the app worked out when the file was opened, discarding your edits.
controls.notes: DESTRUCTIVE. If this leaves every channel of the recording at its default, it DELETES the <datafile>.npcal.json file sitting next to your raw data — you get a warning titled "Reset calibration" reading "Reset will delete <name>.npcal.json." with buttons "Reset and delete the file" and "Cancel" (Cancel is the default). If the file survives but a channel's note would be dropped from it, you instead get "Reset will erase N calibration note(s) from <name>", quoting each note in full — that note exists nowhere else and a project file cannot carry it back. Disabled until a channel is selected.

controls.label: Apply
controls.what_it_does: Commits the typed gain, offset and target units to the selected channel and immediately re-renders the affected traces — no reload.
controls.notes: The panel's default button; pressing Enter in Gain, Offset or Target units does the same thing. Does nothing while the formula line is showing a refusal. Apply can be destructive too: if your typed values happen to equal the defaults it deletes the .npcal.json sidecar, and it raises the same warnings as Reset — worded with "Apply" so the prompt names the button you actually pressed. Disabled until a channel is selected.
controls.correction: Label is verbatim, but it is the dialog's DEFAULT button (setDefault(True)), so Enter anywhere in the panel triggers it. It is greyed out until a channel of a trace recording is selected, it does nothing at all while the typed gain/offset are invalid, and it can raise a destructive delete/erase confirmation when the typed values happen to equal the defaults.

controls.label: Applied · saved to <name>.npcal.json
controls.what_it_does: The status line at the very bottom, reporting what the last commit actually did to the calibration file next to your data.
controls.notes: The wordings you may see: "Applied · saved to <name>"; "Applied · <name> deleted (all channels are back at default)"; plain "Applied" (nothing needed writing); "Nothing changed." (you cancelled a warning); and the TWO failures, which say OPPOSITE things because their consequences are opposite — "Applied to this session only · could NOT update <name> — <the OS's reason>. The calibration is NOT stored next to your data and will be gone when you reopen the recording." (the write failed, so nothing is next to your data) and "Applied to this session only · could NOT delete <name> — <the OS's reason>. The OLD calibration file is still next to your data and WILL re-apply its values (and any note) when you reopen the recording." (the delete failed, so the old file survives). Read either one: your work is live, and the file on disk disagrees with it.

controls.label: <N> mV (e.g. "120 mV")
controls.what_it_does: Bold top-level heading row in the file tree. Recordings are filed under the heading for their nominal voltage, highest voltage first, with "Unknown voltage" always last (file_dock.py `_group_label`: `f"{gv:.0f} mV"`).
