The colleague listed only "Unknown voltage"; the numeric headings are the normal case. Groups start expanded, cannot be clicked or selected (flags are ItemIsEnabled only), and right-clicking one shows no menu.

controls.label: ✂ <recording name>
controls.what_it_does: A recording row shown in italic teal with a scissors prefix is a segment you cut out of another recording with the Segment button, not a file on disk. Its tooltip traces it back: "segment of <parent file>", the sample range, and t₀. It is analysed independently of its parent.

controls.label: (partial: samples 0–5,000,000)
controls.what_it_does: Suffix appended to a recording's name when only part of the file was loaded, so the numbers you see come from that sample window only, not the whole file.

controls.label: <units>  ·  dead
controls.what_it_does: A channel flagged as carrying no signal is greyed out and its Units cell reads "· dead" after the units. Its tooltip gives the reason, or "flagged dead (no signal)" when none was recorded. You can still tick it, but there is nothing to see.

controls.label: Layer colour
controls.what_it_does: Clicking the small colour chip in the Colour column opens a colour picker titled "Layer colour" so you can tell overlaid traces apart; tooltip is "Click to change this layer's colour". Caution: the chip is completely INVISIBLE until the channel's tick box is on — an unticked channel shows an empty Colour cell, not a greyed chip. Picking a colour counts as an edit and arms the unsaved-work prompt on quit.

controls.label: Raw
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Column heading for the left number column: the statistics of the untouched data as it sits in the file.
controls.correction: Title string is verbatim, but it is a QGroupBox holding a grid of read-only labels — nothing in it can be edited or sorted. Its min, max and span are exact over every sample of the channel; only the median row is read from a stride of at most 20,000 points, and the line under the grid names that stride and its counts.

controls.label: Calibrated
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Column heading for the right number column: the same statistics after the gain and offset you have typed. It updates as you type, before you press Apply. Shows "—" whenever the typed gain/offset are not usable. Its min and max are the exact raw extremes put through the same float32 arithmetic Apply uses, so the preview overflows exactly where the commit would.
controls.correction: Title string is verbatim, but it is a QGroupBox holding a grid of read-only labels — nothing in it can be edited or sorted. Its min, max and span are exact over every sample of the channel; only the median row is read from a stride of at most 20,000 points, and the line under the grid names that stride and its counts.

controls.label: median (sampled)
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Row of the preview grid: the middle value of the strided sample, raw and calibrated — the one row of the four that is NOT exact, which is why the label carries "(sampled)" and the three below it do not. It is read from at most 20,000 points in float64, ignoring non-finite samples; hover it for "Median of every Kth sample — M of N samples. Robust to the stride on a stationary trace; the exact rows are min, max and span."

controls.label: min
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Row of the preview grid: the smallest value in the channel, raw and calibrated — exact over every sample, not over the stride the median uses. Reads "—" when the channel holds a NaN or an infinity, because its extremes are then not numbers.

controls.label: max
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Row of the preview grid: the largest value in the channel, raw and calibrated — exact over every sample, not over the stride the median uses. Reads "—" when the channel holds a NaN or an infinity.

controls.label: span
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Row of the preview grid: max minus min, raw and calibrated — the quickest check that your gain has put the trace on a sensible scale. Exact over every sample, like the two rows above it, and "—" on a channel holding a NaN or an infinity.

controls.label: min / max / span: exact over all <N> samples.   median: every <K>th sample (<M> of <N>).
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: The grey coverage line under the grid: what was actually read, in numbers — the stride behind the median and the sample counts behind both halves, so no row in the box is a number of unstated provenance. Reads "every sample (25,000 of 25,000)" on a channel short enough not to be strided, adds "(NaN ignored)" / ", N non-finite ignored" when samples were skipped, and on a channel whose extremes are not numbers it reads "min / max / span: not computable — the channel holds a non-finite sample (NaN/Inf); see File info." instead of claiming exactness over three dashes.
controls.notes: Word-wrapped, so it does not widen the Inspector dock.

controls.label: units: raw = <raw units>    calibrated = <target units>
controls.group: Raw vs calibrated (min / max / span exact · median sampled)
controls.what_it_does: Footer line under the preview grid restating which units the two columns are in. Reads "raw = (unknown)" when the file declares no units; the calibrated half is dropped when neither the file nor Target units names a unit.

controls.label: Measured median (raw)
controls.what_it_does: The median of the recording's own voltage channel, straight out of the file. The whole Command-voltage check box is HIDDEN unless the recording has a voltage channel.

controls.label: × gain
controls.what_it_does: The gain being applied to that voltage channel. While you have the voltage channel itself selected it tracks the gain you are typing; when you are on any other channel it shows the voltage channel's already-applied gain.

controls.label: = effective
controls.what_it_does: Measured median × gain, in mV — the command voltage your calibration actually implies.

controls.label: Nominal (grouping)
controls.what_it_does: The voltage this recording was filed under in the File Manager tree, in mV, for comparison with "= effective". If the two disagree, the gain is wrong (or the filename lied). Shows "—" when no nominal voltage is known.

controls.label: Open-pore current I₀
controls.what_it_does: Median of the recording's first live current channel after calibration, in its calibrated units. The whole Open-pore conductance box is HIDDEN unless the recording has a live current channel — but it stays visible while you are on any channel of that recording, including the voltage one.

controls.label: Applied voltage V
controls.what_it_does: The command voltage used for the conductance, in mV: the measured voltage channel median × its gain, or the nominal (filename/header) voltage when the recording has no voltage channel.

controls.label: G = I₀ / V
controls.what_it_does: The headline open-pore conductance in nS, in bold. It recomputes live as you type a gain, so you can dial the current gain until the number is physically plausible. Shows "—" when the units or the voltage are unknown.

controls.label: <pA / mV -> nS>   ·   V measured on the command channel
controls.what_it_does: Caption under the conductance saying how the units worked out and where the voltage came from. Variants you will see: "…   ·   V from filename/header (nominal)" when there is no voltage channel; "no applied voltage known for this recording"; and, when a unit cannot be converted, a refusal that names EVERY blocking unit rather than the first — "current units (unknown) -> conductance not in nS", "voltage units (unknown) -> conductance not in nS", or both joined with " and " ("current units (unknown) and voltage units (unknown) -> conductance not in nS", the usual case for a freshly opened HDF5 or CSV, which declares neither) — which is why G shows a dash.

controls.label: <channel name>   ·   <channel kind>   ·   <raw units>
controls.what_it_does: The bold heading at the top of the Calibration tab once a channel is selected in the File Manager — it names which channel you are about to change. It reads "No channel selected" only before you pick one, and reverts to that if you close the recording you were editing.

controls.label: raw units unchanged
controls.what_it_does: Greyed placeholder inside the Target units box. Leaving the box empty keeps the file's own units; type e.g. pA or nA to relabel the calibrated trace.

controls.label: gain 0 would make every sample exactly the offset — that deletes the recording rather than scaling it. Use a small gain, not zero.
controls.what_it_does: Replaces the "calibrated = raw × … + …" line when what you typed cannot be applied, and Apply silently does nothing until it is fixed. The other two wordings are "gain/offset: enter a number" (blank or non-numeric) and "gain/offset: enter a finite number — an infinite one makes every sample infinite" (e.g. 1e999).

controls.label: Apply and delete the file
controls.what_it_does: Appears in a warning dialog headed "Apply calibration" (or "Reset calibration" if you pressed Reset to default) reading "Apply will delete <file>.npcal.json." This fires whenever the commit would leave EVERY channel back at its default — Reset to default always, and Apply too if you happen to type the default values. It removes the saved calibration file sitting next to your raw data, and any note stored in it is gone for good. The button reads "Reset and delete the file" when Reset raised it.

controls.label: Apply and erase the notes
controls.what_it_does: Appears in a warning dialog reading "Apply will erase N calibration notes from <file>.npcal.json." when the commit drops a channel's note out of a sidecar that otherwise survives. The dialog prints each note in full, because nothing else on your machine has a copy — copy anything you need before confirming. Singular form is "Apply and erase the note", and "Reset …" when Reset raised it.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.what_it_does: Backs out of either warning dialog; it is the pre-selected default button, so pressing Enter is safe. The status line then reads "Nothing changed." and nothing is written or deleted.

controls.label: Nothing changed.
controls.what_it_does: Status line under the buttons after you cancel a destructive confirmation.

controls.label: Applied · <file>.npcal.json deleted (all channels are back at default)
controls.what_it_does: Status line confirming the calibration file next to your data was removed because every channel is now at its default.

controls.label: Applied to this session only · could NOT update <file>.npcal.json — <reason>. The calibration is NOT stored next to your data and will be gone when you reopen the recording.
controls.what_it_does: Status line when the save failed (disk full, read-only file, disconnected volume, permissions…). The reason is the operating system's own message. Your calibration works for now but is not persisted — fix the cause and press Apply again before reopening the file.

controls.label: Applied to this session only · could NOT delete <file>.npcal.json — <reason>. The OLD calibration file is still next to your data and WILL re-apply its values (and any note) when you reopen the recording.

This is the opposite consequence to the failed-write line above it: the values you just cleared are still on disk and will re-apply themselves — fix the cause and reset again, or remove the <file>.npcal.json yourself, before reopening the recording.

area: Preprocess, recording-specific references, Schmitt/CUSUM and ML detection
summary: Inspector → Analysis contains Preprocess, Detection, ML and Measure tabs. Essential/Advanced controls change visibility, not scientific settings. Preprocess separates Signal chain from Open-pore baseline. Eight conditioning stages and a processed preview make the execution chain visible. New Schmitt/CUSUM runs with high-pass use it for candidate localization while measuring amplitudes on a companion chain with high-pass omitted; boundary-dependent measurements can still change. Detection selects Schmitt trigger (hysteresis) or Sequential CUSUM and explicit thresholds, dwell, merge and polarity. ML has its own model-specific preprocessing. User-supplied open-pore references are explicit, recording/channel-specific Schmitt/CUSUM inputs, not a universal correction.
opened_by: Inspector → Analysis → Preprocess / Detection / ML / Measure. Detect is also Analysis → Run detection (Ctrl+D). Baseline reference… opens the reference controls; Preprocess section selects Signal chain or Open-pore baseline. Sources: nanoscope/gui/panels.py, analysis_panel.py, baseline_panel.py, open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py and reference_context.py.
gotchas: Selecting a different recording or channel RE-SEEDS the whole detection form from that target's stored run — anything you had dialled in and not yet run is replaced without a prompt (clicking the same channel again is treated as navigation and changes nothing).
k_out is clamped live to stay strictly below k_in, so lowering k_in can silently move k_out down for you (to k_in − 0.5); when restoring settings by hand, set k_in first.
A filter stage stays ACTIVE when its page is hidden — the combo only changes what you are looking at. Check the "Active: …" line or the ● markers before running, not the page on screen.

The number in the low-pass cutoff box is not the real corner: zero-phase filtering squares the response, so the applied curve is already about -6 dB there. Read the note under the response plot for the true -3 dB frequency.

A running mean or Savitzky-Golay window can band-limit the trace far harder than the low-pass does, and the rise-time readout does not know about them — compare their -3 dB figures in the response note with the low-pass cutoff.
The High-pass stage is candidate-localization only for new Schmitt/CUSUM runs. It can still move start/end, dwell, rise/fall and ECD integration limits; for drift, prefer the Baseline drift stage.

The baseline-drift window should be substantially longer than events of interest; an overly short baseline window can absorb events. A median-smoothing window should be substantially shorter than the shortest events to preserve. Evaluate each against the recording rather than assuming a universal setting.
ASLS's smoothness (lam) is measured in block units, so changing the Baseline drift window changes what the same lam value means — retune it after any window change.

Typing in the filter and detection spin boxes only commits when you finish editing (press Enter or click away); intermediate digits are deliberately ignored so a half-typed "5000" does not trigger a full refilter.
Selecting a slower recording re-ranges the frequency boxes to that recording's Nyquist, which can pull a cutoff carried over from a faster file down to a legal value without asking.
max dwell does not delete long events — it keeps them in the table marked rejected — and it also right-truncates the dwell sample the fits use.
The polarity override is not validated against the data: forcing the wrong direction detects almost nothing rather than reporting an error.

The ML tab runs its own preprocessing pipeline; the general Preprocess filter chain does not tune its model input. This does not make measurement references irrelevant: accepted Automatic reference windows can still feed event characterization. Check the saved model pipeline and measurement-reference provenance separately.

The open-pore baseline is a separate Preprocess section. Detector runs consume the explicitly configured reference/window settings; changing a draft does not retroactively rewrite an existing table. Preview a supported manual reference, then press Detect explicitly to apply it.

Baseline health can reveal ambiguity but cannot certify which occupied level is physically open pore. A majority-blocked or multilevel trace can make an automatic occupancy-based reference misleading even when other checks are quiet. Use defensible recording-specific evidence and retain it in reference notes.

Schmitt default minimum dwell is 0.0000200 s; CUSUM default is 0.001 s. Max dwell=0 disables that upper limit. Detector merge gap defaults to 0 ms for Schmitt and 0.5 ms for CUSUM; user-edited values may be preserved when switching.

Manual references are supported for new Schmitt/CUSUM detection on calibrated pA. High-pass, runtime baseline subtraction and normalization are incompatible and are refused, not silently disabled. Do not assume those references are supported by ML, batch, threshold sweep, null control or recovery-map workflows.

controls.label: ML
controls.what_it_does: A separate detector: a runtime-loaded Keras model with its own preprocessing and decode settings.
controls.notes: Out of scope for this section. Important interaction: 'The ML detector runs THIS pipeline, not the Preprocess tab' — nothing you set on Preprocess or Detection affects an ML run.

controls.label: Measure
controls.what_it_does: Hosts the cursor-based manual measurement tool (built elsewhere and installed into this page).
controls.notes: A bare DetectionPanel has this tab blank; in the running app the measurement tool is installed into it. Raising the tab never turns the cursors on or off.

controls.label: Low-pass
controls.what_it_does: Picks which filter stage's controls are shown below. Tooltip: "Pick a filter stage to edit. Enabled stages are marked ● here and listed in the summary below; every stage stays active whether or not its page is the one currently shown."
controls.notes: The eight items, in order, are exactly: Low-pass, High-pass, Notch, Median, Baseline drift, Running mean, Savitzky-Golay, Normalize. An enabled stage's item is rewritten with a "● " prefix (e.g. "● Notch"). Switching pages does NOT switch stages off — this control only changes what you are looking at.

controls.label: Active execution order: raw calibrated signal (no stages enabled)
controls.what_it_does: Read-only summary of the actual kernel execution order, not merely the editor order. With high-pass on it reads Candidate-localization order and states that quantitative measurement omits high-pass.
controls.notes: This is the only place the whole recipe is visible at once; the stage pages show one stage at a time.

controls.label: enable Low-pass
controls.what_it_does: Turns the low-pass filter on. With it off the detector sees the full-bandwidth trace and the rise-time line reads "rise time: — (filter disabled; full bandwidth)".
controls.notes: Unlike the other stages, the low-pass is applied inside the detector itself, so its cutoff/order/type are stamped into the run's provenance and are what decides which events get marked filter_limited. Unchecking it sends filter_cutoff_hz = None (the detector's 'off' sentinel).

controls.label: type
controls.what_it_does: Chooses the low-pass design: Bessel (default), Butterworth or Gaussian. Tooltip: "Bessel (the electrophysiology convention) has a maximally flat group delay: it preserves pulse shape and does not ring on a step. Butterworth rolls off harder for the same order but overshoots a square blockade. Gaussian has no overshoot at all and no order (it is a symmetric smoothing kernel)."
controls.notes: Items in order: Bessel, Butterworth, Gaussian. Also from the tooltip: "All three run zero-phase (forward+backward), so edges do not shift — but the magnitude is SQUARED: the response is -6 dB at the nominal cutoff, not -3 dB." Choosing Gaussian greys out the order spin.

controls.label: order
controls.what_it_does: How many poles the low-pass has. Tooltip: "Number of poles. Higher is a steeper roll-off and a longer rise time — and zero-phase filtering DOUBLES the effective order on top of this. Gaussian ignores it. 8 is the hardware convention for an Axopatch-style Bessel." Raising it cuts more high-frequency noise but blurs the fastest events further; lowering it keeps edges sharper and noisier.
controls.notes: Range 1–10, default 8. DISABLED whenever type is Gaussian, and its tooltip then reads "Gaussian is a symmetric kernel and has no order." Changing it also re-measures the rise-time readout.

controls.label: cutoff
controls.what_it_does: The low-pass corner frequency in Hz. Tooltip: "Nominal -3 dB design cutoff. Once a channel is selected the maximum is clamped to just below that recording's Nyquist frequency, so a cutoff the kernel would reject cannot be dialled in." Lowering it removes more noise (shallow events become detectable) but lengthens the rise time, so short events are attenuated and their dwells biased long; raising it keeps fast events honest but lets more noise through.
controls.notes: Range 1.0 Hz up to just under Nyquist (5,000,000.0 Hz until a channel is selected), step 1000.0, default 10,000.0 Hz. Selecting a slower recording can silently pull an out-of-range value down. Above fs/2.5 the rise-time line adds: "⚠ above fs/2.5 …: the transition band is truncated by Nyquist, so this filter barely attenuates anything and the order is meaningless."

controls.label: rise time: — (select a channel)
controls.what_it_does: Bold live readout of the filter's real time resolution, e.g. "rise time: 34 µs (8-pole Bessel, zero-phase)  →  dwells below ~68 µs are filter-limited (depth attenuated, dwell biased long)." Use it to decide whether your shortest events survive the filter you chose.
controls.notes: Reads "— (sample rate unknown)" on a recording with no time base, "— (filter disabled; full bandwidth)" when the low-pass is off, and "— (cutoff X Hz is too low to measure live at Y Hz; detection still measures it)" when the live probe would be too expensive (over 2,000,000 samples). It follows type and order, not just the cutoff.

controls.label: enable High-pass
controls.what_it_does: Turns on a zero-phase high-pass in the classical candidate-localization branch. New Schmitt/CUSUM event-table amplitudes are measured on the companion chain with high-pass omitted.
controls.notes: The tooltip states that the orange preview and candidate response include high-pass; baseline, depth, fractional blockade, mean/max amplitude and SNR do not. Start/end, dwell, rise/fall and ECD limits still inherit the filtered boundaries, so keep the cutoff well below the event bandwidth. Manual measurement of Processed signal follows the orange branch.

controls.label: type
controls.what_it_does: Chooses the high-pass design: Butterworth (default) or Bessel. Tooltip: "Butterworth has a maximally flat pass-band above the cutoff. Bessel trades some roll-off sharpness for a flatter group delay. (Gaussian is a low-pass kernel and has no high-pass counterpart.)"
controls.notes: Items in order: Butterworth, Bessel.

controls.label: order
controls.what_it_does: Poles in the high-pass. Tooltip: "Number of poles. A steeper high-pass droops and rings a square blockade harder, not less — keep it low and keep the cutoff far below the event band."
controls.notes: Range 1–10, default 4.

controls.label: cutoff
controls.what_it_does: Where drift removal starts, in Hz. Raising it flattens drift more aggressively but eats further into real event shape; lowering it is safer for event fidelity and removes less drift.
controls.notes: Range 0.1 Hz up to just under Nyquist (5,000,000.00 Hz until a channel is selected), step 10.0, default 100.00 Hz. Carries the same distortion warning as the enable box.

controls.label: enable (mains hum + harmonics, zero-phase)
controls.what_it_does: Removes mains hum at the line frequency and its harmonics without shifting edges in time.
controls.notes: Nearly free for sub-millisecond events; it distorts slow (~10 ms) events whose own frequency band overlaps the line.

controls.label: frequency
controls.what_it_does: The mains line frequency to remove. Tooltip: "Mains line frequency: 60 Hz in the Americas, 50 Hz in most of the world."
controls.notes: Range 1.0–100,000.0 Hz (capped just under Nyquist once a channel is selected), step 10.0, default 60.0 Hz.

controls.label: harmonics
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "How many multiples of the line to notch (60/120/180 …). Harmonics at or above Nyquist are skipped automatically." Raise it when hum is visible at 120/180 Hz as well as at the fundamental.
controls.notes: Range 1–20, default 3. The note under the response plot lists exactly which lines will be notched and how deep the deepest one is.

controls.label: Q
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Quality factor: higher Q is a narrower notch (Q=30 at 60 Hz is ~2 Hz wide)." Raise it to take out less of the surrounding signal; lower it to catch a wandering line frequency at the cost of a wider bite.
controls.notes: Range 1.0–500.0, step 5.0, default 30.0. The response note warns that a narrow notch "rings for roughly the inverse of that at each end of the trace".

controls.label: enable (sliding median, despikes edges intact)
controls.what_it_does: Deletes single-sample spikes and glitches while leaving square event edges intact. Applied early in the chain, so spikes are gone before any smoothing can spread them.
controls.notes: A median has no frequency response, so the response plot goes blank and says so: "A sliding median is a NON-LINEAR rank filter: it has no transfer function, so there is no |H(f)| to draw."

controls.label: window
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Median window in seconds. Rejects spikes up to about half the window wide, so keep it a few samples — MUCH shorter than the shortest real event, or the median eats the events along with the spikes. Clamped up to an odd sample count."

controls.label: remove baseline wander (flatten slow drift)
controls.what_it_does: Estimate a slow baseline envelope and subtract its variation while retaining the representative open-pore level. This can flatten slow drift before classical detection.
controls.notes: The retained DC reference is the median of the estimated baseline, not proof that every absolute level or event depth is unchanged. The estimator/window can absorb long events, distort transitions or amplify wander; inspect before/after traces and warnings. This is different from a known-current reference, which supplies the level against which detection is computed. Source: nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py, remove_baseline_wander.

controls.label: method
controls.what_it_does: Choose the baseline-drift subtraction estimator.
controls.notes: Choices: block median, percentile, ASLS, event-masked median, robust median, and Savitzky-Golay baseline (subtract). Parameters depend on the selected method. This stage subtracts a fitted baseline; it is different from specifying an open-pore reference for detection.

controls.label: window
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Smoothing window for the open-pore estimate. Must be MUCH longer than the longest event, or the baseline dives into events and subtracts them (depths come out shallow, short events vanish)." Raise it for safety on long events; lower it only to follow faster drift.
controls.notes: Range 0.001–60.000 s, step 0.1, default 0.500 s. Changing it also changes what ASLS's smoothness means (see below).

controls.label: Block median has no shape parameters — the window above is all it takes.
controls.group: Preprocess ▸ Signal chain ▸ Baseline drift (block median)
controls.what_it_does: Explains why no extra controls appear when the block-median estimator is selected.

controls.label: percentile
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "How far toward the OPEN-PORE side to take the level, already sign-corrected for polarity — 80 means 'the level 80% of the way toward open pore', not a raw numpy percentile. Raise it when events are dense enough to drag a median (the case this method exists for); lower it when the trace is mostly open pore."
controls.notes: Range 0.1–99.9, step 5.0, default 80.0. Only visible when method = percentile.

controls.label: smoothness (lam)
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Smoothness (Eilers-Boelens lambda). Higher is a stiffer, flatter baseline. It is measured in BLOCK units, so its meaning rescales with the window and the knot spacing below — changing the window without revisiting this changes what ASLS does."
controls.notes: Range 1–1,000,000,000, step 10,000, default 60,000. Only visible when method = ASLS.

controls.label: asymmetry (p)
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Asymmetry. Small means heavily one-sided, which is what lets the fit ignore the events and follow the open pore. Raising it toward 0.5 makes the fit symmetric — it will start tracking events."
controls.notes: Range 0.00001–0.50000, step 0.001, default 0.00100. Only visible when method = ASLS.

controls.label: iterations
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Reweighting iterations. More costs time and converges the asymmetric fit further onto the open-pore side."
controls.notes: Range 1–100, default 10. Only visible when method = ASLS.

controls.label: knot spacing
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Knot spacing as a fraction of the window. Finer than 1 so some knots fall between dense events; the smoothness comes from lambda, not from this."
controls.notes: Range 0.001–1.000, step 0.05, default 0.100. Only visible when method = ASLS.

controls.label: enable (centred moving average, zero-phase)
controls.what_it_does: Turns on a plain centred box average — fast, unbiased noise reduction that does not shift features in time, but rounds peaks and smears steps.
controls.notes: Applied on the already-flattened trace, just before the Savitzky-Golay stage.

controls.label: window
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Averaging window in seconds. Suppresses noise by about sqrt(window·fs), but a box average rounds peaks and smears steps — keep it SHORTER than the shortest event you care about. Centred, so it does not shift features in time."
controls.notes: Range 0.00001–1.00000 s, step 0.0001, default 0.00050 s. If the window works out to a single sample the note under the plot says the stage "is the IDENTITY — it is enabled but changes nothing. Widen the window."

controls.label: enable (peak-preserving polynomial smooth)
controls.what_it_does: Turns on polynomial-in-a-window smoothing, which suppresses noise while preserving peak height and edges far better than a moving average. It is applied last in the chain.
controls.notes: The response note warns when it peaks above the pass band: "a Savitzky-Golay overshoots the plateau of a square blockade and leaves an opposite-sign lobe flanking each edge."

controls.label: window
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Smoothing window in seconds. Keep it SHORTER than the shortest event you care about, or the smoother rounds the event off along with the noise. It is clamped up to an odd sample count with more points than the polynomial order."

controls.label: poly order
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Order of the polynomial fitted in each window. 2–3 is typical; a higher order follows sharper curvature but smooths less."
controls.notes: Range 2–6, default 3.

controls.label: enable (rescale the whole trace — NOT pA)
controls.what_it_does: Turns on the stage that changes current samples to a dimensionless scale. The tooltip warns that current-derived amplitude/baseline/threshold readouts and pA/pA·s export fields retain legacy labels while no longer carrying physical units, and that centering invalidates fractional blockade (dI/I0).
controls.notes: OFF by default and applied LAST. The group-level amber banner remains visible on every stage page. z-score, robust and min–max are data-dependent affine transforms; model input additionally clips to a configured bound and can change event boundaries or counts. Index, time, source, review and status fields keep their ordinary meanings. Use Normalize to feed a model or compare dimensionless recordings, never to measure conductance.

controls.label: mode
controls.what_it_does: Which rescale. The four entries are "z-score  (x − mean) / std", "robust z  (x − median) / 1.4826·MAD", "min–max  → [−0.5, +0.5]" and "model input  (trimmed σ, clipped) → [−1, +1]".
controls.notes: z-score uses the whole trace; robust z uses the detector's 1.4826·MAD noise scale; min–max is sensitive to extreme samples; model input uses a twice-trimmed median/MAD, clips at the configured sigma bound, and divides to [−1,+1]. The menu is built from the kernels' own mode list.

controls.label: frequency / |H| response plot
controls.what_it_does: Draws the magnitude response of the stage currently selected in the combo, at the exact values in the boxes above it, with a dashed orange line at the nominal cutoff and a dotted grey line at -3 dB. It shows the response AS APPLIED, so the zero-phase squaring is visible rather than implied.
controls.notes: Blank with an explanation for Median and Baseline drift (neither has a transfer function) and until a channel with a known sample rate is selected ("select a channel with a known sample rate to see its frequency response").

controls.label: response note (line under the plot)
controls.what_it_does: One sentence saying what the selected filter really does, e.g. "At the nominal 10000 Hz the applied response is -6.0 dB — zero-phase, so |H| is SQUARED. The true -3 dB corner is 7800 Hz (0.78× the number in the box)." For the window smoothers it gives the width in samples and warns that whichever of the smoother and the low-pass has the LOWER -3 dB point sets the real bandwidth — and that the rise-time readout only knows about the low-pass.

controls.label: show processed trace on the plot
controls.what_it_does: Overlays the candidate-localization signal — every enabled stage, then low-pass — on the main trace. With high-pass on, classical detector event-table amplitudes use a companion branch with high-pass omitted.
controls.notes: Manual measurement of Processed signal follows this orange trace, including high-pass. The toggle is disabled until at least one stage is enabled and clears when every stage is off or the selected recording/channel changes.

controls.label: processed-trace preview unavailable: …
controls.what_it_does: Orange warning that appears when the preview could not be computed. It carries the kernel's own reason for a misconfigured stage (an over-Nyquist cutoff, a detrend window longer than the trace, a segment too short for the filter's padding, or a drift window so long the baseline is constant and tracks nothing), and the panel's own reason otherwise — "sample rate unknown — the filter stages are designed in Hz and seconds, so the processed trace cannot be computed for this recording (detection is disabled for the same reason)." It also reports what the PLOT could not do, so a ticked box over a plot with no orange curve is never silent.
controls.notes: Without it the preview curve would simply vanish with the box still ticked.

controls.label: k_in (enter)
controls.what_it_does: How far the current must depart from the open-pore baseline before an event is declared to start, in multiples of the trace's own noise RMS. Raise it to keep only deep, unambiguous events (fewer false positives, shallow events lost); lower it to catch shallower events at the cost of noise being counted as events.
controls.notes: Range 0.50–50.00, step 0.5, default 5.00. The Sweep threshold… dialog writes its recommended value straight into this box. Raising it drags k_out's ceiling up with it; lowering it can clamp k_out down (see below).

controls.label: k_out (exit)
controls.what_it_does: How far back toward the baseline the current must return before the event is declared over, again in noise-RMS units. The gap between k_in and k_out is what stops noise at the crossing from shattering one event into many. Raise it (toward k_in) for tighter, shorter event boundaries; lower it to keep slow tails and recovery inside the measured dwell.
controls.notes: Range 0.10–49.50, step 0.5, default 2.00. It is clamped LIVE to stay strictly below k_in: its maximum becomes k_in − 0.01, and if it ever reaches k_in it is knocked down to k_in − 0.5. So lowering k_in can move k_out without you touching it.

controls.label: min dwell
controls.what_it_does: Events shorter than this are dropped outright as sub-resolution. Raise it to suppress noise spikes and filter-limited blips; lower it to keep the fastest translocations — along with more false positives.
controls.notes: Range 0.0000000–1.0000000 s, step 0.00001, default 0.0000200 s (20 µs). Compare it with the rise-time readout on the Preprocess tab: anything below about twice the rise time is filter-limited anyway.

controls.label: max dwell
controls.what_it_does: Tooltip: "Events longer than this are KEPT but marked rejected (a clog is real signal you must see, not something to disappear). It also truncates the dwell sample on the right: the fits read this limit from provenance and condition the likelihood on it, because a left-truncation-only fit of a right-cut sample biases tau SHORT (-24% when the limit sits at 2.5 tau)." Lower it to flag clogs and stuck events; leave it at 0 to impose no upper limit.
controls.notes: Range 0.000000–100.000000 s, step 0.001, default 0.000000 s, and the suffix says it: " s  (0 = off)". Must exceed min dwell or the run is rejected. Events over the limit stay in the table with flag 'dwell>max_dwell_s' and accepted = false.

controls.label: merge gap
controls.what_it_does: Two events separated by less than this gap are joined into one, transitively along a chain — the same rule and the same unit as the Merge panel's Window. Raise it to stitch a flickering or multi-level blockade back into a single translocation; leave it at 0 to count every excursion separately.
controls.notes: Range 0.0000–1000.0000 ms, step 0.01, default 0.0000 ms, suffix " ms  (0 = off)". It reads MILLISECONDS: 15 ms is 15, not 0.015. The value is stored in provenance in SECONDS, and set_params converts, so a project written before this field changed unit still reads back correctly (a stored 0.015 s shows as 15 ms). This is the ONE merge control where 0 genuinely means off: merging is an optional step inside a detection run, and 0 maps to the detector's None sentinel. The Merge panel has no such state — its window sits beside a button whose only meaning is merge — which is why it floors at 0.01 ms instead. A run whose merged span would be mostly open pore is REFUSED rather than merged here too: 40 clean 0.4 ms events 8 ms apart are not one 312 ms translocation, so they are left as separate events.

controls.label: measured
controls.what_it_does: Read-only result of the polarity measurement from the last run, e.g. "blockade (down): 412 down / 7 up (confidence 0.98, measured)", or "undetermined: 0 down / 0 up — no clear excursions".
controls.notes: Starts as "not yet measured", fills in after a detection has run, and goes back to "not yet measured" the moment you point at a recording or channel that has no detection of its own — it never keeps another recording's line on screen. The direction shown is a readout, never a signed feature — depths reported elsewhere are always positive magnitudes.

controls.label: override
controls.what_it_does: Tells the detector which way events go instead of letting it measure. "auto (measure)" reads the direction from the data; the other two force it. Use a forced value when the trace is so drifty or sparse that the automatic measurement lands on the wrong side.
controls.notes: Items in order: "auto (measure)", "blockade (down, -1)", "enhancement (up, +1)". Careful: forcing the wrong direction does not raise an error — it simply detects almost nothing. Note also that on a negative-bias recording an ordinary blockade can legitimately be an UPWARD excursion in the signed current.

controls.label: Detect
controls.what_it_does: Runs the Schmitt-trigger detection on the selected current channel using everything on the Preprocess and Detection tabs plus the open-pore baseline block, and replaces the event table below with the result.
controls.notes: This is the panel's DEFAULT button, so pressing Enter in the panel fires it. Also available as Analysis ▸ Run detection (Ctrl+D). Greyed out with a banner unless a CURRENT channel with a known sample rate is selected. It runs in the background and can be cancelled; a cancelled run returns nothing rather than a half-built table.

controls.label: Sweep threshold…
controls.what_it_does: Re-runs detection at a whole range of enter thresholds and opens the Threshold sweep dialog: events-vs-k plotted with the plateau shaded and a surrogate (false-positive) curve overlaid — the evidence that replaces guessing at k_in.
controls.notes: Same enable gate as Detect. Runs off-thread. On some recordings the dialog itself warns that the surrogate is "NOT a null here", meaning that curve is not a false-positive count for this trace.

controls.label: Null control…
controls.what_it_does: Runs the current detection settings against a surrogate (event-free) version of this trace to estimate how many of your events could be false positives, and fills in the false-discovery readout in the summary panel below.
controls.notes: Same enable gate as Detect; runs off-thread. The polarity override and every preprocessing key are stripped before the control run.

controls.label: Recovery map…
controls.what_it_does: Measures how efficiently the current settings recover events as a function of dwell time, and makes the resulting efficiency curve available to the dwell-time fits in the summary panel.
controls.notes: Same enable gate as Detect; runs off-thread. Once it has run, the summary panel's "use measured efficiency" option becomes meaningful for this recording/channel.

controls.label: gate banner (top of the panel)
controls.what_it_does: Orange line above the tab strip that explains why the run buttons are greyed out — either "Detection runs on CURRENT channels; this is a <kind> channel." or "Sample rate unknown — dwell time is undefined without a time base, so detection is disabled for this recording." or "Select a CURRENT channel to run detection."
controls.notes: It sits above the tabs deliberately, so the reason is visible no matter which tab is showing.

controls.label: Use recommended k
controls.group: Threshold sweep dialog (opened by Sweep threshold…)
controls.what_it_does: Accepts the sweep's recommended enter threshold and writes it straight into the k_in (enter) box on the Detection tab.
controls.notes: DISABLED when the sweep found no plateau — the dialog then says "No plateau found — the event count never stabilised. Widen the k range." Committing k does not re-run detection; press Detect afterwards.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.group: Threshold sweep dialog (opened by Sweep threshold…)
controls.what_it_does: Closes the sweep dialog without changing k_in.

controls.label: Signal chain
controls.what_it_does: The group box that holds all seven pre-detection filter stages. The combo inside it picks which stage's controls are shown; every stage stays active whether or not its page is the one currently on screen, so a stage you cannot see is still being applied.

controls.label: High-pass
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Second item of the filter-stage combo; raises the high-pass (DC / slow-drift removal) page. When the stage is enabled the item text becomes '● High-pass' and the stage is added to the 'Active: …' summary line.

controls.label: Notch
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Raises the mains-hum notch page. Shown as '● Notch' once enabled.

controls.label: Median
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Raises the sliding-median despiker page. Shown as '● Median' once enabled. This stage has no frequency-response curve — the plot clears and the note explains that a median is a non-linear rank filter.

controls.label: Baseline drift
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Raises the baseline-wander removal page. Shown as '● Baseline drift' once enabled. Like the median it has no |H(f)| curve: the plot clears and the note says it is an estimator, not a filter.

controls.label: Running mean
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Raises the centred moving-average page. Shown as '● Running mean' once enabled.

controls.label: Savitzky-Golay
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Raises the polynomial-smoothing page. Shown as '● Savitzky-Golay' once enabled.

controls.label: Normalize
controls.group: Preprocess tab > Signal chain (stage selector combo)
controls.what_it_does: Raises the whole-trace rescale page — the eighth and LAST stage in the chain. Shown as '● Normalize' once enabled.

controls.label: Gaussian
controls.what_it_does: Third choice of the low-pass type combo (the others are 'Bessel', the default, and 'Butterworth'). Picking Gaussian greys out the 'order' spinbox, which then reads the tooltip 'Gaussian is a symmetric kernel and has no order.'; switching back to Bessel or Butterworth re-enables it.

controls.label: block median
controls.what_it_does: Default baseline estimator. Selecting it shows only the grey note 'Block median has no shape parameters — the window above is all it takes.' — the percentile and ASLS spinboxes are hidden.

controls.label: ASLS
controls.what_it_does: Selecting this method is what reveals the four ASLS shape spinboxes (smoothness (lam), asymmetry (p), iterations, knot spacing); they are hidden under the other two methods.

controls.label: Polarity
controls.what_it_does: Group box holding the measured-polarity readout and the manual override.

controls.label: not yet measured
controls.what_it_does: The 'measured' readout before any detection has run. After a run it reports the evidence, e.g. 'blockade (down): 128 down / 3 up (confidence 0.98, measured)', or 'undetermined: 0 down / 0 up — no clear excursions' when the trace gives no clear excursions. The last field is the verdict and is one of 'measured', 'tie' or 'undetermined' — never 'decisive'.

controls.label: auto (measure)
controls.what_it_does: Default override choice: let the detector measure the event direction from the data instead of forcing it.

controls.label: blockade (down, -1)
controls.what_it_does: Force downward (current-blocking) events, ignoring the measurement.

controls.label: enhancement (up, +1)
controls.what_it_does: Force upward (current-enhancing) events, ignoring the measurement.

controls.label: Load model…
controls.what_it_does: Opens a file picker (titled 'Load Keras model', starting in your Downloads folder, filter 'Keras model (*.keras)') to choose an event-detector model; it is run on the current channel and only loaded off the GUI thread when you run detection. The button is greyed out entirely when TensorFlow is not installed. The same action is on MainWindow's 'Load ML model…' menu item.

controls.label: Student models only
controls.what_it_does: Pop-up shown when the file you picked is a 12-feature TEACHER model: it explains that this app runs STUDENT models only and asks you to load the matching student export. Nothing is loaded when this appears.

controls.label: none
controls.what_it_does: The 'model' row readout: shows the file name of the loaded model, or 'none' until one is loaded. Loading also reads the model's input width and may re-default the preprocessing preset (see the note in Model preprocessing).

controls.label: range
controls.what_it_does: Where to run the model: 'Visible view' (default) or 'Whole recording'. Inference is slow (~0.24x realtime on CPU), so whole recording can take minutes. This is a separate choice from the normalization scale in Model preprocessing.

controls.label: Run ML detection
controls.what_it_does: Runs the loaded model over the chosen range and puts its events into the same event table as the threshold detector. Enabled only when TensorFlow is installed AND a model is loaded AND the selected channel is a CURRENT channel with a known sample rate.

controls.label: TensorFlow is not installed, so ML detection is unavailable. Install tensorflow (2.15) to enable it.
controls.what_it_does: Amber gate message under the Run button naming the first unmet condition. The other two texts are 'Select a CURRENT channel with a known sample rate to run ML detection.' and 'Load a .keras model to run ML detection.'; the line disappears once the Run button is live.

controls.label: Model preprocessing
controls.what_it_does: The editable preprocessing pipeline fed to the loaded ML model, separate from the general Preprocess signal chain. A shipped or user-saved preset populates these controls; editing them produces a CUSTOM deviation indicator rather than locking the pipeline.
controls.notes: Match the model’s actual training contract. Save as… stores this tab’s preprocessing and decode settings as a user preset; Delete cannot remove shipped presets. Automatic-estimator measurement windows confirmed in Preprocess are merged separately into ML characterization provenance. Known-current and selected-interval user references are not supported for ML and are refused rather than silently substituted. Sources: nanoscope/gui/panels.py, ml_params and _build_ml_preprocess_group; nanoscope/gui/analysis_panel.py, _run_ml_detection and _launch_ml.

controls.label: The ML detector runs THIS pipeline, not the Preprocess tab. Pick the preset the model was trained with — the Ferritin presets and the Apo-ferritin ones are different MOLECULES, not just different settings.
controls.what_it_does: Standing note at the top of the group. It is rewritten when a model is loaded: it appends the model's input width, warns in capitals if the width says one molecule and the selected preset says the other, and says so explicitly when loading a model changed the preset for you.

controls.label: preset
controls.what_it_does: Picks the training pipeline the model was built under; choosing one rewrites every ML parameter below. Items, separated into two molecule blocks: 'Ferritin — nb1 (steady baseline, ferritin_data1)', 'Ferritin — nb2 (spiky, masked baseline, ferritin_data2)', 'Ferritin — nb3 (gating pore, 30 ms baseline, ferritin_data3)', 'Apo-ferritin — −500 mV (notebook, thr 0.20 / min 15 ms)', 'Apo-ferritin — −600 mV (notebook, thr 0.10 / min 1 ms)' (the default), 'Apo-ferritin — −700 mV (notebook, thr 0.20 / min 1 ms)', 'Apo-ferritin — raw-global model (student_raw_global_raw_best, W=3072)'. Once you pick a preset by hand, or hand-edit any ML parameter, loading a model will never overrule your choice again.

controls.label: molecule
controls.what_it_does: States the molecule of the selected preset outright, e.g. 'APO-FERRITIN — a model trained on the other molecule will not behave as measured on this one.'

controls.label: matches Apo-ferritin — −600 mV (notebook, thr 0.10 / min 1 ms)
controls.what_it_does: Deviation indicator under the preset row. Reads 'matches <preset>' in grey while every value is the preset's; turns amber and reads 'CUSTOM — N change(s) from <preset>: <first four fields>, …' as soon as you edit one, or 'custom (values not yet valid)' while the form is momentarily inconsistent (e.g. exit above enter mid-edit).

controls.label: notch lines
controls.what_it_does: Comma-separated notch frequencies in Hz, applied in this order; training used 60, 120, 180. Unparseable or non-positive entries are dropped, and an empty result falls back to 60, 120, 180 so a typo can never hand the model an un-notched signal. Capped at 32 lines — each is one filtfilt pass over the analysed range — and an over-cap paste is refused by name ("…capped at 32") rather than silently freezing the run.

controls.label: notch Q
controls.what_it_does: Quality factor of each notch line (higher Q is a narrower notch).

controls.label: round to float32 after notch
controls.what_it_does: Reproduces the apo notebook, which rounds to float32 after notching so the baseline stage runs in float32; the ferritin chain keeps float64. The measured difference is 3e-05 pA — but it is the difference between bit-exact and not.

controls.label: baseline
controls.what_it_does: Baseline estimator for the model's chain: 'robust median' (outlier-resistant rolling median, notebook 1), 'event-masked median' (events exposed, masked, interpolated over, then a short median tracks drift — notebooks 2 and 3), 'Savitzky-Golay' (polynomial envelope, apo legacy only; it overshoots around deep/long events) or 'none'. Your choice decides which of the seven rows below stay visible.

controls.label: decimation
controls.what_it_does: Calculation decimation for the model’s median baseline estimate. It changes the estimator’s sampling resolution and must match the training pipeline; it is not universally lossless.
controls.notes: For example, decimation 50 at 50 kHz leaves 1 ms between estimator samples. Short windows and rapid baseline features require particular care. The setting is visible for robust-median and event-masked-median model baselines. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py and MLPreprocessConfig.

controls.label: rough window
controls.what_it_does: Masked-median only: the rough window that exposes events before they are masked. Visible only when the baseline is 'event-masked median'.

controls.label: base window
controls.what_it_does: Masked-median only: the short window that tracks drift after events have been masked and interpolated over. Visible only when the baseline is 'event-masked median'.

controls.label: mask sigma
controls.what_it_does: Samples deeper than median − sigma × MAD noise are masked as events (the MAD is global over the preprocessed span). Visible only for 'event-masked median'.

controls.label: mask dilate
controls.what_it_does: Widens the event mask by this many milliseconds before the baseline is re-fitted. Visible only for 'event-masked median'.

controls.label: de-spike
controls.what_it_does: Post-detrend median filter that removes 1-2 sample spike artifacts. 0 displays as 'off' and is the default; only notebook 2 uses it, at size 3.

controls.label: divide by max|x| + 1e-8
controls.what_it_does: Global normalization applied before the signal is cut into windows; on by default. (The 12-feature teacher contract standardizes internally and never uses this.)

controls.label: subtract the mean first
controls.what_it_does: Uses the apo notebook's (x − mean) / (max|x − mean| + 1e-8) instead of the ferritin chain's pure rescale. On real apo data it shifted 0 of 236 events, but it is what the apo code executes.

controls.label: norm scope
controls.what_it_does: Where the mean and max|x| are measured: 'Whole recording' (default — what both notebooks did, so the model's input scale does not depend on your zoom) or 'Analysed range' (the older behaviour, where a sub-range run silently rescaled the input).

controls.label: cover the tail
controls.what_it_does: Adds a final window anchored at the end of the data so the last partial stride is still scored. Neither notebook does this — with it off their tails sit at probability zero.

controls.label: starts may reach n − W
controls.what_it_does: Chooses which notebook's window-start loop to reproduce when the tail is not anchored (off = ferritin's, on = apo's). They differ only when the recording length makes the ferritin loop stop one window early and leave a whole stride unscored. Ignored when 'cover the tail' is ticked.

controls.label: Model decode
controls.what_it_does: Group box turning the model's per-sample probability trace into events: smoothing, the two hysteresis thresholds, merging/duration limits and the onset/offset snapping.

controls.label: smoothing
controls.what_it_does: Median-filter kernel applied to the probability trace before thresholding (forced odd). 1 means no smoothing at all, which is what the apo notebook does.

controls.label: enter
controls.what_it_does: Enter threshold on the per-sample event probability: a run of samples is an event only if the probability reaches this. Shows 0.10 on a fresh panel — the default preset (Apo-ferritin — −600 mV) writes it; the kernel's own default of 0.5 is never what is on screen.

controls.label: exit
controls.what_it_does: Exit threshold: the event stays alive until the probability falls below this. Clamped live to at most 'enter' — raising enter/lowering exit is done for you rather than failing the run. Shows 0.10 on a fresh panel, from the default preset.

controls.label: min duration
controls.what_it_does: Drops ML events shorter than this, in milliseconds. Applied last, so the test uses the final merged and trimmed extent.

controls.label: onset snap
controls.what_it_does: Walks each onset back to where the current really entered the blockade (below median − sigma × MAD noise), correcting the model's onset latency. 0 displays as 'off'; notebook 3 uses 2.0.

controls.label: onset lookback
controls.what_it_does: How far back, in milliseconds, the onset snap is allowed to walk.

controls.label: onset gap tol
controls.what_it_does: How many consecutive shallow samples the backward onset walk tolerates before it stops.

controls.label: offset trim
controls.what_it_does: Snaps each event end to the last sample deeper than median − sigma × MAD noise, removing shallow recovery tails. 0 displays as 'off'; notebook 3 uses 3.0.

controls.label: Summary
controls.group: Stats panel (same file — check overlap with any 'stats' area)
controls.what_it_does: Read-only one-column table (header 'value') of the current detection, rows: 'n events', 'n accepted', 'rate (Hz, accepted)', 'median dwell (µs)', 'median depth (pA)', 'median dI/I0', 'open pore (median stamped, pA)', 'baseline window', 'baseline fingerprint', 'n filter-limited', 'n pores'. Every cell shows an em dash until a detection exists. The last three of the middle rows are the provenance of the depths above them — the open pore they were measured against, the windows that produced it, and the fingerprint the voltage-dependence guard reads.

controls.label: false-positive rate: not measured (run Null control)
controls.group: Stats panel (same file — check overlap with any 'stats' area)
controls.what_it_does: FDR readout under the summary. After a null control it reads 'estimated false-positive rate: 4.2% (AAFT, 20 surrogates) — individual surrogates gave 1.9–11.3%'; the trailing clause is dropped only when every surrogate lands on the same printed percentage. The printed rate is the MEAN of independent draws, so the run is seeded from the recording and the settings and the tooltip carries the per-surrogate counts and that seed — press it again and the same number comes back. When the surrogates are not a valid null it refuses to give a rate and instead reports 'false-positive rate NOT estimated — N detection(s) on this recording's own event-free noise (a lower bound, measured with no surrogate).' It resets to 'not measured' whenever you point at a recording that has no null control of its own.

controls.label: Fits
controls.group: Stats panel (same file — check overlap with any 'stats' area)
controls.what_it_does: Group box holding the distribution-fit controls and the Fit button.

controls.label: dwell components
controls.what_it_does: How many exponential components to fit to the dwell-time distribution (1-4).

controls.label: depth components
controls.what_it_does: How many log-normal components to fit to the depth distribution (1-4).

controls.label: use measured efficiency (needs recovery map)
controls.what_it_does: Corrects the fit with the detector efficiency actually measured for this recording. Greyed out until a recovery map exists — run 'Recovery map…' on the Detection tab; if the map goes away the box is unticked for you.

controls.label: include filter-limited events
controls.what_it_does: Off by default: events whose dwell is within ~2× the filter rise time are excluded from the dwell and depth fits, because their depth is attenuated and their dwell biased long. Tick it to fit them alongside the resolved events.

controls.label: 12 accepted event(s) are filter-limited — excluded from the fits.
controls.what_it_does: Live count of how many accepted events the fit will drop, shown before you run it; the wording flips to 'INCLUDED in the fits' when you tick 'include filter-limited events'. Blank when the count is zero.

controls.label: Fit
controls.what_it_does: Fits the dwell and depth distributions of the ACCEPTED events of the current detection and stores each fit with its provenance. Disabled until a detection exists, with the reason shown beside it: 'Run detection first — the fits are computed from the accepted events of the current detection.' The spinboxes and toggles stay live so you can dial a fit in beforehand.

controls.label: Fit results appear here.
controls.what_it_does: Placeholder in the read-only monospace results box below the Fit button, where the fit summary text is printed.

controls.label: Detector score (vs your curation)
controls.what_it_does: Scores the DETECTOR against your curated truth. Rows: 'detected', 'truth (kept)', 'matched (TP)', 'spurious (FP)', 'missed (FN)', 'auto-rejected', 'precision', 'recall', 'F1'. 'spurious (FP)' and 'missed (FN)' count YOUR gestures — the events you rejected and the ones you added by hand; the rows the detector rejected on its own (boundary-clipped, over the max dwell, non-finite) are counted apart under 'auto-rejected' and are never scored as false positives. It refreshes on every curation, edit, hand-added event or new result; a ratio with a zero denominator shows as 'n/a' and never a fabricated 0, the three ratios read 'not scored yet' while nothing has been rejected or hand-added, and every row shows an em dash when there is nothing to score.

controls.label: accepted
controls.what_it_does: The event table's only editable column: a checkbox per row that keeps or rejects that event. Ticking it updates the summary, the score panel and the trace overlays immediately. Every column header is clickable to sort, and selecting a row jumps the trace view to that event.

controls.label: dwell_s ⚠
controls.what_it_does: Column headers gain a '⚠' badge and turn amber when their values were measured against an open-pore baseline that is no longer the configured one. Header and every cell in the column carry the same tooltip: the numbers are shown exactly as stored, nothing has been re-measured, and you can fix them with the Re-measure depths button on the banner above the table or Analysis > Compare baseline estimators.

controls.label: j / k / a / r / f
controls.what_it_does: Keyboard curation, active while the table itself has focus (click a row first): 'j' moves down a row, 'k' moves up, 'a' accepts the current event, 'r' rejects it, and 'f' adds the curator flag to that row's existing reasons (it never overwrites a detector flag such as clipped_by_boundary). These keys are swallowed by the table, so they do not trigger type-to-search.

controls.label: Threshold sweep
controls.what_it_does: Window title of the dialog opened by 'Sweep threshold…'. It plots the event count against k with the plateau shaded, marks the recommended k with a dotted 'k*=…' line, and overlays the surrogate count as a dashed series named either 'surrogate (false +)' or, when the surrogates are not a valid null for this recording, 'surrogate — NOT a null here (see below)' drawn in grey.

controls.label: Recommended k = 5.5 (centre of the plateau where the event count is insensitive to threshold, while the surrogate count stays low).
controls.what_it_does: The sentence under the plot. When no plateau was found it instead reads 'No plateau found — the event count never stabilised. Widen the k range.' and the 'Use recommended k' button is greyed out — that button is only clickable when a plateau exists. When the surrogate is not a null the sentence drops the surrogate clause and appends the sweep's own explanatory note.

controls.label: Compare baseline estimators
controls.what_it_does: Window title of the report that shows what re-measuring this recording would change before it changes anything: a headline sentence, a 'Measured with' / 'Would be measured with' pair of rows, an old-vs-new depth scatter against the dashed y = x line, and a histogram of the per-event depth ratio with a 1.0x marker.

controls.label: Re-measure now
controls.what_it_does: Re-measures these events against the configured estimator; events are not re-detected, so every span and every accept/reject survives. Stays clickable even when nothing would change (a harmless no-op that clears the stale banner); it is disabled only when there is no live recording, with the tooltip 'There is no live recording to re-measure against.'

controls.label: Close
controls.what_it_does: Closes the comparison without re-measuring anything. Nothing is installed by opening this dialog.

controls.label: Health warnings from the new baseline:
controls.what_it_does: Amber bullet list shown above the buttons only when the proposed baseline reports health warnings for this recording.

controls.label: loaded (model combo)
controls.what_it_does: Every model loaded THIS SESSION, switchable without re-browsing. Loading a model adds it here; picking one makes it the active detector (path, label and input-width preset all follow).
controls.notes: Session-scoped on purpose — a persisted list would accumulate dead paths. Re-loading a model already listed selects it rather than duplicating it. Disabled and reading 'none loaded' until the first load.

controls.label: Protocol (combo + Save as… + Delete)
controls.what_it_does: Named preprocessing protocols: 'Save as…' captures the WHOLE chain — every stage's enable flag and parameters (low-pass, high-pass, notch incl. harmonics, median, baseline drift, running mean, Savitzky-Golay) — under a name; picking a name applies it all at once; Delete forgets it.
controls.notes: Stored per user (QSettings JSON), so protocols survive restarts and apply to any recording. Editing any stage by hand drops the combo back to '— manual —' — the name only stands while the chain is exactly the saved one. Detection thresholds (k_in/k_out/min dwell…) are deliberately NOT captured: a protocol conditions the signal, it must not change what an event is.

controls.label: Controls
controls.what_it_does: Choose Essential or Advanced visibility.
controls.notes: Visibility only; hidden controls keep their values. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: Baseline reference…
controls.what_it_does: Open the recording-specific reference controls.
controls.notes: Does not apply a reference or rerun detection. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: detector
controls.what_it_does: Choose Schmitt trigger (hysteresis) or Sequential CUSUM.
controls.notes: Each detector has separate stored results/settings. Selecting an existing result does not itself run detection. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: Schmitt trigger (hysteresis)
controls.what_it_does: Locate excursions with separate enter/exit thresholds.
controls.notes: Defaults: k_in=5, k_out=2; exit is lower than entry. Tune against noise, event duration and reference evidence. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: Sequential CUSUM
controls.what_it_does: Locate excursions using a sequential cumulative-sum change detector.
controls.notes: Defaults k=0.750 σ and h=28.00 σ·samples; not the same operation as fitting substates inside detected events. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: k (drift)
controls.what_it_does: Set the CUSUM allowance in noise-sigma units.
controls.notes: Default 0.750 σ. Changes detection when explicitly run. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: h (threshold)
controls.what_it_does: Set the CUSUM cumulative decision threshold.
controls.notes: Default 28.00 σ·samples. Depends on sample rate and the recording, not a universal amplitude cutoff. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: Advanced detection settings
controls.what_it_does: Reveal maximum dwell and detector merge gap.
controls.notes: May require this disclosure even when Controls is Advanced. Maximum dwell is seconds; merge gap is milliseconds. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: event-masked median
controls.what_it_does: Estimate baseline from an initial rough baseline, event mask and a tracking pass.
controls.notes: Inspect mask threshold/dilation and both windows; heavy occupancy can leave insufficient open-pore evidence. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: robust median
controls.what_it_does: Use the robust median baseline-drift estimator.
controls.notes: Uses its method-specific robust handling; validate preservation of long and low-amplitude events. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: Savitzky-Golay baseline (subtract)
controls.what_it_does: Subtract the smooth polynomial baseline estimate.
controls.notes: Different from the Savitzky-Golay smoothing stage, which keeps the smooth fit rather than its residual. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: decimation
controls.what_it_does: Set supported baseline-estimator calculation decimation.
controls.notes: Numerical estimator parameter, not merely display decimation; method-specific controls apply. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: rough window / tracking window
controls.what_it_does: Set the event-masked estimator’s rough and tracking windows.
controls.notes: Recording-dependent seconds; they are distinct from the event-duration threshold. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: mask threshold / mask dilation
controls.what_it_does: Control event exclusion in the masked baseline estimator.
controls.notes: Threshold is in noise sigma; dilation is milliseconds. Inspect sensitivity to these scientific settings. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

controls.label: poly order / decimation
controls.what_it_does: Set Savitzky-Golay baseline polynomial order and calculation decimation.
controls.notes: Applies only to the subtracting baseline estimator, not the separate smoothing page. Source: nanoscope/gui/panels.py.

area: Results, fitting, post-detection merge and manual measurements
summary: Results provides Events, Summary, Fits and Quality views of the selected stored detection. Fits explicitly use accepted events, with filter-limited and efficiency options. Merge sub-events is a post-detection curation operation with an occupancy guard, distinct from the detector merge gap. Measure provides cursor-based live statistics and a separate saved measurement table. An event result, a manual measurement, a fitted substate table and a frozen plot are separate artifacts with separate provenance.
opened_by: Inspector → Analysis → Results (Events / Summary / Fits / Quality). The Table selector in Merge sub-events chooses a stored detector result. Measure is the fourth compact tab; Analysis → Measure event arms cursors and Add measurement to list (Ctrl+M) saves a measurement. Sources: nanoscope/gui/analysis_panel.py, merge_panel.py, panels.py, measure_panel.py.
gotchas: The Fit button is dead until the current channel has a stored detection — the amber line beside it tells you so, but only after you look; it is not the results box.
Fits use ACCEPTED events only, so every accept/reject you make in the event table silently changes what the next Fit reports.
Filter-limited events are EXCLUDED from fits by default — check the count line above the Fit button, or the fit's n will not match "n accepted" in the summary.
Toggling "include filter-limited events" does not re-run the fit; it only rewrites the count line. Press Fit again.
"use measured efficiency" stays greyed out until you run Recovery map… for THIS target — a map from another recording will not enable it.
The false-positive-rate line only ever fills in after running Null control…, and it resets to "not measured" whenever you switch recordings.

Merge edits are undone through Edit → Undo, not by redetecting. An explicit replacement detection can replace curation and prompts when applicable; save a project before intentionally replacing reviewed results.
"Merge all" acts on the whole detection in one click with no per-event confirmation; check the before/after counts in the status bar.

A merge can be REFUSED rather than performed, and "nothing merged" is not the same sentence as "nothing to merge": a run of events the window really did catch is left alone when the span it would make is mostly open pore (the fragments covering less than 50% of it), because that is several translocations glued to the gaps between them, not one repaired. The status bar names the count and says to try a smaller window. Read a refusal as "this window is too wide for this recording", never as "the merge is not working".
"Merge events in selection" ignores the Window value completely and needs a live Measure region — it will refuse with a status-bar nudge if you have not dragged one.
The Measure toggle switches itself off whenever you change recording or channel, so a Ctrl+M press after switching does nothing until you re-arm it.

Above 200,000 selected samples the live readout is a subsampled preview and min/max/peak-to-peak read "—"; with amplitude method min or max, level/amplitude/dI/I₀/SNR blank out too. Saved rows are always exact regardless.

"Snap to view" and trace double-click place a mask no wider than 20% of the visible window. This is an initial-placement cap only: either circular edge handle can still be dragged farther for a long event.
Double-clicking a row jumps the trace to that measurement, but double-clicking its "label" cell edits the text instead — the two gestures look identical.
"This recording only" hides rows from the view but Export CSV still writes every measurement in the table, from every recording.
"Remove selected" deletes hand-drawn work nothing can re-derive; it confirms first and Edit ▸ Undo can restore it, but a saved project is your real safety net.
Ctrl+C copies selected rows as TSV only while the measurements table itself has focus — click into the table first.

A saved measurement's row number carries THREE verdicts, not two: nothing means checked against the live calibration and current, ⚠ means measured under a calibration that has since changed (and it is KEPT, with a different tooltip, once its recording is closed and the check can no longer be repeated), and ? means nobody could check it — the recording is not open, or the row predates the stamp columns — which is not the same as matching.

controls.label: Summary
controls.what_it_does: Read-only readout of what the current detection contains. Seven rows: "n events", "n accepted", "rate (Hz)", "median dwell (µs)", "median dI/I0", "n filter-limited", "n pores". Every value shows "—" until a detection exists.
controls.notes: "n accepted" tracks your curation live — accept/reject in the event table or Event Inspector and this recomputes. "rate (Hz)" is events over the ANALYSED duration, not the recorded duration, and reads "—" when detection did not record how much signal it analysed. "median dwell" / "median dI/I0" are over ALL events, not just accepted ones. "n pores" is the number of distinct pore_id values in the table. Not editable.

controls.label: false-positive rate: not measured (run Null control)
controls.what_it_does: The false-discovery-rate line under the summary table. Once a null control has been run it reads "estimated false-positive rate: N.N% (AAFT, N surrogates)".
controls.notes: Only populated by the "Null control…" button on the Detection tab — it is not part of this box. The FDR belongs to the recording it was measured on, so switching to another target resets this line to "not measured" rather than leaving the previous recording's number on screen. When the null control refuses to stand behind a rate it instead reads "false-positive rate NOT estimated — N detection(s) on this recording's own event-free noise (a lower bound, measured with no surrogate)", and the reason is in the tooltip.

controls.label: ⚠ About these numbers
controls.what_it_does: The amber advisory block directly under the Summary table: every caveat the detection on screen was produced under, one bullet each, taken whole from the result's warnings — it knows nothing about which warning it is showing, so a new caveat surfaces here without any code that special-cases it. The one you will meet most reads "The open pore here is NOT CERTIFIED, only chosen": it names both conductance levels and how much of the recording each holds, then prints dI/I0 BOTH ways, against the tracked baseline and against the other level, because the two readings are the same samples and nothing in the Baseline health block separates them.
controls.notes: Raised whenever the trace holds a second level for at least 2.5% of the recording (ALT_LEVEL_OCCUPANCY_MIN — true of all four reference apo files, whose other level holds 0.054 / 0.099 / 0.087 / 0.077) or the tracked level holds under 80% of it. It is not an inversion detector and does not claim to be; it is the app saying the identification was made and never verified, and it ends by telling you to compare the baseline with the open-pore current you know for this pore. There is NO dismiss control: the block clears only when the next run's warnings no longer carry the sentence — measure the recording, confirm the windows, detect again. Hidden entirely when a result carries no warnings, and the whole block is its own tooltip for a dock dragged narrow.

controls.label: dwell components
controls.what_it_does: How many components the dwell-time distribution is fit with — 1 for a single exponential, more for a mixture of populations.
controls.notes: Range 1–4, default 1. Stays live even with no detection loaded, so you can dial a fit in before running detection.

controls.label: depth components
controls.what_it_does: How many components the blockade-depth distribution is fit with — 1 for a single log-normal, more for a mixture.
controls.notes: Range 1–4, default 1. Stays live with no detection loaded.

controls.label: use measured efficiency (needs recovery map)
controls.what_it_does: Correct the dwell fit for the detector's measured recovery efficiency η(t) instead of assuming every event was found.
controls.notes: DISABLED until you run "Recovery map…" (on the Detection tab) FOR THIS target — a map run on a different recording/channel does not enable it. Unchecking happens automatically whenever the map goes away. Even if checked, the fit only uses it while the box is enabled.

controls.label: include filter-limited events
controls.what_it_does: Off (default): events whose dwell is within ~2x the filter rise time are excluded from the dwell and depth fits — their depth is attenuated and their dwell biased long, and the count excluded is reported with the fit. On: they are fit alongside the resolved events.
controls.notes: Default OFF. Toggling it does not re-run the fit — it only rewrites the count line below; press Fit again to see the change. The excluded events are the ones the scatter figure already draws as open markers over a shaded band.

controls.label: N accepted event(s) are filter-limited — excluded from the fits.
controls.what_it_does: Says, before you press Fit, how many accepted events the fit is about to drop as filter-limited. The verb flips to "INCLUDED in the fits" when the checkbox above is ticked.
