controls.notes: Blank when the count is zero. This is the difference between the "n accepted" the summary table shows and the n the fit will report — the whole reason it appears before the fit rather than only in the result text.
controls.correction: "{n} accepted event(s) are filter-limited — {verb} the fits." where verb is "excluded from" when "include filter-limited events" is OFF and "INCLUDED in" (capitalised) when it is ON. The reported string is only the unchecked state; the label is empty and invisible when the count is 0.

controls.label: Fit
controls.what_it_does: Fit the dwell and depth distributions of the ACCEPTED events of the current detection (exponential / log-normal mixtures), and store each fit with its provenance.
controls.notes: DISABLED until the current channel has a stored detection. While disabled an amber line beside it says why: "Run detection first — the fits are computed from the accepted events of the current detection." (the same reason is appended to the button's tooltip). Only ACCEPTED events are fit, so rejecting events in the table changes the fit.
controls.correction: "{n} accepted event(s) are filter-limited — {verb} the fits." where verb is "excluded from" when "include filter-limited events" is OFF and "INCLUDED in" (capitalised) when it is ON. The reported string is only the unchecked state; the label is empty and invisible when the count is 0.

controls.label: Run detection first — the fits are computed from the accepted events of the current detection.
controls.what_it_does: The amber gate reason shown beside the Fit button while it is disabled.
controls.notes: Hidden entirely once a detection exists. It exists because the Fit button used to accept the click and then write the failure into the results box below, where nobody was looking.

controls.label: Fit results appear here.
controls.what_it_does: Monospace, read-only area holding the fit summary — the fitted parameters for each component, and the count of any filter-limited events that were excluded.
controls.notes: That string is the placeholder shown when empty, not a result. Read-only: you cannot type or correct anything here. Cleared/replaced on every new fit.

controls.label: Merge sub-events
controls.what_it_does: The box title. Stitch a translocation the detector split into several fragments back into one event.
controls.notes: Reversed by Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z). NOT by re-running detection — a re-detection replaces the whole table and takes every accept/reject decision with it, which is the single most destructive click in the application.

controls.label: Window
controls.what_it_does: Merge window: detected events whose gap (next start − current end) is within this many milliseconds are stitched into one (transitively along a chain).
controls.notes: Range 0.01–100 ms, default 0.15 ms, two decimals, arrow step 0.5 ms. ~0.15 ms is a few samples at 50 kHz — long enough to bridge a brief threshold recrossing, short enough to leave genuinely separate events alone. There is NO 0: the minimum is 0.01 ms, a fifth of a sample at 50 kHz, which still stitches fragments that touch exactly. 0 LOOKED like the "0 = off" sentinel the Detection tab's merge gap really has and was not one — at 0 the window is 0 samples, gap <= 0 is true for exactly-touching rows, and Merge all still merged them — so the field floors at the smallest window that is honestly a window. A 0 restored from an older session comes back as that minimum rather than as a window that reads off and is not. This spinbox stays ENABLED even with no detection so you can dial it in ahead of time. It also supplies the window for the Event Inspector's "Merge with next".

controls.label: Merge all
controls.what_it_does: Merge every run of fragments within the window across the whole detection. The status bar reports the before/after counts, e.g. "Merged 12 fragment(s): 340 → 328 events."
controls.notes: DISABLED until the active channel has a stored detection. Acts on the ENTIRE detection at once — there is no per-event confirmation. If nothing sits within the window the status bar says "No sub-events within 0.15 ms to merge." and nothing changes. A run the window DID catch can still be REFUSED: the gap rule is transitive and has no brake, so a regularly spaced train of clean events collapses the moment the window exceeds the spacing — at a 10 ms window, 40 isolated 0.4 ms / 300 pA events spaced 8 ms apart became ONE row of dwell 312.40 ms and depth 0.70 pA, accepted, with a blank flag, because the depth is a median over a span that is 96% open pore. So a group is merged only when its fragments cover at least 50% of the span they would make; below that it is left as separate events and counted as a refusal, and the status bar says which happened rather than reporting it as nothing to merge: "Nothing merged: N run(s) within X ms are mostly open pore between their events, so merging them would make one long, shallow event. Try a smaller window.", or — when part of the table did merge — "Merged 12 fragment(s): 340 → 328 events. 3 further run(s) were left alone: they are mostly open pore between their events." A merge that IS performed but is only 50–80% occupied is kept and recorded in the merge provenance as low-occupancy, so a marginal stitch stays auditable afterwards. On a large table it runs in the background and narrates itself first — "Merging N events… (Cancel in the status bar stops it; nothing is changed until it finishes.)" Reversed by Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z), which restores the exact table including your curation.

controls.label: Merge events in selection
controls.what_it_does: Merge every detected event overlapping the on-trace Measure selection into one event (an explicit selection overrides the window). Turn on the Measure tool and drag a region first.
controls.notes: DISABLED until the active channel has a stored detection, AND it additionally needs a live cursor region: with no region the status bar says "Select a region on the trace first — turn on the Measure tool and drag, then Merge events in selection." Ignores the Window value entirely — anything the region touches is merged, however wide the gap. What an explicit selection does NOT override is the open-pore check: a drag is a coarse gesture, and a span its events cover less than 50% of is refused with "That selection is mostly open pore between its events, so merging it would make one long, shallow event rather than one translocation. Nothing was changed — drag over the fragments of a single event instead." With fewer than two events overlapping it says "Fewer than two events overlap the selection — nothing to merge." Reversed by Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z).

controls.label: Measure
controls.what_it_does: The fourth mode tab, holding the whole cursor-measurement tool: the toggle, the live statistics readout and the saved-measurements table.
controls.notes: The cursors deliberately stay LIVE while this tab is hidden — you can arm them here, switch to Detection, and keep measuring with Ctrl+M. Sits beside Preprocess / Detection / ML detector.

controls.label: Measure event (cursors)
controls.what_it_does: Show a movable region on the current-channel trace; its two edges are the boundary cursors. Double-click the trace to place it, drag the shaded body to move it, or drag either circular handle to resize it.
controls.notes: A TOGGLE (stays pressed), not a one-shot. Disabled when no channel is selected. Turns itself OFF automatically when you switch recording or channel — the region belonged to the old channel's pane. Kept in sync with the checkable Analysis ▸ Measure event menu item, which drives the same toggle and also raises this tab.

controls.label: Snap to view
controls.what_it_does: Place a mask over the middle 20% of the visible view, then drag its circular edge handles to fit the event. Double-clicking the trace places it at the click.
controls.notes: Turns the Measure toggle on for you. The 20% cap applies to initial placement only; either handle can still be dragged farther for a long event.

controls.label: Snap to selected event
controls.what_it_does: Set the cursors to the event last selected in the event table.
controls.notes: DISABLED until you have selected a row in the event table AND that event belongs to the channel currently on screen. Turns the Measure toggle on for you.

controls.label: Mark selection as missed event
controls.what_it_does: Add the current cursor selection to the active source detection as an event the detector MISSED. It is characterized like a detected event, marked reviewed + accepted + added, and counts as a miss (FN) in the detector score.
controls.notes: Feeds the SOURCE DETECTOR event table, not the measurement list below — this is the one button on this panel that does. The panel button is source-gated, but the Ctrl+Shift+M menu-action twin stays enabled whenever a recording is selected so it can loudly explain that no source exists or that Reconciled is derived and cannot be edited directly. A valid add also needs Measure on, an open target and a live selection. Never uses the preview: the raw samples of the bracketed span are re-characterized in full, under a wait cursor on a big span. Distinct from Ctrl+M, which saves an independent manual measurement and does not create a detector-training candidate.

controls.label: amplitude method
controls.what_it_does: How the in-selection level is defined for the amplitude: median/mean — central level; min/max — the deepest/peak sample; mode — the histogram-peak (flat-blockade) level.
controls.notes: Items in order: median, mean, min, max, mode. Default median. Changing it recomputes the readout immediately. WARNING with min/max: under a subsampled preview the level IS a tail order statistic, so level, amplitude, dI/I₀ and SNR are all blanked to "—" rather than reported low — they return the moment you save or zoom in. 'mode' is the most robust to rise/fall shoulders on a flat blockade.

controls.label: Live statistics
controls.what_it_does: Read-only live readout of everything about the current cursor selection, recomputed as you drag. Eighteen rows in order: "n samples", "dwell", "amplitude", "dI/I₀ (frac)", "level", "baseline I₀", "mean", "median", "std", "variance", "min", "max", "peak-to-peak", "rms", "skewness", "kurtosis (excess)", "area / ECD", "SNR".
controls.notes: Not selectable, not editable, takes no focus. Dwell auto-scales its unit (µs / ms / s); signal rows carry the channel's units, area/ECD carries units·s, variance units². "baseline I₀" is a LOCAL open-pore reference read from a window just outside your selection (capped at ~3 ms), not a global baseline. "kurtosis (excess)" is 0 for a Gaussian. A row showing "—" during a preview has a tooltip explaining it was withheld, not missing. The readout does not update on every drag frame — it settles ~60 ms after the cursors stop, and instantly on mouse-release.

controls.label: ≈ preview: 1:N sampling (M of T samples). Saving re-measures every sample.
controls.what_it_does: Amber line that appears under the readout when the selection is too big (over 200,000 samples) to measure in full at drag speed. Gives the sampling ratio and, when applicable, appends "Not estimated: min, max, ptp."
controls.notes: A preview is a normal working state, not an error — the numbers are good, they are just not the final ones. It disappears the moment an exact value is in hand, including right after Add to list. Saved rows are NEVER approximate: Add to list re-measures over every sample first.
controls.correction: f"≈ preview: 1:{stride} sampling ({measured:,} of {total:,} samples). Saving re-measures every sample." plus, when statistics were blanked, a second sentence appended after TWO spaces: f"  Not estimated: {', '.join(suppressed)}." (e.g. "  Not estimated: min, max."). The counts are thousands-separated. The line is hidden, not merely emptied, when the readout is exact.

controls.label: (refusal note)
controls.what_it_does: Red line that appears under the readout when the samples under the cursors (or the open-pore window beside them) are NaN/Inf, explaining why the whole readout is blank.
controls.notes: This IS an error state, unlike the amber preview line. It describes the CURRENT cursors and clears by itself as soon as you drag off the poisoned span. Without it the panel would just show a column of "—", which reads as "nothing selected".
controls.correction: No such placeholder exists in the source — the refusal line shows the text of the NonFiniteSelection exception, which reads either "selection [{start}, {stop}): {N} of {M} samples are non-finite (NaN/Inf) (first at index {i}) — a localised taint, not a dead channel. Every statistic over them is either NaN or a robust number quietly measured on a poisoned window. Crop the selection or clean the trace." or, when the flanks are the problem, "the open-pore window beside selection [{start}, {stop}): … The baseline, the polarity and the SNR denominator are all read from that window, so every amplitude here would be measured against a reference that is not a number. Move the selection away from it, or clean the trace." (When every sample is bad the middle clause instead reads "every one of {M} samples is non-finite (NaN/Inf) — a dead or mis-calibrated channel (a zero/infinite gain, or a conversion that overflowed float32), not a recording with a few bad samples.") It is red, it clears itself as soon as the cursors move off the poisoned span, and it is why the readout is all "—".

controls.label: Add to list
controls.what_it_does: Append the current measurement to the table below.  (Ctrl+M)
controls.notes: SHORTCUT Ctrl+M, but the shortcut lives on Analysis ▸ Add measurement to list, so it works from ANY tab — you never have to look at this panel. DISABLED until there is a valid live measurement. Always saves EXACT numbers: if the readout was a preview it is re-measured over every sample first (under a wait cursor above 2 M samples, ~1 s at 15 M), and the readout is then refreshed to show what was actually stored. Each row gets a running measurement_id that is never reused.

controls.label: Remove selected
controls.what_it_does: Delete every selected row. Shift/Ctrl-click to select more than one.
controls.notes: DESTRUCTIVE, and asks first: "Delete N manual measurements?" with the warning "You drew these on the trace by hand — nothing in the app can re-derive them. Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z) puts them back, and any project you have already saved still holds them." The default button is Cancel. Deletes by the rows you can SEE, correctly mapped through the sort/filter. Removing rows renumbers nothing — surviving measurement_ids stay as they were.

controls.label: Export CSV…
controls.what_it_does: Write every listed measurement to a CSV for extraction.
controls.notes: Writes the WHOLE table — every recording, every channel — regardless of what "This recording only" is currently hiding and regardless of what is selected. Suggests the filename measurements.csv. With an empty table it just says "No measurements to export yet — use “Add to list” first." and writes nothing.

controls.label: Go to measurement
controls.what_it_does: Put the cursors back on the selected row's span and zoom the trace to it (double-clicking the row does the same). Switches recording/channel if needed.
controls.notes: DISABLED until a row is selected. With several rows selected it goes to the TOPMOST ONE ON SCREEN (the one whose marker is highlighted), not the earliest measured. Fails honestly in the status line rather than silently: "…is not open — reopen it to return to this measurement." if the recording was closed, or "This measurement's span is no longer inside the loaded data." if you reopened the project at a shorter sample range.

controls.label: This recording only
controls.what_it_does: Hide rows measured on other recordings. The table itself still holds them (and Export CSV still writes them all).
controls.notes: Default off. The saved table is ONE pooled log across every recording, segment and channel measured this session — this only filters the view. With nothing selected and this ticked, the table shows nothing. Rows saved before the app recorded a durable document key fall back to matching on the display name.

controls.label: Show on trace
controls.what_it_does: Shade every saved measurement of this channel on the trace, so you can see at a glance where you have already measured. The selected row is highlighted.
controls.notes: Default ON. Muted violet for the set, brighter violet for the currently selected row — deliberately distinct from the detector's orange event spans and the blue measure region. Purely decorative; if no overlay renderer is available it switches itself off and says "On-trace markers are unavailable (no overlay renderer)."

controls.label: (saved measurements table)
controls.what_it_does: The running log of every measurement you have stamped. Column headers are the raw schema names, in order: measurement_id, recording, doc_key, channel, channel_index, start_idx, end_idx, t_start_s, dwell_s, n_samples, amplitude_method, level, baseline, amplitude, frac_amplitude, mean, median, std, var, min, max, ptp, rms, skewness, kurtosis, area_ecd, snr, label, units, cal_gain, cal_offset, t0_s. The last four are the row's provenance stamp: the units, gain and offset it was measured under and its recording's instrument-clock origin.
controls.notes: Click any header to sort (numeric columns sort numerically, not as text); starts sorted on measurement_id ascending. Multi-select with Shift/Ctrl. Ctrl+C (Cmd+C) copies the selected rows as TSV — header plus values, in the order displayed — but only while the table has focus. DOUBLE-CLICK navigates back to that measurement, EXCEPT on the "label" column, where it opens an editor instead. "label" is the ONLY editable cell — free text for why the row exists ("the weird double-dip"); it round-trips through the CSV and the project. THE TABLE NAMES ITS CLOCK: the t_start_s header reads "t_start_s (t₀=0)" whenever the recording on screen starts at a non-zero instrument time, and each row's own t0_s column carries its recording's origin — the table pools recordings, so t_start_s + t0_s is the row's start on the instrument clock. Row numbers on the left are view positions, not measurement ids, and they carry the row's calibration verdict: "⚠" for a row measured under a calibration that has since changed (kept, with a different tooltip, once its recording is closed), "?" for a row whose stamp has not been compared with anything (recording not open, or saved before the stamp columns existed), nothing at all for checked-and-current. Saved numbers are never rescaled — re-measure the span for a row under the current calibration.
controls.correction: The table has no title text at all; it is an untitled QTableView whose column headers are the MEASUREMENT_SCHEMA names, verbatim and in this order: measurement_id, recording, doc_key, channel, channel_index, start_idx, end_idx, t_start_s, dwell_s, n_samples, amplitude_method, level, baseline, amplitude, frac_amplitude, mean, median, std, var, min, max, ptp, rms, skewness, kurtosis, area_ecd, snr, label, units, cal_gain, cal_offset, t0_s — 32 columns, and t_start_s gains a " (t₀=0)" badge when the recording's clocks disagree. Row headers down the side are 1-based positions, not measurement ids, and may carry a trailing ⚠ or ?.

controls.label: Measure event
controls.what_it_does: Hand-select an event with cursors and measure its dwell, amplitude and full statistics (incl. kurtosis) live; add measurements to a saveable table.
controls.notes: Checkable, and kept in exact sync with the panel's own "Measure event (cursors)" toggle — one source of truth. Turning it on also RAISES the Measure tab, because a menu item that silently arms an invisible tool is what made this panel hard to find. Disabled until there is a live channel to select on.

controls.label: Add measurement to list
controls.what_it_does: Append the region currently selected on the trace to the measurement table. Works from any tab — turn on Measure event and drag a region first.
controls.notes: This is where Ctrl+M actually lives (not on the panel), so it fires no matter which tab or dock page is raised — that is the point, since the cursors stay live when the Measure tab is hidden. Tells you the first real blocker in the status bar instead of failing silently: "Nothing to measure — select a recording first.", "Measure is off. Turn on Analysis ▸ Measure event…", or "No region is selected on the trace — drag one across the event you want to measure, then press Ctrl+M."

controls.label: Fits
controls.what_it_does: The box that holds the fit controls — the two component spinboxes, the two checkboxes, the filter-limited note and the Fit button all live inside it. Source: QGroupBox("Fits") in StatsPanel.__init__.
controls.correction: "{n} accepted event(s) are filter-limited — {verb} the fits." where verb is "excluded from" when "include filter-limited events" is OFF and "INCLUDED in" (capitalised) when it is ON. The reported string is only the unchecked state; the label is empty and invisible when the count is 0.

controls.label: estimated false-positive rate: {pct}% (AAFT, {n} surrogates)
controls.what_it_does: The measured state of the false-positive line: after a Null control run it replaces "false-positive rate: not measured (run Null control)" with the percentage and how many AAFT surrogates it came from. Verbatim source: f"estimated false-positive rate: {100.0 * fdr:.1f}% (AAFT, {n} surrogates)". It is reset back to "not measured" whenever you select a recording that has no null control of its own, so it never reports another pore's number.

controls.label: false-positive rate NOT estimated — {n} detection(s) on this recording's own event-free noise (a lower bound, measured with no surrogate).
controls.what_it_does: The third state of the same line: shown when the null control refuses to stand behind a rate. Instead of a percentage you get the count of false detections found on the recording's own event-free noise, which is a lower bound. Hovering the line shows the reason for the refusal (the first entry of the result's notes).

controls.label: Detector score (vs your curation)
controls.group: Statistics panel (panels.py ScorePanel) — sits with the Summary
controls.what_it_does: A whole readout box the colleague's list omits entirely. Tooltip (verbatim): "Scores the DETECTOR against your curated truth: matched (kept), spurious (rejected) and missed (hand-added) events, and the precision/recall/F1 they imply. A ratio with a zero denominator shows as n/a." Its nine rows, verbatim and in order: "detected", "truth (kept)", "matched (TP)", "spurious (FP)", "missed (FN)", "auto-rejected", "precision", "recall", "F1". It refreshes on every curation / edit / hand-added event / new result, shows "—" when there is no detection and "n/a" (never a fake 0) for a ratio with a zero denominator; the values are selectable with the mouse so they can be copied. "auto-rejected" is the rows the DETECTOR rejected on its own (clipped by the boundary, over the max dwell, non-finite); they used to be counted as "spurious (FP)", which published the detector's honest self-flagging as its own false-positive rate. While no event has been rejected or hand-added BY YOU the three ratios read "not scored yet" rather than 1.000, and an amber caption under them says "Nothing rejected or hand-added yet — the truth is the detector's own output, so precision / recall / F1 would be 1.000 by construction." followed, when there are any, by "(N row(s) the detector rejected on its own are its flags, not your verdict, and are not counted as spurious.)"

controls.label: Manual measurement (cursors)
controls.what_it_does: The bold heading at the top of the measurement panel. Worth distinguishing from the tab, whose text is only "Manual measurement" (DetectionPanel.mode_tabs.addTab(self._measure_page, "Manual measurement")).

controls.label: label
controls.what_it_does: The free-text annotation column — the ONLY editable cell in the saved table. Double-click it (or press the edit key) to type why the row exists; the text is written into the CSV export and saved with the project. Double-clicking ANY OTHER column is the navigate gesture instead (it jumps the trace to that measurement), so this column is the one place a double-click means "rename". Rows are multi-select (Shift/Ctrl-click) and the table is sortable by clicking a header; it opens sorted by measurement_id ascending.

controls.label: Ctrl+C
controls.what_it_does: Copies the selected rows to the clipboard as TSV — a header line plus one line per row — in the order the rows appear ON SCREEN, not the order they were measured. Nothing in the UI advertises it: it is a QShortcut(QKeySequence.Copy) scoped to the table, so it only fires while the saved-measurements table has focus. The status line then reads "Copied N measurement(s) to the clipboard."

controls.label: Delete {n}
controls.what_it_does: The confirm button in the warning dialog that Remove selected always raises first. Dialog text: "Delete {n} manual measurement{s}?" and, verbatim, "You drew these on the trace by hand — nothing in the app can re-derive them. Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z) puts them back, and any project you have already saved still holds them." The other button is Cancel and it is the DEFAULT, so pressing Enter cancels. Choosing Cancel writes "Nothing was deleted." to the status line.

controls.label: Added measurement #{id} ({n} in list).
controls.group: Manual measurement panel (status line at the bottom)
controls.what_it_does: The grey status line under the saved table — the panel's only channel for telling you what happened, and absent from the colleague's list. Verbatim messages it shows: "Added measurement #N (M in list)."; "Removed N measurement(s) (M in list)."; "Nothing was deleted."; "Restored N measurement(s)." (project reopen); "Copied N measurement(s) to the clipboard."; "Wrote N measurement(s) to <file>." (after Export CSV…); "Select a saved measurement first." (Go to measurement with no row selected); "Showing measurement #N (recording · channel)."; "“<recording>” is not open — reopen it to return to this measurement."; "This measurement's span is no longer inside the loaded data."; "Could not switch to “<recording>” channel N to show this measurement."; "Could not re-measure the selection exactly; nothing was added."; "On-trace markers are unavailable (no overlay renderer)."; and, during a long exact measurement, "Characterizing all N samples…" alongside a wait cursor.

controls.label: Not shown while the readout is a subsampled preview — this statistic depends on the extreme samples, which subsampling systematically misses. The saved measurement includes it, computed over every sample.
controls.what_it_does: The tooltip put on each Live-statistics cell that has been blanked to "—" during a subsampled preview. It is how the user tells a withheld statistic (min/max-dependent ones) from a genuinely undefined one; the value appears as soon as the measurement is exact, and always appears in the saved row.

controls.label: Export measurements
controls.what_it_does: The title of the save dialog Export CSV… opens (suggested filename "measurements.csv", filter "CSV (*.csv);;All files (*)"; it writes exactly the file you name). With an empty table the same title appears on an information box reading, verbatim: "No measurements to export yet — use “Add to list” first." — and nothing is written.

controls.what_it_does: Show the selected stored result and its quality/fit views.

controls.what_it_does: Inspect the selected detector event table.
controls.notes: Candidate count includes rejected rows; accepted count is separate. Source: nanoscope/gui/analysis_panel.py.

controls.what_it_does: Read counts, rate and recorded event summaries.
