area: Event results, review decisions and Event Inspector
summary: The shared event table is sortable and supports acceptance, review and flags. The scientific event schema remains distinct from optional curation/amplitude columns, so column count depends on the result. Event Inspector shows one event with context, baseline, equivalent red level and optional fitted substates. Curate exposes explicit acceptance and optional amplitude methods, including a manually editable red level. Optional amplitude curation does not redefine the detector median depth, fractional depth, SNR, boundaries or fitted states.
opened_by: Select a result in Inspector → Analysis → Results → Events. Open Event inspector… from Analysis, or open a tile from Event gallery. Curate contains amplitude editing. Sources: nanoscope/gui/event_inspector.py, event_amplitude_controls.py, panels.py and analysis_panel.py; nanoscope/analysis/event_amplitude.py.
gotchas: There is NO search or filter box on the Event table — the only way to narrow it down is to sort by a column header, or to switch to the Event Inspector and use its All / Accepted only / Rejected only combo.
Table sorting compares the DISPLAYED TEXT, not the numbers, so numeric columns sort alphabetically (a dwell of '9e-05' sorts after '0.0012') — use it to group rows, never to rank them.
Sorting by the accepted column does nothing useful, because that column shows a checkbox and no text for the sorter to compare.

Only the accepted checkbox is editable in the table; every other cell is read-only, so double-clicking a wrong-looking number will never let you correct it — fix the event by dragging its region in the Event Inspector instead.
A plain click on a row only selects it — to change accepted you must click the checkbox indicator itself, or select the row and press a or r.
The j / k / a / r / f curation keys have no on-screen label anywhere and only work once the table has keyboard focus, so click a row first.

The f key adds the 'flagged' token to a row's existing reasons rather than replacing them, but re-running detection replaces the whole table and destroys every hand-written flag along with every accept/reject.

Accept all and Reject all rewrite the accepted column of the WHOLE detection — not just the events in the current filter — so they wipe every judgement you have already made; Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z) is the only way back. Accept all is the one exception: events the detector flagged as not measurable (clipped_by_boundary, dwell>max_dwell_s, non_finite) stay rejected, and a grey note under the button bar counts them — "3 events kept rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable".

Dragging an event region in the Event Inspector re-measures the event and can flip it from accepted to rejected on its own, because the automatic rules (clipped at a boundary, over max dwell, measured from a non-finite sample) are re-judged against the new bounds. zero_baseline is flagged on the row but never rejects it.

Changing event bounds invalidates the previous fitted levels for those bounds. The Inspector can re-fit that single event when the standing fit context remains valid; otherwise it clears the levels with an explicit reason. It does not silently reinterpret the old fit as current.
The Event Inspector's 'levels:' line and its 'CUSUM levels:' line are two different estimators and are allowed to disagree — the readout tells you when they do, and CUSUM is the fitted one.
The CUSUM level listing stops after 8 levels; if an event has more, the readout says how many it withheld and you must export the level table to see them all.

'Merge with next' silently uses the Window value from the Merge sub-events group in the Analysis panel — it never prompts, so check that number before clicking or the merge may report 'No sub-events within N ms to merge.'

Curating an event out of the active filter subset does not move you off it: the event stays on screen and the readout switches to 'filtered out of …', which can look like the Prev/Next buttons have stopped working.

A column header ending in ⚠ means those numbers were measured against an open-pore baseline that is no longer the configured one — they are shown exactly as stored, and can be an order of magnitude off on some recordings.

Event inspector… (Ctrl+I) requires a stored detection for the selected source. A saved result can be inspected without rerunning detection; selecting a recording with no detection leaves the inspector empty.

Optional amplitude fields retain the method, interval/level, units and provenance separately from detector median depth. Stale or unreproducible measurement contexts disable editing rather than silently falling back to raw data.
A selected or manually curated amplitude can be useful for an analyte without replacing the app-wide definition of depth_pA. Report which estimator was used.

controls.label: event_id
controls.what_it_does: The event's number within its source recording. This is the id the Event Inspector, the trace overlays and the merge report all refer to.
controls.notes: Sorting is done on the displayed text, so ids sort as text (10 lands next to 1, not after 9).

controls.label: recording
controls.what_it_does: Name of the recording the event came from.

controls.label: pore_id
controls.what_it_does: Which physical pore produced this event.
controls.notes: The schema's own warning: never pool statistics across different pores.

controls.label: start_idx
controls.what_it_does: First sample of the event, as a sample index.
controls.notes: Rewritten if you drag the event region in the Event Inspector.

controls.label: end_idx
controls.what_it_does: One past the last sample of the event, as a sample index.
controls.notes: Half-open, so end_idx − start_idx is the event length in samples. Rewritten by an Event Inspector region drag.

controls.label: t_start_s
controls.what_it_does: When the event starts, in seconds from the start of the recording.

controls.label: dwell_s
controls.what_it_does: How long the event lasted, in seconds ((end_idx − start_idx)/sample rate).
controls.notes: Shown to 6 significant figures, unlike most float columns which show 4.

controls.label: baseline_pA
controls.what_it_does: The event-span reference level summarized from the recorded open-pore baseline.
controls.notes: The reference may be an automatic track, known current or selected-interval track. The legacy _pA suffix does not supersede source units/domain. Changing the reference does not rewrite stored values until an explicit supported analysis action.

controls.label: depth_pA
controls.what_it_does: The median of the polarity-adjusted in-event deviation from the recorded baseline.
controls.notes: For standard correctly polarized events this is a positive excursion magnitude, not the peak, mean or optional curated amplitude. Source signal units/domain govern interpretation; the column keeps its legacy name. Source: nanoscope/analysis/characterize.py.

controls.label: frac_depth
controls.what_it_does: depth_pA divided by |baseline_pA| — i.e. ΔI/I₀, the fractional blockade.
controls.notes: Shown as 'dI/I0' in the Event Inspector title and readout. Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: ecd_pA_s
controls.what_it_does: Integrated charge deficit — the excursion summed over the event's duration.
controls.notes: Shown to 6 significant figures. Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: max_dev_pA
controls.what_it_does: The single largest excursion anywhere inside the event.
controls.notes: Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: mean_dev_pA
controls.what_it_does: The average excursion across the event.
controls.notes: Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: rise_s
controls.what_it_does: How long the current took to fall into the event (10–90% entry time), in seconds.
controls.notes: Shown to 6 significant figures. Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: fall_s
controls.what_it_does: How long the current took to come back out (90–10% exit time), in seconds.
controls.notes: Shown to 6 significant figures. Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: snr
controls.what_it_does: depth_pA divided by the baseline noise RMS.
controls.notes: Carries the ⚠ stale badge after a baseline-estimator change.

controls.label: n_levels
controls.what_it_does: How many sub-states were resolved inside the event; 1 means a simple square event.
controls.notes: This is the always-on BIC count, NOT the CUSUM fit. The Event Inspector prints both and says so when they disagree — BIC over-splits on a filtered trace, so disagreement is expected.

controls.label: filter_limited
controls.what_it_does: True when the event is shorter than about twice the filter rise time, so the low-pass never let the current reach the true blockade level.
controls.notes: These events are EXCLUDED from the dwell and depth fits by default (the Fits group's 'include filter-limited events' box turns that off). The Event Inspector appends 'filter-limited' to its plot title for such events.

controls.label: accepted
controls.what_it_does: The tick box that decides whether this event survives curation. Ticked events are the ones counted in the summary, fitted, plotted and written to exports; unticked ones are kept in the table but left out.
controls.notes: THE ONLY EDITABLE CELL IN THE TABLE — every other cell is read-only (NoEditTriggers). Click the checkbox indicator itself to toggle; a plain row click only selects. Ticking here writes the shared event frame in place, so the Event Inspector's Accepted box, the trace span overlays and the summary all update at once. Ticking is REFUSED on a row the detector flagged as not measurable (clipped_by_boundary, dwell>max_dwell_s, non_finite): the box snaps straight back, nothing is written, and the grey line under the table says "1 event kept rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable". Unticking is never blocked. This column shows no text, so sorting by it does nothing useful.

controls.label: flag
controls.what_it_does: Why an event is suspect — a ';'-joined SET of reasons, or empty. Tokens you can see here include zero_baseline, dwell>max_dwell_s, clipped_by_boundary, non_finite and flagged.
controls.notes: It is a set, not a single slot: a row can carry several reasons at once. 'flagged' is the only token a person writes (the f key); everything else the app derived.

controls.label: added
controls.what_it_does: True for an event you marked by hand with the Measure tool's 'Mark selection as missed event' rather than one the detector found.
controls.notes: Appears as a 21st column the first time a detection is shown; it is what the Detector score panel counts as a missed event (FN).

controls.label: name ⚠
controls.what_it_does: A column header that ends in ⚠ means those numbers were measured against an open-pore baseline that is no longer the configured one. The values shown are exactly what was stored — nothing has been re-measured.
controls.notes: Hovering the header OR any cell in that column shows the reason: 'Measured against an open-pore baseline that is no longer the configured one… Use the Re-measure depths button on the banner above, or Analysis > Compare baseline estimators... to see how much they would change.' Badged text also turns amber, but the ⚠ is there because colour is lost to colour-blind readers, screenshots and printed figures. Affects baseline_pA, depth_pA, frac_depth, ecd_pA_s, mean_dev_pA, max_dev_pA, snr, rise_s and fall_s.

controls.label: (column header — click to sort)
controls.what_it_does: Clicking any column header sorts the whole table by that column; clicking again reverses the direction.
controls.notes: No on-screen label of its own. Sorting is a display-only proxy — it never reorders or touches the underlying event data, and event_id keeps meaning the same event. IMPORTANT: it sorts on the DISPLAYED TEXT, so numeric columns sort alphabetically (a dwell of '9e-05' sorts after '0.0012'). Use it to group, not to rank.

controls.label: (table row — click to select)
controls.what_it_does: Clicking a row selects that whole event, zooms the trace view to it with a little padding, and drops a single marker overlay on it. If the Event Inspector is open it jumps to the same event.
controls.notes: No on-screen label of its own. One row at a time only (single selection, whole-row). You must select a row before the a / r / f keys will do anything.

controls.label: (refusal note)
controls.what_it_does: Grey line under the event table naming the accepts this table declined. Reads "N events kept rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable" (rows that were already rejected and stay so), "N events corrected back to rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable" (rows that were sitting accepted beside a rejecting flag), or, on a frame with no flag column, "N events NOT accepted: this table has no 'flag' column, so the detector's own rejections cannot be read — refusing rather than guessing". Recounted from the frame on every repaint, so it is a statement about the data and not about the last click: it survives an undo, a merge and a window opened afterwards, and dies only when the refused rows stop being refused or a new detection replaces the table.

controls.label: j
controls.what_it_does: Moves the selection down one row.
controls.notes: Keyboard only — nothing on screen says so. The table must have keyboard focus (click a row first). These keys are swallowed by the table, which also stops Qt's type-to-search from jumping to a row starting with that letter.

controls.label: k
controls.what_it_does: Moves the selection up one row.
controls.notes: Keyboard only. Works even with no row currently selected (it starts from the top).

controls.label: a
controls.what_it_does: Accepts the selected event — same as ticking its accepted box.
controls.notes: Keyboard only, and it does nothing unless a row is selected. Pair with j/k to curate a long table without touching the mouse. It goes through the same guard as the checkbox: on a row the detector flagged as not measurable the accept is refused, nothing is written, and the grey refusal line under the table counts it. r is never blocked.
controls.correction: pg.InfiniteLine(angle=0, movable=False, label="baseline") — a fixed grey dashed marker at the row's baseline_pA. It cannot be dragged; calling it a slider invites the user to try. event_inspector.py:258-261.

controls.label: r
controls.what_it_does: Rejects the selected event — same as unticking its accepted box.
controls.notes: Keyboard only; requires a selected row.
controls.correction: QLabel("Filter:") — a static caption, not a combo. The control beside it is an unlabelled QComboBox holding All / Accepted only / Rejected only. event_inspector.py:229.

controls.label: f
controls.what_it_does: Marks the selected event with your own 'flagged' token in the flag column — 'I looked at this one and want to find it again'.
controls.notes: Keyboard only; requires a selected row. It ADDS to the flag cell rather than overwriting it, so an event that was already clipped_by_boundary keeps that reason. This is the only flag token a person writes; it survives a merge, a mask resize and a hand-added event, and re-running detection destroys it (which is why re-detection warns and is undoable).
controls.correction: QLabel("of 0") — a read-only caption, not a combo box. Its text is rewritten to f"of {n}" (e.g. "of 412") whenever the filter subset changes; "of 0" is only the empty state. event_inspector.py:187, 1007, 1013.

controls.label: Event inspector…
controls.what_it_does: Opens the Event Inspector window: 'Step through the detected events one at a time: see each event's raw waveform with its baseline/level/boundaries and accept/reject it. Curation flows back to the table, the trace, the summary and the exports.'
controls.notes: DISABLED until the currently selected recording+channel has a detection — run detection (or the ML detector) first. Ctrl+I opens the Inspector. Only ever one Inspector window: choosing it again re-focuses the existing one and re-feeds it the current detection. The menu item is written '&Event inspector…' in source, so the underlined mnemonic is E.

controls.label: ◀ Prev
controls.what_it_does: Goes to the previous event in the current filter (←).
controls.notes: Disabled when you are already on the first event of the subset, and when the subset is empty. If you just curated the displayed event out of the subset (e.g. rejected it while viewing 'Accepted only'), this snaps to the nearest remaining event behind it.

controls.label: Event
controls.what_it_does: Jump to the i-th event of the current filter subset — type a number or use the arrows.
controls.notes: The box's prefix is the word 'Event ', so it reads e.g. 'Event 12'. This is a POSITION within the current filter (1..N), not the event_id. DISABLED whenever the current filter subset is empty; otherwise its range is 1 to the subset size.
controls.correction: setPrefix("Event ") — trailing space; the visible text is "Event 3" (the i-th event of the current filter subset, 1-based), not "Event". It is disabled and shows 0 when the subset is empty. event_inspector.py:183, 1004-1012.

controls.label: of 0
controls.what_it_does: A read-only count sitting beside the spinbox: how many events are in the current filter subset, e.g. 'of 412'.
controls.notes: Not a control — it is a label. It reads 'of 0' when there is no detection or nothing matches the filter.
controls.correction: QLabel("of 0") — a read-only caption, not a combo box. Its text is rewritten to f"of {n}" (e.g. "of 412") whenever the filter subset changes; "of 0" is only the empty state. event_inspector.py:187, 1007, 1013.

controls.label: Next ▶
controls.what_it_does: Goes to the next event in the current filter (→).
controls.notes: Disabled when you are on the last event of the subset, and when the subset is empty.

controls.label: Filter:
controls.what_it_does: A label naming the filter combo to its right.
controls.notes: Static text, not a control.
controls.correction: QLabel("Filter:") — a static caption, not a combo. The control beside it is an unlabelled QComboBox holding All / Accepted only / Rejected only. event_inspector.py:229.

controls.label: All
controls.what_it_does: Browse every detected event, accepted or not. This is the default and the state the window resets to whenever a new detection is installed.
controls.notes: One of the three items in the Filter combo, whose tooltip reads: 'The browsed subset. Prev/Next step within it (curation moves events between the Accepted and Rejected subsets).'

controls.label: Accepted only
controls.what_it_does: Restrict Prev/Next and the Event spinbox to events you have accepted.
controls.notes: Rejecting the event you are looking at leaves it on screen but drops it out of this subset — the readout then says 'filtered out of Accepted only (N shown)' instead of 'i of N'. If nothing is accepted, the plot shows 'No events match “Accepted only”.'

controls.label: Rejected only
controls.what_it_does: Restrict Prev/Next and the Event spinbox to events you have rejected — the fast way to re-check what you threw away.
controls.notes: Same behaviour as above: accepting the displayed event moves it out of this subset without navigating away.

controls.label: Accept all
controls.what_it_does: Mark every detected event accepted — the whole column, including events you have already judged. Events the detector flagged as unmeasurable (clipped by the boundary, over the dwell limit, measured from a non-finite sample) stay rejected: that is not a decision this button can reverse — the note under this bar counts them. Reversed by Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z).
controls.notes: DESTRUCTIVE to hand curation: it overwrites the accepted column of the whole detection, not just the events in the current filter, so every reject you have made is wiped — except the detector's own rejections, which it refuses to overwrite. The table, the trace span overlays and the summary all reset from it, and the grey note under the bar reads e.g. "3 events kept rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable". It is a no-op when there is no detection or the detection found no events.

controls.label: Reject all
controls.what_it_does: Mark every detected event rejected — the whole column, including events you have already judged. Reversed by Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z).
controls.notes: DESTRUCTIVE in the same way as Accept all, and it empties your exports until you accept something again. The intended workflow is 'Reject all, then accept the good ones' (or the reverse with Accept all).

controls.label: (refusal note)
controls.what_it_does: Grey line under the button bar naming the accepts this window declined — the same sentence, in the same words, as the event table's own note, and covering the Accepted checkbox and the A key as well as Accept all. Reads "N events kept rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable" (rows that were already rejected and stay so), "N events corrected back to rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable" (rows that were sitting accepted beside a rejecting flag), or, on a frame with no flag column, "N events NOT accepted: this table has no 'flag' column, so the detector's own rejections cannot be read — refusing rather than guessing". Recounted from the frame on every repaint, so it is a statement about the data and not about the last click: it survives an undo, a merge and a window opened afterwards, and dies only when the refused rows stop being refused or a new detection replaces the table.

controls.label: Merge with next
controls.what_it_does: Stitch this event to the following event(s) within the merge window into one event, then advance. Reversed by Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z).
controls.notes: DISABLED until a detection is installed and an event is displayed. The window it uses is the 'Window' spinbox (ms) in the Merge sub-events group of the Analysis panel — this button never asks you for one. If no following event sits within that window the status bar says 'No sub-events within N ms to merge.' and nothing changes. If one IS within the window but the span the two would make is mostly open pore — its events covering less than 50% of it — the merge is REFUSED rather than performed, and the status bar says so; see 'Merge all' for why. Undo restores the exact table the merge replaced; re-running detection does NOT — that replaces the whole table and takes every accept/reject with it.

controls.label: Accepted
controls.what_it_does: Curate this event (A = accept, R = reject, Space = toggle).
controls.notes: DISABLED until a detection is installed and an event is displayed. Ticking it does NOT navigate — the event you just judged stays on screen; only what Prev/Next will step through changes. The tick writes the same shared frame the table edits, so the matching table row's checkbox flips at the same moment.

controls.label: (shaded event region — drag either edge)
controls.what_it_does: The orange shaded band marks where the event is. Its two edges are draggable handles: pull one to correct the event's start or end, and on release the event's boundaries are rewritten and every measured number for it is recomputed.
controls.notes: Dragging re-measures event bounds under the recorded analysis context and re-evaluates acceptance rules. Optional amplitude measurements are checked for staleness. Existing substates are re-fit only when the valid standing context permits, otherwise cleared with an explicit explanation.

controls.label: baseline
controls.what_it_does: The grey dashed horizontal line labelled 'baseline' shows the local open-pore current (this row's baseline_pA) that the event's depth was measured against.
controls.notes: Not draggable — it is an annotation. Falls back to the median of the displayed window if the stored baseline is not a finite number.
controls.correction: pg.InfiniteLine(angle=0, movable=False, label="baseline") — a fixed grey dashed marker at the row's baseline_pA. It cannot be dragged; calling it a slider invites the user to try. event_inspector.py:258-261.

controls.label: level
controls.what_it_does: Show the equivalent event level corresponding to its current amplitude measurement.
controls.notes: By default the level represents the detector median depth relative to the recorded baseline. In Curate, Edit red level unlocks dragging; releasing saves an optional manual amplitude for this event. It does not change depth_pA, frac_depth, SNR, boundaries or substates. Edit → Undo reverses the curation.

controls.label: (green level segments)
controls.what_it_does: When a CUSUM level fit has been run, each fitted sub-state is drawn as a flat green horizontal segment at its own mean current, spanning exactly that state's samples — so you can judge by eye where the fit says the molecule changed state.
controls.notes: No on-screen label. Only appears after a level fit has been run for this detection; absent otherwise. Cleared for an event whose region you drag, and cleared entirely when a different detection is installed (a fit belongs only to the frame it was fitted on). Drawn as a bright green stroke over a near-black casing so it reads over the waveform, with a thin dashed riser at each state change and a per-level label (e.g. “L0  12.3 pA”) on segments wide enough to carry one.

controls.label: Event
controls.what_it_does: The group box under the waveform holding the full per-event numbers in a fixed-width font. Its text is selectable so you can copy a value out.
controls.notes: Group box title is the single word 'Event'. In the empty state it shows the same message as the plot, e.g. 'No detection — run detection to browse events.'
controls.correction: setPrefix("Event ") — trailing space; the visible text is "Event 3" (the i-th event of the current filter subset, 1-based), not "Event". It is disabled and shows 0 when the subset is empty. event_inspector.py:183, 1004-1012.

controls.label: Event 12    [3 of 412 · All]
controls.what_it_does: First readout line: the event's id, then where it sits in the current filter subset and which filter that is.
controls.notes: If you curate the displayed event out of the active subset this line changes to 'filtered out of Accepted only (N shown)' — the event is still on screen, it just is not in the subset Prev/Next walks.

controls.label: accepted:
controls.what_it_does: 'yes' or 'no' — whether this event currently survives curation.
controls.notes: Mirrors the Accepted checkbox and the table's accepted column.

controls.label: dwell:
controls.what_it_does: How long the event lasted, in microseconds, with the seconds value in brackets after it.

controls.label: depth:
controls.what_it_does: The excursion magnitude, in the channel's own units.
controls.notes: The unit shown is read from the calibrated channel, so it may say pA, nA or nothing — even though the underlying column is named depth_pA. A non-finite or unmeasurable value prints as an em dash (—).

controls.label: dI/I0:
controls.what_it_does: The fractional blockade, depth divided by |baseline| (the frac_depth column).

controls.label: SNR:
controls.what_it_does: Depth divided by the baseline noise RMS.

controls.label: rise / fall:
controls.what_it_does: The 10–90% entry time and the 90–10% exit time, both in microseconds, separated by a slash.

controls.label: levels:
controls.what_it_does: How many sub-states were resolved inside the event (1 = a simple square event).
controls.notes: This is the always-on BIC count from the events table, NOT the CUSUM fit. If a CUSUM fit disagrees, the block below says so explicitly.

controls.label: filter-limited:
controls.what_it_does: 'yes' or 'no' — whether the event is short enough that the low-pass attenuated its depth and stretched its dwell.
controls.notes: 'yes' events are dropped from the dwell/depth fits unless you turn on 'include filter-limited events' in the Fits group. The plot title also appends 'filter-limited' for these.

controls.label: baseline:
controls.what_it_does: The local open-pore current this event was measured against, in the channel's own units.

controls.label: CUSUM levels:
controls.what_it_does: Heading of the per-level breakdown: how many sub-states the CUSUM fit found for this event.
controls.notes: THIS WHOLE BLOCK IS ABSENT unless a CUSUM level fit has been run — a level fit is on-demand, so most of the time the readout ends at 'baseline:'. It is also dropped for any event whose region you drag.

controls.label: (BIC count says N; CUSUM is the fitted estimate)
controls.what_it_does: Appears only when the always-on BIC level count and the CUSUM fit disagree, telling you which number to trust.
controls.notes: Disagreement is expected, not a bug: BIC over-splits on a filtered trace. The line names CUSUM as the fitted estimate.

controls.label: L0: …
controls.what_it_does: One line per fitted sub-state: its index (L0, L1, L2…), its depth in the channel's units, its dwell in µs, its dI/I0, and — when defined — a signed 'step' giving the change from the previous level.
controls.notes: These are the same states drawn as green segments on the waveform above.

controls.label: … N more (export the level table to see all)
controls.what_it_does: Appears when an event has more than 8 fitted levels: the readout lists only the first 8 and this line says how many were withheld.
controls.notes: The cap exists so a 32-level event cannot push the window taller and squeeze the waveform. Export the level table to see the complete set.

controls.label: No detection — run detection to browse events.
controls.what_it_does: Shown centred on the blank plot (and in the readout) when the Inspector has no detection installed at all.
controls.notes: Run detection, or select a recording+channel that has one.

controls.label: Detection found no events.
controls.what_it_does: Shown when a detection ran but produced zero events.
controls.notes: Loosen the detection thresholds or the dwell limits and run again.

controls.label: No events match “All”.
controls.what_it_does: Shown when the chosen Filter subset is empty — the quoted word is whichever filter is selected (All / Accepted only / Rejected only).
controls.notes: Switch the Filter combo back to All to see the events again.

controls.label: The recording for this detection was closed.
controls.what_it_does: Shown when the recording whose events you were browsing has been closed, so there is no waveform left to draw.
controls.notes: Re-open the recording. Closing a recording takes its results with it and Undo cannot reach past a close.

controls.label: This channel has no samples to show.
controls.what_it_does: Shown when the channel behind the detection contains no data to plot.

controls.label: NanoScope — Event inspector
controls.what_it_does: The title bar of the inspector itself — it is a separate top-level window (QMainWindow), not a dock or a tab inside the main window. Opened from Analysis ▸ Event inspector…, it opens at 780×640 and there is only ever one; re-invoking the menu action re-focuses the existing window. Source: setWindowTitle("NanoScope — Event inspector") at event_inspector.py:140.

Left-arrow key: same as ◀ Prev — steps back one event within the current Filter subset. It is a window-wide shortcut (Qt.WindowShortcut), so it fires wherever the focus is inside the inspector, including while the Event spin box has focus. Source: event_inspector.py:297.
Right-arrow key: same as Next ▶ — steps forward one event within the current Filter subset. Window-wide shortcut, fires wherever the focus is inside the inspector. Source: event_inspector.py:298.

controls.label: Space
controls.what_it_does: Toggles the Accepted checkbox for the event currently on screen (accept if it was rejected, reject if it was accepted). A and R also work in this window — A accepts, R rejects — and unlike the table's a/r keys they act on the event the inspector is displaying, not on the table's selected row. Curating does NOT navigate: the event stays on screen even if it just dropped out of an "Accepted only" view. Source: event_inspector.py:299-301.

controls.label: (shaded event region — drag the middle to slide the whole window)
controls.what_it_does: The orange region is fully movable, not only its two edges: dragging its body slides the entire event window along the trace, changing both bounds at once. Either gesture (edge or body) rewrites this event's start_idx / end_idx / t_start_s in the shared event table and re-measures every statistic on the same conditioned trace the detector used — which can also flip the row's accepted state and rewrite its flag text, and it DISCARDS any CUSUM levels fitted for that event until you re-run the level fit. A drag that collapses or crosses the edges snaps back and makes no change. The edit is recorded in the undo history (Edit ▸ Undo). Source: pg.LinearRegionItem(movable=True) at event_inspector.py:254, _on_region_edited / _write_measured_row / _invalidate_levels_for_row.

controls.label: Event 12   ·   dwell 250 µs   ·   depth 45.2 pA   ·   dI/I0 0.153   ·   filter-limited
controls.what_it_does: The one-line title drawn above the waveform (separate from the "Event" readout box below it): event id, dwell in µs, depth in the channel's own units and dI/I0, joined by "   ·   ". The trailing "filter-limited" appears only when that event is filter-limited. The title is cleared in the empty states. Source: _event_title(), event_inspector.py:851-862.

controls.label: filtered out of Accepted only (12 shown)
controls.what_it_does: Replaces the "[3 of 412 · All]" part of the readout's first line when the event on screen is no longer a member of the chosen Filter subset — e.g. you press R while browsing "Accepted only". The event stays displayed; Prev/Next then jump to the nearest event that IS in the subset. Source: f"filtered out of {self._filter} ({len(subset)} shown)", event_inspector.py:875.

controls.label: step +1.234 pA
controls.what_it_does: Tail of each "  L0: …" level line: the signed change in current from the previous level, in the channel's units. It is omitted when the step is not a finite number (e.g. the first level). Source: f"   step {lv.step_pA:+.4g}{units}", event_inspector.py:980-981.

controls.label: (readout text — drag to select and copy)
controls.what_it_does: The whole monospaced stats block inside the "Event" box is selectable text: drag across it and copy to paste the numbers into a notebook or email. It is read-only — typing in it does nothing. Source: setTextInteractionFlags(Qt.TextSelectableByMouse), event_inspector.py:276.

controls.label: (row-number header — 0-based, renumbers when you sort)
controls.what_it_does: The narrow grey header down the left edge numbers the visible rows starting at 0. It is NOT the event id and it does not follow a row through a sort — use the event_id column to identify an event. Source: headerData() returns the raw section number for the vertical header, panels.py:2913-2914.

controls.label: Accept
controls.what_it_does: Accept the displayed event — the same write as the A key and the Accepted checkbox. Does not advance; press → for the next event.
controls.notes: Added because the Accepted checkbox is a state indicator, not an action affordance — a whole detection was once curated without either being found. DISABLED until a detection is installed and an event is displayed. Accepts an event the detector flagged unmeasurable only if the derived guard allows it; a refusal is reported under the toolbar, nothing is written.

controls.label: Reject
controls.what_it_does: Reject the displayed event — the same write as the R key. Does not advance; press → for the next event.
controls.notes: Same handler as the R key, exactly. The curated event stays on screen so you can change your mind; the Prev/Next filter subsets reflect the new state immediately.

controls.label: ⟵ / ⟶ (pan)
controls.what_it_does: Pan the waveform view left/right by half a window, to inspect the trace before/after the event.
controls.notes: A pure VIEW move: the event mask, the table and the readout are untouched, and the next Prev/Next re-centres as always. Buttons rather than drag because the movable mask region owns the drag gesture over the middle of the view — dragging there resizes/moves the mask, not the view. DISABLED until an event is displayed.

controls.label: Gallery…
controls.what_it_does: Open (or focus) the Event gallery — the contact sheet of every detected event.
controls.notes: The direct road between the two curation surfaces; the same window as Analysis ▸ Event gallery… (under 'Explore this recording', where it is easy to miss from here).

controls.label: Show in trace
controls.what_it_does: Centre the main trace on the event you are looking at — the same jump as double-clicking its tile in the gallery.
controls.notes: The third side of the triangle, and the one that did not exist: the Analysis panel opens the inspector and the gallery, and the gallery jumps to the trace, but from here the only way to see the event in its recording was to hunt for its row in the event table. A pure VIEW move — it changes no curation. DISABLED until an event is displayed.

controls.label: Context:
controls.what_it_does: How much recording to load either side of the event. Four choices: "± 3 ms" (default), "± 30 ms", "± 300 ms" and "Whole trace". Tooltip: "How much recording to load either side of the event. Kept while you step through events; the pan arrows and the mouse (drag / wheel) move within it and load more as needed."
controls.notes: ±3 ms was the hard-coded pad and unreachable from the UI, which made it a CEILING rather than a default — panning inside a 6 ms slice cannot answer "was the pore quiet before this?", only loading more samples can. The choice PERSISTS across navigation on purpose: it is a working preference, not a per-event one, so stepping with Prev/Next does not throw it away. Re-picking the entry that is already current re-frames the view, which is how you get back to ±3 ms after zooming out with the wheel.

controls.label: Amplitude
controls.what_it_does: Choose an optional event-amplitude estimator.
controls.notes: Median depth (whole event), Mean depth (whole event), Peak excursion (whole event), Histogram mode (whole event), Median of selected interval / state, Mean of selected interval / state, or Manual level. This is an opt-in measurement distinct from detector median depth. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Apply
controls.what_it_does: Save the chosen optional amplitude for the current event.
controls.notes: Leaves depth_pA, dI/I0, SNR, boundaries and fitted states unchanged. Read the recorded units and method. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Apply to all…
controls.what_it_does: Apply a supported whole-event amplitude estimator to eligible events.
controls.notes: Read the scope/confirmation; selected intervals and a manual level are event-specific, not universal analyte estimates. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Reset amplitude
controls.what_it_does: Clear the optional amplitude measurement for the current event.
controls.notes: Returns the presentation to the detector median-depth convention; does not rerun detection. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Edit red level
controls.what_it_does: Unlock the red equivalent-level line for manual curation.
controls.notes: A drag release saves a manual amplitude for this event only. Undo through Edit → Undo. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Interval samples
controls.what_it_does: Set the absolute inclusive start and exclusive stop sample for a selected-interval amplitude.
controls.notes: These are sample indices, unlike the open-pore reference interval table in seconds. The purple interval stays inside the event and does not resize its detected boundaries. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Use fitted state
controls.what_it_does: Populate an amplitude interval from an available fitted state.
controls.notes: Uses an existing state; selecting it does not run the substate fitter. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Equivalent level
controls.what_it_does: Type a signed manual level in the recorded current units.
controls.notes: Apply to commit, or drag the unlocked red line. This is a level, not directly an unsigned depth. Source: nanoscope/gui/event_amplitude_controls.py.

controls.label: Source detections
controls.what_it_does: Choose stored source detector tables.
controls.notes: Two or more detector results, or one table containing both manual and automatic candidates, are needed for a useful reconciliation. Source: nanoscope/gui/reconcile_dialog.py.

controls.label: Minimum temporal overlap
controls.what_it_does: Set shared time as a percentage of the shorter candidate.
controls.notes: Range 1–100%, default 50%; this is not IoU. Source: nanoscope/gui/reconcile_dialog.py.

controls.label: Required detector support
controls.what_it_does: Choose how many selected detector tables must support an automatic group.
controls.notes: One gives union, all gives intersection, intermediate counts give agreement. These are matching rules, not confidence levels. Source: nanoscope/gui/reconcile_dialog.py.

controls.label: Keep manual-only events
controls.what_it_does: Retain hand-added candidates without automatic detector support.
controls.notes: Default on. Their manual provenance remains distinct from automatic support. Source: nanoscope/gui/reconcile_dialog.py.

controls.label: Preview
controls.what_it_does: Calculate the proposed derived table and its counts without storing it.
controls.notes: Any input change invalidates the preview. Inspect contradictory curation decisions and unresolved label conflicts. Source: nanoscope/gui/reconcile_dialog.py.

controls.label: Create reconciled table
controls.what_it_does: Install the exact current preview as a separate result.
controls.notes: Source tables remain unchanged; use Table to switch between them. Creation does not certify the reconciled table as ground truth. Source: nanoscope/gui/reconcile_dialog.py.

area: Event gallery — paged waveform review and curation
summary: Event gallery is a contact sheet of the selected detection, with waveform tiles, sorting, selection, paging and immediate shared curation. It is not the Figure Library: gallery actions review events, while library actions store frozen figures. Acceptance changes reach the live event table and summary; previously generated plots and saved snapshots retain their captured values and can become stale. Source units and reference validity still determine how amplitudes may be interpreted.
opened_by: Analysis → Event gallery… (Ctrl+G), Event gallery on the launcher/Analysis home, or Gallery… in Event Inspector. A stored detection is required. Reopening reuses the gallery window. Sources: nanoscope/gui/event_gallery.py, event_inspector.py and main_window.py.
gotchas: Curation here is immediate and shared with the active event table/trace/summary. Generated plot results and Figure Library snapshots keep their captured numbers and can become stale; they are not silently recomputed. Apply in the label toolbar applies a label, not an acceptance decision. Undo lives in the main window.

"Accept all …" / "Reject all …" at the bottom act on the entire current filter across every page, not on the page you are looking at — with Show = "All" that is the whole detection, in one click, with no confirmation. "Accept all …" additionally refuses the tiles the detector flagged as not measurable: it says so before you click (its label becomes "Accept 313 of 317") and again afterwards, in the status line's "N tiles kept rejected" clause.
Space is not a per-tile toggle: on a mixed selection, if any selected tile is accepted the whole selection becomes rejected.
Under Show = "Accepted only" or "Rejected only", curating a tile makes it vanish from the grid immediately and re-numbers the pages — the events are fine, they have just left the filter.
With "Same depth scale" unchecked, every tile fills its full height whatever its depth, so a 15 pA and a 45 pA event look identical; never judge depth in that mode, only shape.

With "Same depth scale" checked, the scale is the 98th percentile of the detection's depths, so unusually deep events are deliberately clipped at the tile's bottom edge — a flat-bottomed tile means "deeper than the bulk", not "measured this depth".
The ◀ and ▶ tooltips advertise ← and →, but the arrow keys only move the tile cursor within the page; use PgUp/PgDn, Home/End or the pager buttons to turn pages.
Home means "first page" in this window, whereas Home in the main window resets the trace zoom.
Double-click opens the event in Event Inspector; it does not accept/reject it. Show in trace is the explicit trace-navigation action. Check the current status hint for modifier and keyboard gestures.
Under Per page = "Fit" there is no scrollbar at all, and resizing the window silently changes how many tiles a page holds and how many pages there are.

Depth captions must be interpreted using the source units/domain; fractional depth is dimensionless. Do not infer physical pA merely from a historical field name or from a visually similar tile height.
Events whose sort value could not be measured are always parked at the very END of the grid (last page), not left where they fell — check the last page when sorting by depth or dwell.

The window always shows the CURRENTLY selected detection: switching recording or detection re-feeds it, and selecting something with no detection empties it to "No detection — run detection to fill the gallery."
Opening the gallery focuses its first tile, which moves the main window's event selection and trace to that event even though you only asked to open a window.

controls.label: Show
controls.what_it_does: Chooses which events the grid contains: all of them, only the ones you have accepted, or only the ones you have rejected. Options are "All", "Accepted only" and "Rejected only".
controls.notes: Same three subsets, by the same names, as the Event inspector. Changing it re-pages the grid from the start of the new subset, and it also decides what "Accept all …" / "Reject all …" at the bottom will act on.

controls.label: All
controls.what_it_does: Every detected event in the current detection appears as a tile, accepted or not. This is the default.
controls.notes: Only with this option does "Accept all …" / "Reject all …" act on the whole detection.

controls.label: Accepted only
controls.what_it_does: Shows only events currently marked accepted — the set that will actually go into your plots and exports.
controls.notes: The moment you reject a tile in this view it disappears from the grid; that is not a bug, it has left the filter. Tile counts and page count change under you as you curate.

controls.label: Rejected only
controls.what_it_does: Shows only the events you have thrown out — useful for a second pass over your own culling before you export.
controls.notes: Accepting a tile here makes it vanish from the grid. "Accept all …" while this filter is on un-rejects everything you had rejected.

controls.label: Sort
controls.what_it_does: Sets the order tiles are laid out in, and changes what each tile's caption reports. Options are "Detection order", "Dwell (longest first)", "Depth (deepest first)" and "dI/I0 (deepest first)".
controls.notes: Sorting also rewrites every caption, so the grid can be read down as a sequence. Events whose value could not be measured (NaN) are always parked at the END of the grid, never scattered through the middle.

controls.label: Detection order
controls.what_it_does: Lays tiles out in the order the detector found them, i.e. in time. This is the default, and the only order in which a tile's neighbours are its neighbours in the recording.
controls.notes: Use this when hunting for bursts of false positives from one disturbance — they show up as a run of bad tiles rather than being scattered. Caption reads "<id> · <dwell>".

controls.label: Dwell (longest first)
controls.what_it_does: Longest events first, shortest last. Puts your clogs and long translocations at the top of page 1 and your one-sample spikes at the very end.
controls.notes: Caption reads "<id> · <dwell>", e.g. "412 · 1.35ms". Dwell is auto-formatted: microseconds under 1 ms, then ms.

controls.label: Depth (deepest first)
controls.what_it_does: Deepest blockade (largest current drop in pA) first. Combined with "Same depth scale" on, the grid then visibly shallows as you read down.
controls.notes: Caption switches to "<id> · <depth>" — a bare 3-significant-figure number with NO unit shown; it is pA.

controls.label: dI/I0 (deepest first)
controls.what_it_does: Sort by each event’s recorded fractional depth, rather than absolute current excursion.
controls.notes: A ratio is not invariant to arbitrary drift, offsets or reference errors. Review the baseline and source units; this sort does not recalculate the values.

controls.label: Tiles
controls.what_it_does: Sets how big each waveform thumbnail is drawn. Options are "Small", "Medium" (default) and "Large".
controls.notes: Bigger tiles mean fewer events per screen; under Per page = "Fit" the page size is recomputed immediately, so changing tile size changes how many pages you have. Every thumbnail is redrawn at the new width (a large tile is genuinely recomputed, not a blown-up small one), so there is a brief redraw on a big detection.

controls.label: Small
controls.what_it_does: 96 x 72 px thumbnails — the most events per screen, for a fast "is anything obviously wrong here" sweep.
controls.notes: At this size a marginal event and a clean one can be hard to tell apart; use it to find suspicious runs, then switch up to judge them.

controls.label: Medium
controls.what_it_does: 140 x 104 px thumbnails. The default, and the working size for most triage.
controls.notes: This is the size restored whenever the window is first built in a session.

controls.label: Large
controls.what_it_does: 200 x 148 px thumbnails — enough detail to see sub-states and noise character without opening the inspector.
controls.notes: Fewest tiles per page, so expect many more page turns under Per page = "Fit".

controls.label: Same depth scale
controls.what_it_does: "Draw every tile against one depth scale for the whole detection, so a deep event looks deeper than a shallow one. Uncheck to scale each tile to itself, which is better for comparing event SHAPE when the depths are similar."
controls.notes: ON by default. When on, the shared scale is the 98th percentile of the detection's own depths (not the maximum), so one freak deep event cannot flatten the other nine hundred — an outlier simply clips at the bottom edge of its tile. Each tile is still referenced to its OWN open-pore baseline, so a drifting baseline does not push traces off the tile. When off, every tile fills top-to-bottom regardless of depth, which makes a 15 pA and a 45 pA event draw identically — do not judge depth in this mode. Toggling is instant (repaint only, no recompute).

controls.label: Inspector…
controls.what_it_does: Open the FOCUSED tile's event in the Event Inspector, where its bounds, its sub-state levels and its flags can be edited. (Verbatim tooltip; it adds "Double-clicking a tile does the same; right-click a tile for the trace instead.")
controls.notes: Acts on the tile that has FOCUS, not on the whole selection, and does nothing at all with nothing focused — "open this one" needs a this. It emits the same request the double-click and the context menu do, so all three land on the same inspector rather than on three implementations of one. This is the way out of the grid; the inspector's own "Gallery…" is the way back.

controls.label: Accept selected
controls.what_it_does: "Mark every selected tile accepted (drag a box, or Ctrl/Shift-click, to select)."
controls.notes: Keyboard equivalent: A. Does nothing if no tiles are selected. Disabled while the current page has no tiles (no detection loaded, or the filter subset is empty). Writes the shared events table immediately — no separate confirm — and the change reaches the event table, the trace overlays, the summary and the exports. Selected tiles the detector flagged as not measurable are NOT accepted: they stay rejected and the status line's "N tiles kept rejected" clause counts them. Reject selected is never blocked.

controls.label: Reject selected
controls.what_it_does: "Mark every selected tile rejected."
controls.notes: Keyboard equivalent: R. Same gating as Accept selected (disabled when the page is empty; a no-op with nothing selected). Rejected events are excluded from plots and exports, so this is the main culling action in this window.

controls.label: (tile grid)
controls.what_it_does: The contact sheet itself: one tile per event on the current page. Each tile draws the calibrated current around the event as a blue min/max envelope, with the event's own span shaded in orange behind it (the same hue the main trace uses for event overlays) and a caption underneath giving the event id and the value the current sort is about.
controls.notes: The window shown on a tile is the event plus half its own length of open pore on each side (at least 25 samples), so the blockade always sits in the middle ~50% of the tile with real baseline either side to judge it against. The trace is a min/max band, one vertical segment per pixel column, so a short sub-state inside a long event still shows instead of being stepped over. Rejected tiles are drawn dimmed with a red border and red caption; the focused/selected tile gets a thick blue border and a lighter background. A tile reading "no signal" means the recording or channel behind it could not be read (document closed, channel changed) — not that the event is empty. Medium and Large tiles also draw the fitted sub-state levels (when a CUSUM fit is stored) as thin bright-green bars at each level's own current — the same ink as the trace and the inspector; Small tiles skip them deliberately.

controls.label: Click a tile
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Focuses that event: it becomes the selection here and the rest of the app follows — the event table highlights the row and the trace view moves to it.
controls.notes: Opening the gallery automatically focuses the first tile, which also drives the main window's selection to that event.

controls.label: Double-click a tile
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Goes to that event in the trace: the main window zooms its trace onto the event and comes to the front, in front of the gallery.
controls.notes: Double-click does NOT accept or reject — it used to, and was changed precisely because a destructive action on the open-things gesture was wrong. Rejecting is a click plus R (or the button). Expect the gallery to be covered by the main window afterwards.

controls.label: Drag a rubber band over tiles
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Sweep a box across the grid on empty space to select every tile it touches — the fast way to grab a whole block of bad detections before pressing R.
controls.notes: Ctrl-click adds/removes single tiles and Shift-click extends a range. Selection is per page: turning the page abandons the selection.

controls.label: A
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Accept every selected tile — the keyboard twin of the "Accept selected" button.
controls.notes: Plain letter key, no modifier; works anywhere in this window. Silent no-op if nothing is selected. Same guard as the button: a selected tile the detector flagged as not measurable stays rejected, and the status line says how many were kept rejected.

controls.label: R
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Reject every selected tile — the keyboard twin of "Reject selected", and the key the status line tells you to use.
controls.notes: Plain letter key, no modifier. Silent no-op if nothing is selected.
controls.correction: Same: constructor text "Reject all shown", rewritten by _sync_controls to f"Reject all {subset}" — e.g. "Reject all 412". The "shown" wording never appears once a detection is loaded.

controls.label: Space
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Flips the selection's accept/reject state in one press.
controls.notes: It is NOT a per-tile toggle on a mixed selection: if ANY selected tile is currently accepted, the whole selection becomes REJECTED. Only when every selected tile is already rejected does Space accept them. That bias is deliberate (the gallery is used to cull), but it will surprise you on a mixed sweep.

controls.label: PgDn / PgUp
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Turn to the next / previous page of tiles, same as the ▶ and ◀ buttons.
controls.notes: Clamps at the ends rather than emptying the grid.

controls.label: Home / End
controls.group: Mouse and keyboard in the grid
controls.what_it_does: Jump to the first / last page of the current subset.
controls.notes: In this window Home means "first page" — not "reset zoom", which is what Home does in the main window. The left/right arrow keys move the tile cursor within the page; despite what the ◀ / ▶ tooltips say, they do not turn the page.

controls.what_it_does: "First page (Home)" — jumps to the start of the current filtered, sorted subset.
controls.notes: Greyed out while you are already on page 1.

controls.what_it_does: "Previous page (PgUp, or ←)" — steps back one screenful of tiles.
controls.notes: Greyed out on page 1. The tooltip mentions ←, but only PgUp is actually bound; the arrow keys move the tile cursor inside the page.

controls.label: (page number)
controls.what_it_does: "Jump to a page." Type or spin a page number to go straight there.
controls.notes: 1-based, and its maximum is the current page count — which changes whenever you change Show, Per page, tile size, or resize the window under "Fit".

controls.label: of 1
controls.what_it_does: Reads "of N" — how many pages the current filter subset comes to at the current page size.
controls.notes: Display only. Shows "of 1" when there is no detection or the subset fits on one page.
controls.correction: QLabel("of 1") is only the initial value; _sync_controls sets it to f"of {n_pages}", so it reads "of 1", "of 42", etc. depending on the page count. Documenting it as the fixed string "of 1" is wrong.

controls.what_it_does: "Next page (PgDn, or →)" — advances one screenful of tiles.
controls.notes: Greyed out on the last page. As with ◀, the → in the tooltip is not actually bound.

controls.what_it_does: "Last page (End)" — jumps to the end of the current subset.
controls.notes: Greyed out while you are already on the last page.

controls.label: Per page
controls.what_it_does: "Tiles per page. \"Fit\" sizes the page to the window, so a page is exactly one screenful and turning the page is the only way to move." Options are "Fit" (default), "24", "48", "96" and "200".
controls.notes: Changing this keeps you looking at roughly the same tile — the first tile of your current page stays on screen — rather than keeping the same page NUMBER and dumping you somewhere else in the recording.

controls.label: Fit
controls.what_it_does: Computes the tile count from the window size, so one page is exactly one screenful and there is never anything below the fold. Default.
controls.notes: No scrollbar ever appears in this mode — that is the point. Resizing the window (or changing Tiles size) immediately re-paginates.

controls.what_it_does: A fixed 24 tiles per page regardless of window size.
controls.notes: With any explicit size, a vertical scrollbar appears if the tiles do not fit the window — it exists so events cannot become silently unreachable.

controls.what_it_does: A fixed 48 tiles per page.
controls.notes: Same scrollbar caveat as the other explicit sizes.

controls.what_it_does: A fixed 96 tiles per page.
controls.notes: Same scrollbar caveat as the other explicit sizes.

controls.what_it_does: A fixed 200 tiles per page — few page turns, lots of scrolling.
controls.notes: On a small window this will overflow; scroll the grid to reach the rest of the page.

controls.label: (status line)
controls.what_it_does: Reads e.g. "49–96 of 412 (all)   ·   380 of 412 accepted   ·   drawn from: calibrated (as recorded)   ·   select in bulk: drag a box or shift-click for a run, ⌘-click to add or drop one, ⌘A all on the page, Esc none, ⌘I inverse   ·   click to select, R to reject — each acts on every selected tile   ·   no labels defined — define some under Analysis ▸ Event labels… to arm the digit keys   ·   double-click opens it in the Event Inspector   ·   right-click for the inspector, the trace, or accept/reject": which slice of the subset is on screen, how much of the whole detection is currently accepted, which trace the tiles were drawn from, and the gestures that matter — including the right-click menu, which is where "go to it on the trace" and the per-tile accept/reject live. THE DIGIT HINT NAMES ONLY THE KEYS THE PALETTE ARMS: with labels defined the two clauses collapse into one, "click to select, R to reject, 1–3 to label" (a run of digits reads as a span, a gap as a list "1, 3", a single palette entry as "1"); the line advertised nine digits unconditionally, on sessions whose palette armed none of them. A subpopulation filter or a representative sample adds its own clause, and after a refused accept a "N tiles kept rejected: flagged by the detector as not measurable" clause sits before the hints.
controls.notes: Two empty states, not one: a run that found nothing reads "Detection found no events — nothing to show in the gallery." (the Event inspector's wording, deliberately — the same result must not be described in two ways), and no detection at all reads "No detection — run detection to fill the gallery." The "N of M accepted" figure is always for the WHOLE detection, not the filtered subset, so it is the number to watch while culling.

controls.label: Accept all shown
controls.what_it_does: Marks every event in the current filter accepted — across ALL pages, not just the page you can see. Its label changes to show what it will really do: "Accept all 412" when it would accept them all, "Accept 313 of 317" when the detector's own rejections make the number smaller.
controls.notes: Tooltip: "Mark every tile in the CURRENT filter accepted — not the whole detection unless the filter is All. Tiles the detector flagged as unmeasurable (clipped by the boundary, over the dwell limit, measured from a non-finite sample) stay rejected; the status line counts them." When the shortfall is real the tooltip is prefixed with "4 of the 317 tiles shown are flagged by the detector as not measurable … They stay rejected, so this accepts 313." It reads "Accept all shown" only until a detection is loaded. No confirmation dialog — Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z) in the main window walks it back, recorded as "Accept all events" when the filter covered the whole detection and as "Curate N events" when it did not. Disabled while the grid is empty.
controls.correction: "Accept all shown" is only the constructor text. _sync_accept_all_button rewrites it on every refresh: f"Accept all {subset}" when every shown tile is acceptable, f"Accept {acceptable} of {subset}" otherwise. "Accept all shown" is visible only when no detection is loaded, and the button is disabled then.

controls.label: Reject all shown
controls.what_it_does: Marks every event in the current filter rejected — across all pages. Its label changes to show the count, e.g. "Reject all 412".
controls.notes: Tooltip: "Mark every tile in the current filter rejected." Destructive to your curation and applied with no confirmation; recovery is Edit ▸ Undo in the main window (recorded as "Reject all events"). With Show = "All" this empties your accepted set entirely, which also re-locks the surfaces that need at least one accepted event (e.g. Event plots). Disabled while the grid is empty.
controls.correction: Same: constructor text "Reject all shown", rewritten by _sync_controls to f"Reject all {subset}" — e.g. "Reject all 412". The "shown" wording never appears once a detection is loaded.

controls.label: Ctrl-click / Shift-click a tile
controls.what_it_does: Adds to or extends the tile selection without clearing it — the grid is set to ExtendedSelection (view.setSelectionMode(QAbstractItemView.ExtendedSelection)), so Ctrl-click toggles one tile in or out of the selection and Shift-click selects the whole run from the current tile. The app itself advertises this in the Accept selected tooltip: "Mark every selected tile accepted (drag a box, or Ctrl/Shift-click, to select)." Without it the user only has plain click (one tile) and rubber-band drag.

Advertised but NOT bound — a manual must not promise these. The Previous/Next page tooltips read "Previous page (PgUp, or ←)" and "Next page (PgDn, or →)", but the shortcut table in _build_ui only registers A, R, Space, PageDown, PageUp, Home and End; there is no Key_Left/Key_Right action and no keyPressEvent override. In the tile grid the arrow keys do QListView's own thing — move the focused tile within the current page (which fires eventSelected) — they do not turn the page.

controls.label: (vertical scrollbar on the tile grid)
controls.what_it_does: Appears down the right of the tile grid only when the chosen "Per page" count does not fit the window (policy is ScrollBarAsNeeded); horizontal scrolling is switched off permanently (ScrollBarAlwaysOff). Under the default "Fit" page size the page is computed from the viewport, so the scrollbar never appears — it exists as a safety valve for the fixed sizes 24/48/96/200, where a big count in a small window would otherwise put tiles out of reach.

controls.label: No detection — run detection to fill the gallery.
controls.what_it_does: The empty state of the status line: shown instead of the usual counts whenever no detection has been handed to the window. In this state all four curation buttons are disabled and the two "all" buttons keep their literal startup text ("Accept all shown" / "Reject all shown"). Note the four curation buttons (Accept selected, Reject selected, Accept all…, Reject all…) are enabled only while the CURRENT PAGE has at least one tile — _sync_controls gates them on rowCount() > 0, i.e. tiles on this page, not events in the detection.

controls.label: NanoScope — Event gallery
controls.what_it_does: The title bar of the gallery, which is a standalone top-level window (940×700 on first open), not a dock or tab inside the main window. Useful for the manual because the user has to find this window again among the others.

controls.label: Right-click a tile (context menu)
controls.what_it_does: Per-tile menu: 'Open in Event Inspector' (opens the inspector ON this event — the table row and trace zoom land with it), 'Go to event in trace' (same as double-click), and 'Accept'/'Reject' for just this tile.
controls.notes: 'Open in Event Inspector' selects through the Analysis panel — the same relay as a table-row click — so the inspector, the table and the trace all agree about which event is being looked at.

controls.label: Neighbour spans (tile shading)
controls.what_it_does: Each tile shades its OWN event at full strength and every other ACCEPTED event inside the padded window at half strength — so a fragmented detection reads the same here as on the main trace.
controls.notes: Before this, the sibling dip of a fractured event sat bare in the tile while the main panel shaded it, and the tile looked like a missed detection. Rejected neighbours stay unshaded, exactly as they are on the trace.

controls.label: 'page taller than the window — scroll for the rest' (status hint)
controls.what_it_does: Appears in the status line whenever the current page holds more tiles than one screenful.
controls.notes: A FIXED page size (e.g. 96) can overflow the window, and macOS overlay scrollbars are invisible until you scroll — so the count in '1–96 of 982' used to look wrong when only ~40 tiles were in view. 'Fit' page size never overflows, so under it the hint never appears.

area: Distributions, descriptive comparisons, appearance and publication figures
summary: The Analysis Explorer hosts Distributions, Distribution summaries and Comparison figures alongside recording-level pages. Distributions offers histograms, scatter, KDE, PCA and clustering from stored event or manual-measurement sources; sources are separately identified, not silently pooled. Optional descriptive pages provide ECDF, uncensored empirical survival, box/violin, facets, pair matrices and strip/swarm comparisons. The common Data → Analysis → Appearance → Export structure separates numerical actions from styling. Figure Library stores named frozen numerical/appearance snapshots, supports multi-panel composition, and exports images or reproducible bundles. Current describes source/settings agreement, not scientific validity.
opened_by: Analysis → Distributions… / Distribution summaries… / Comparison figures…, or the corresponding Analysis home entry. Save to Figure Library… and Save figure bundle… are on the Explorer; Figure Library… is also in Analysis. Sources: nanoscope/gui/analysis_explorer.py, plots_panel.py, distribution_summary_panel.py, comparison_figures_panel.py, plot_appearance.py, source_appearance.py, plot_export_options.py, figure_library.py and figure_composer.py.
gotchas: A generated plot is a captured result, not a live mirror. Refresh current or the page Refresh re-gathers the relevant live sources; saved snapshots remain frozen. Opening or exporting a stored snapshot does not run scientific analysis.

Ticking or unticking a source silently discards any clustering and PCA result you had computed AND clears any pinned Axis range; toggling 'Use accepted events only' discards the clustering and PCA result but leaves the Axis range pinned. Either way you must press Run clustering / Run PCA again.
'Axis range' only moves the camera; 'Fit range' changes which data the fit actually sees. Using the wrong one is the easiest mistake in this window.

Fit range numbers are typed in the unit the axis is showing: whatever the Time unit combo shows for a time column (ms by default), and the column's own unit otherwise — pA for depth_pA, dimensionless for frac_depth. Never raw seconds unless Time unit is "s".

Time unit rescales displayed coordinates and axis text for time-valued quantities; source data and fitted scientific quantities remain stored in seconds. Custom axis labels must retain the correct displayed unit and log convention.
With two or more sources ticked, colour means SOURCE: the histogram 'Colour by' is disabled and the scatter 'Colour by = Cluster' is ignored. Untick all but one source to colour by cluster.
Clustering and PCA always run on the PRIMARY (first ticked) source only, never on the overlay as a whole.

Fits refuse to run on fewer than 20 events (20 per component), and the refusal only appears as 'Fit unavailable: …' in Details — the histogram still draws, so it is easy to miss that no curve was fitted.

'gaussian-mixture' is for amplitude/depth-like columns and 'exponential'/'gamma'/'inverse-gaussian'/'exponential + gamma' are for dwell-like columns; the combo will happily let you fit the wrong family to the wrong column.
BIC/AIC values only compare between fits over the SAME data and the SAME truncation — change Fit range, the source, or the accepted-only filter and the numbers are no longer comparable.

Absolute current/charge comparisons require compatible source units, verified calibration and defensible references. Read Details for signal-domain and baseline-fingerprint differences. Dimensionless fractional depth is not automatically comparable when offsets, references or pore context differ.

When the histogram is split by cluster, the fitted curve is fitted over the WHOLE source, not per cluster — the cluster labels come from a multi-feature clustering, not from a mixture model of that one column.
'Use accepted events only' is greyed out for tables with no 'accepted' column (e.g. hand measurements), so 'accepted-only' silently does not apply to those sources.
'include filter-limited events' stays disabled until a fit is selected AND a ticked source carries the filter_limited flag, and it changes the FIT only — never which bars are drawn.
Highlighting a row in the source list does nothing; you must click its checkbox.
Log x drops non-positive values and log y drops non-positive counts/values — if everything is dropped you get an empty plot with a message rather than an error.

Plot t_start_s (or t_end_s) from two sources and Details says the axis carries two origins — it names each recording's t₀, flags any source that is a segment rebased onto its own start, and states that two points at the same x are not simultaneous — because the column is seconds from EACH recording's own first loaded sample, so one physical event can sit at two x positions on what looks like a single timeline.

Appearance edits (titles, fonts, colors, lines, legends) do not rerun fits, detection or clustering and do not reset the view range. Data/analysis controls remain distinct; Apply fit and Generate are explicit scientific actions.

Warnings and scientific caveats belong in the persistent summary, expandable Details and provenance, not alongside the exported plotting artwork. Keep details with the figure bundle when sharing a clean figure.
An unapplied draft and the visible generated result can differ. Save/export captures the visible committed result, not a promise to run the draft. Verify status and Details before final export.

Single/double-column dimensions are convenient 85/180 mm presets, not certification of a journal standard. Print-readability targets are user preferences and cannot certify unmeasured graphical elements.

controls.label: Data sources
controls.what_it_does: A checkable list of everything you can plot: "Every open recording (segments included) that has a stored detection, plus the manual-measurement table." Tick one to plot it; tick two or more to overlay them.
controls.notes: Each row is inked in that source's own overlay colour, so the list doubles as the legend key. Hovering a row shows its row count, whether it is a derived segment, its module id and its detector's min_dwell_s (or "no detector provenance (hand measurements)" for the manual table). Merely HIGHLIGHTING a row does nothing — you must tick the checkbox. The hint above the list reads: "Tick two or more to overlay them. Colour then means SOURCE, and the histogram normalizes so unequal-n recordings stay comparable." Changing the ticks throws away any clustering/PCA result and clears any pinned Axis range, because the row set changed underneath them. With an overlay the column pickers show only the columns ALL ticked sources share (the intersection). The FIRST ticked source is the "primary" one — clustering and PCA operate on it alone. Each row is also EDITABLE: double-click one and type to rename that series everywhere it is named — the legend, the fit lines, the Details pane and the plot title. The source's real label is kept underneath, so clearing the edit back to empty removes the override and the true name comes back rather than the legend going blank. The rename is a display override only; it changes nothing about the data or the fits.

controls.label: Use accepted events only
controls.what_it_does: Plots only the events you kept during curation, dropping the rejected ones from every histogram, scatter, fit, clustering and PCA.
controls.notes: On by default. Disabled (greyed) unless at least one ticked source actually carries an 'accepted' column — the manual-measurement table typically does not. Toggling it discards any existing clustering/PCA result, since the row set changed.

controls.label: Refresh
controls.what_it_does: "Re-pull the current measurements and events." Takes a fresh snapshot of the app's tables so newly detected events or newly saved measurements appear here.
controls.notes: The window is a deliberate snapshot, not a live view — nothing you do in the main window shows up here until you press this. Sources still present after a refresh keep their ticked state, but any clustering/PCA you had run is dropped.

controls.label: Histogram
controls.what_it_does: Plot type: one numeric column as a binned distribution, with optional fitted curve. Selecting it swaps the control page below to the histogram controls.
controls.notes: The plot-type combo is the first (unlabelled) control in the Plot box; its four entries are Histogram / Scatter / KDE (density) / PCA. Switching plot type clears any pinned Axis range (the new plot has different axes).
controls.correction: These are the four ITEMS of ONE unlabelled QComboBox at the top of the "Plot" group: self._plot_type_combo.addItems(list(_PLOT_TYPES)) where _PLOT_TYPES = ("Histogram", "Scatter", "KDE (density)", "PCA"). Picking an item swaps the QStackedWidget of controls underneath it, and also clears any pinned Axis range (a different plot has different axes). A user hunting for four separate combos will not find them.

controls.label: Scatter
controls.what_it_does: Plot type: any two numeric columns as an X-Y point cloud, optionally coloured by cluster and with a best-fit line.
controls.notes: Same combo as Histogram / KDE (density) / PCA. Switching plot type clears any pinned Axis range.
