controls.label: Time unit
controls.what_it_does: Choose seconds, milliseconds or microseconds for displayed time coordinates and labels.
controls.notes: Stored data and fitted scientific values remain in seconds. Fit range and Axis range entries follow the displayed axis units; changing Time unit is not changing event duration.

controls.label: Column
controls.what_it_does: Which numeric column to histogram.
controls.notes: Only numeric, non-boolean columns that have at least one finite value are offered — flags like accepted / filter_limited never appear. Seeds itself to a dwell-like column (dwell_s, dwell, rise_s, fall_s) when one exists. With several sources ticked, only columns they all share are listed.

controls.label: Bins
controls.what_it_does: Number of histogram bins (2 to 500, default 30).
controls.notes: With an overlay, ONE set of bin edges is computed over the union of every drawn source and reused for all of them, so the shapes are measured against the same ruler.

controls.label: Normalize
controls.what_it_does: "What the y axis counts. count: raw events per bin — only comparable at equal n. density: counts / (n × bin width) — the shape, independent of how long each recording ran. THE one to use when overlaying. The heights are per unit of the column IN ITS STORED UNIT (per second for a dwell, per pA for a depth), which is what the y axis says; they integrate to 1 over that unit — not over a ms/µs tick scale, and not over a log axis. probability per bin: counts / n — bin heights sum to 1." The three entries are literally "count", "density" and "probability per bin".
controls.notes: Auto-switches to "density" the moment you tick a second source (and back to "count" when you are down to one) — but only until you pick a value yourself; after that your choice is pinned and the automatic switch stops. The fitted curve is rescaled to match whichever quantity is shown. Renamed from "density (area = 1)" by report S6-03: the heights are per the column's STORED unit while the x ticks follow the Time-unit combo, so the area under the DRAWN curve was 1000 on the default ms axis and ~23 on a log-x one. The y axis now names the unit ("density (1/s)", "density (1/pA)") and the Details pane says where the drawn area is not 1. A sidecar or template written before the rename still opens and still selects density.

controls.label: Colour by
controls.what_it_does: "Split the histogram by cluster label after Run clustering — the other half of the clustering workflow (scatter/PCA already colour by cluster)." Entries: None, Cluster.
controls.notes: Single source only. With two or more sources ticked it is DISABLED, reset to None, and its tooltip changes to "Colour already means SOURCE while more than one source is drawn — untick all but one to split by cluster instead." Choosing Cluster does nothing until you press Run clustering. When split, every cluster is normalized against the same total (they are parts of one distribution), rows the clustering dropped appear as a grey "dropped (non-finite features)" series, and any fitted curve is fitted over the WHOLE source, not per cluster — the window says so in Details.

controls.label: Log x
controls.what_it_does: Log-scale the value axis and use log-spaced bins — the usual way to look at a dwell-time distribution spanning decades.
controls.notes: Non-positive values cannot be drawn and are dropped, with the count reported in Details. The Time unit rescale applies on a log axis as well: the label reads e.g. "dwell (ms, log)" and the tick values are in that unit. Only decades get tick labels (minor ticks stay unlabelled) so the axis does not smear.

controls.label: Log y (count)
controls.what_it_does: "Log-scale the count axis — makes an exponential tail read as a line."
controls.notes: On a log count axis the bars lose their fill and draw as a step outline only (a fill baseline would be log(0)); empty bins therefore read as gaps.

controls.label: Fit
controls.what_it_does: Overlays a fitted distribution on the histogram and prints its parameters in the title, the legend and Details. Tooltip: "exponential: the classic escape model — monotonic, cannot peak. gamma / inverse-gaussian: densities WITH a mode, for a dwell histogram that peaks away from zero. All three are truncated at the detector's min_dwell_s, so their BIC values compare directly." The six entries, verbatim, are: none / exponential / gamma (peaked) / inverse-gaussian (first passage) / exponential + gamma (bimodal) / gaussian-mixture.
controls.notes: SELECTING A FAMILY DOES NOT DRAW IT — press "Apply fit" beside the combo; until you do, the button reads "Apply fit ●" and the plot still shows the previous fit (or none). WHEN TO PICK WHAT — "none": no overlay (default). "exponential": the classic first-order escape model for a dwell column; monotonically decreasing, so it can never describe a histogram that peaks away from zero; reports τ. "gamma (peaked)": a dwell density that HAS a mode — use it when the dwell histogram rises to a peak before falling; reports k. "inverse-gaussian (first passage)": the other peaked dwell family, the first-passage-time model; reports μ. "exponential + gamma (bimodal)": a fast escape AND a slow peaked passage in one model — for a bimodal dwell distribution whose slow lobe has a mode, which none of the single families can express; reports k. "gaussian-mixture": for an amplitude/depth-like column (frac_depth, depth_pA, max_dev_pA, mean_dev_pA), not for dwell; reports μ per component and fits |value| (negatives are fit by magnitude, and the count is reported). The four dwell families are all truncated at the same detector floor, so their BIC values in Details compare directly; the mixture is a different kind of animal and is not comparable with them. Choosing anything but "none" enables Fit components and (if a source carries the flag) 'include filter-limited events'. Fits refuse to run on fewer than 20 events (20 × components for a multi-component fit) — the refusal is printed as "Fit unavailable: …" in Details and the histogram still stands. If a rival component count beats the current one by more than 10 BIC, Details prints "NOTE: N components fit markedly better …; set Fit components = N to see it."

controls.label: Apply fit
controls.what_it_does: Draws the family chosen in the Fit combo beside it. Choosing a family is a PROPOSAL; this button is what makes it the drawn fit.
controls.notes: It exists because picking from the combo used to fit, draw and start the advisory batch on the spot, so walking down the list merely to READ the options ran five maximisations — one of them (exponential + gamma) a nine-second twelve-start optimisation. While a chosen family has not been applied the button reads "Apply fit ●", so a plot never silently disagrees with the combo above it. The same gate is on the Scatter page, and on the Voltage-dependence window's own Fit combo.

controls.label: Fit components
controls.what_it_does: "Number of mixture components for the fit." 1 to 4, default 1.
controls.notes: Disabled until Fit is set to anything other than "none", and disabled again while the "Auto (BIC)" box beside it is ticked — that box is itself only enabled for "exponential" and "gaussian-mixture", the two families with a component count, and it writes the k it chose back into the spin so the number on screen is the one that was fitted. Each extra component needs another 20 events or the fit refuses. Details always prints "BIC = … AIC = … components = …" so you can judge whether the extra component earned its place.

controls.label: Fit range
controls.what_it_does: Two text boxes (placeholders "min" and "max") that restrict the fit to part of the distribution: "Fit only this part of the distribution, in the AXIS unit shown. This is a TRUNCATION, not a crop: the likelihood is renormalised to the range, so restricting to a peak does not bias the estimates the way silently dropping data would. BIC is only comparable between fits over the SAME range."
controls.notes: This changes WHICH DATA THE FIT SEES — it is not the same thing as the Axis range box below, which only moves the camera. Values are typed in the unit the axis is currently showing (ms by default for a dwell column), and are converted back internally. Takes effect when you leave the field (editing finished). Leave both blank for the full range; a min ≥ max is ignored. The window's own detection floor and your range are intersected, and Details prints the INTERSECTION — not the pair you typed — to 12 significant figures, in the same unit as the fitted parameters above it: "FIT RANGE [lo, hi] unit — n = … of the available events; the likelihood is TRUNCATED to this window, not merely cropped. BIC/AIC compare only against fits over the SAME range." When the intersection differs from what you typed the line adds "Your typed range was [lo, hi] unit; it was intersected with what this source's detector could report, and the intersection above is what was fitted." Only the four dwell families condition their likelihood on the window; for "gaussian-mixture" the middle clause reads instead "the sample is CROPPED to this window — this family does not renormalise its likelihood to it, so the estimates are those of a distribution fitted to the surviving values, not of one conditioned on the window."
controls.correction: Not a list. form.addRow("Fit range", fit_range) where fit_range is a QHBoxLayout holding TWO QLineEdits, self._fit_lo (placeholder "min") and self._fit_hi (placeholder "max"). Both commit on editingFinished.

controls.label: include filter-limited events
controls.what_it_does: "Off (default): events whose dwell is within ~2x the filter rise time are excluded from the fit (depth attenuated, dwell biased long) and the count is reported in Details. On: they are fit alongside the resolved events."
controls.notes: Off by default, matching the Fits panel. Disabled unless BOTH a fit is selected (Fit ≠ none) AND at least one ticked source carries a 'filter_limited' column. It affects the FIT only, not which bars are drawn.

controls.label: X
controls.what_it_does: Numeric column on the horizontal axis.
controls.notes: Seeded to a dwell-like column when one exists. With an overlay, only columns every ticked source carries are offered.
controls.correction: Not lists. Four QLineEdits, each with placeholder text "auto" and a QDoubleValidator, built by the loop over (("xmin", "X min"), ("xmax", "X max"), ("ymin", "Y min"), ("ymax", "Y max")) in the "Axis range" group. Pressing Enter/Return in any of them applies the range immediately (returnPressed → _apply_axis_range) — that is the only keyboard shortcut anywhere in this file; there is no setShortcut or QKeySequence in plots_panel.py at all. Blank means auto; a pair is only honoured when BOTH ends of that axis are filled, and non-positive bounds are ignored on a log axis.

The Time unit rescale applies on a log axis as well: the label reads e.g. "dwell (ms, log)" and the tick values are in that unit. If every point is dropped you get "No points to plot for this pair (check the log-axis toggles)."

controls.label: Log y
controls.what_it_does: Log-scale the Y axis.
controls.notes: Points with a non-positive Y are dropped from the plot.

controls.label: Colour by
controls.what_it_does: Colours the points plainly (None) or by cluster label (Cluster), with a legend swatch and count per cluster.

With more than one source ticked it is IGNORED — colour means source there — and Details says "Colour by Cluster is ignored while several sources are overlaid — colour means SOURCE here. Untick all but one source to colour by cluster." Rows the clustering dropped draw grey and are labelled "dropped (non-finite features)".

controls.label: Fit
controls.what_it_does: "Overlay a least-squares best-fit line; power law fits in log-log space." Entries: none / linear / power law (log-log).
controls.notes: SELECTING A FAMILY DOES NOT DRAW IT — press "Apply fit" beside the combo. Pick "linear" for a straight y = m·x + c relationship; pick "power law (log-log)" when you expect y ∝ x^n (the fit is done on the logs, so it needs positive values on both axes). The summary — slope/intercept or coefficient/exponent, the axis units, R² and n — goes into Details and becomes the plot title unless you typed your own. R² is qualified wherever it carries no information: a two-parameter line through two points prints "R² = 1.000 (exact by construction)" and a y that does not vary prints "R² undefined (y does not vary)", each with a full sentence under it in Details. A log-log fit that had to drop points with no logarithm says so — "power-law fit: N of M point(s) have x ≤ 0, y ≤ 0, or a non-finite value …" — and still draws the line over the points it did use. With an overlay each source gets its OWN dashed line in its own colour and its own legend entry; there is never one pooled regression through two clouds. If the fit cannot run (too few points, constant x, no positive values for log-log) Details shows "Fit unavailable: …" and the points still draw.

controls.label: Apply fit
controls.what_it_does: Draws the best-fit line chosen in the Fit combo beside it. As on the histogram page, the combo is a proposal and this button is what draws it.
controls.notes: Cheaper per fit than the histogram's, but a regression line that appears the instant the combo is opened is the same surprise, and one gate that behaves the same way on both pages is one rule. Reads "Apply fit ●" while a chosen family is not yet drawn.

Pressing it also switches the plot type to PCA. Features are z-scored first. Changing the feature selection invalidates the result and you must run it again.

controls.label: Details
controls.what_it_does: A read-only monospaced pane under the plot that carries everything the picture cannot show: n per series, the fitted parameters, BIC/AIC and component count, the detection limit that was used and where it came from, every value that was dropped and why, clustering sizes and per-cluster means, and any caution about comparing recordings.
controls.notes: READ THIS — it is where the fit's honesty lives. Typical lines: "detection limit t_min = … s (from …)"; a warning when overlaid sources were detected at DIFFERENT resolutions ("…Each fit below uses its OWN t_min; the shading marks the shallowest of them."); "no detection limit is known for “col”…" whenever the drawn column carries no detector provenance — and it names the floor the likelihood actually used: "the fit falls back to the shortest observed value (… unit) as t_min" (which biases tau SHORT) when you typed no Fit range min, and "the typed Fit range min (… unit) is the floor t_min the likelihood is conditioned on — nothing was substituted from the data" when you did; "CAUTION — comparing depth_pA, … across recordings: …" when you overlay an absolute-current column (baseline_pA, depth_pA, ecd_pA_s, max_dev_pA, mean_dev_pA, amplitude, rms) across recordings without a shared gain calibration; and "Fit unavailable: …" instead of a silent missing curve. It also carries the FULL source names that the legend abbreviates.
controls.correction: "Details" is a QGroupBox title (QtWidgets.QGroupBox("Details")) wrapping a READ-ONLY QPlainTextEdit in monospace, max height 180 px — not a table. It is where the fit parameters, per-source event counts, the detection limit t_min and its source, cluster sizes/means, the gain-comparability CAUTION line and any warnings are printed.

controls.label: (right-truncation note — who imposed t_max)
controls.what_it_does: The Details line a right-truncated fit prints — "right truncation at t_max=… is MODELLED: … values above it were never reported (…), so the likelihood is conditioned on t_min <= t <= t_max" — whose parenthetical names WHO imposed the bound instead of blaming the detector for all of them: "(detector max_dwell_s)" when the surviving ceiling is the detection's own stored limit, and "(the fit range that was typed, NOT a detector limit)" when it is the Fit range max you typed.
controls.notes: The window decides by comparing the ceiling the fitter actually got with the detection's stored max_dwell_s: equal is the detector's, anything else came from the Fit range box. The dwell wording is used only when the fitted column really is a dwell (dwell_s, dwell, dwell_time_s), so a depth_pA fit bounded by a typed range cannot claim a dwell ceiling the detector never had — that combination raises rather than prints. With no provenance at all the note keeps a hedge instead of a claim: "(detector max_dwell_s, or curation)" on a dwell column, "(a fit range, or curation)" on any other. A third wording, "(curation removed everything above it, NOT a detector limit)", is defined for a ceiling left by curation. It matters because the truncation correction is conditioned on the bound: a typed window printed as a detector limit makes an artefact of your own fit range look like a physical ceiling.

controls.label: Plot area

Legend labels longer than 34 characters are middle-elided with "…" — the full name is in Details. On a dwell histogram the region below the detector's shortest reportable event is shaded grey with a dashed line labelled "below detection limit"; that region is an artefact of the detector, not of the physics.
controls.correction: No such string exists anywhere in plots_panel.py. The plot is an unlabelled pyqtgraph PlotWidget (self._plot_widget, minimum 420×320) in the right-hand splitter; it has no title, no caption and is not a table. It is mouse zoom/pan-able and carries pyqtgraph's own right-click context menu. When there is nothing to draw it shows a centred grey message instead — the exact strings are "No data yet — run detection or add measurements, then Refresh.", "Tick a source on the left — none of the checked ones has rows to plot.", "This source has no rows to plot.", "Pick a numeric column to histogram."

The window switches to this automatically the moment a second source is ticked, unless you have already picked a normalization yourself (picking one from the combo pins your choice permanently). area: Noise spectrum, I-V, voltage dependence, event waveforms and Subpopulations
summary: Analysis Explorer recording-level pages include Noise spectrum (Welch PSD, FFT, spectrogram and all-points histogram), I-V / conductance, Voltage dependence and Event waveforms (event-count heatmap and aligned ensemble). Noise uses a selected raw calibrated recording span, not the detector filter chain. I-V estimates conductance from current/voltage observations; voltage dependence summarizes stored event metrics. Subpopulations is an explicit exploratory waveform-feature/clustering/mixture report, not molecular identification. Open-pore reference controls live in Preprocess and are documented here together with their detailed automatic-estimator probe controls.
opened_by: Analysis → Noise spectrum… / I-V / conductance… / Voltage dependence… / Event waveforms… opens the corresponding Explorer page. Noise spectrum of the measured region transfers the trace selection by sample index. Generate Subpopulations… computes a report; Open saved Subpopulations… reopens it without analysis. Reference controls: Inspector → Analysis → Preprocess → Open-pore baseline. Sources: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py, iv_panel.py, voltage_dep_panel.py, event_plot_panel.py, subpop_window.py, baseline_panel.py and main_window.py.
gotchas: The Noise spectrum page deliberately ignores your filter chain and your detection — it always transforms the RAW calibrated trace, so a spectrum will not match a filtered view of the same recording.

A spectrum is only pore QC if the segment is quiet: leave translocations inside the Start/End window and you are measuring the events, not the pore. That is what the group is called 'Segment (quiet open-pore baseline)'.

'Total RMS noise: 0' is almost never a perfect pore. If every sample in the window is identical the window says so explicitly and tells you to check the Calibration panel's raw-vs-calibrated read-out — a flat channel usually means an unset or wrong gain, a disconnected headstage or a dead ADC channel.

One NaN or inf sample anywhere in the analysed window makes EVERY Welch bin NaN, so the whole spectrum disappears rather than losing one point; the window explains this instead of showing an empty plot.

Overlaid spectra are comparable in SHAPE (α, where the white floor sits, where the capacitive rise starts) but not in absolute height unless the recordings share a real calibration — and if two curves are in different units the y axis is labelled with the PRIMARY's, so their heights are meaningless as drawn. The Noise details NOTE lines say so.
The RMS read-out and the noise summary are always per curve. There is deliberately no combined number for two pores.

In the Noise spectrum page, changing the Source recording re-ranges and RESETS the Start/End segment and the f low/f high band to that recording's full duration and Nyquist — a hand-dialled band does not survive a source change.
Voltage dependence and I-V do not watch the session: detect (or open) another recording and nothing changes until you press that window's own Refresh.
'Accepted only' in Voltage dependence is on by default; turning it off silently changes every metric to include rejected events, so the plot will stop matching your curated tables.

Voltage dependence needs suitable stored event results and known applied voltage for at least two recordings. Do not assume every open recording is eligible; inspect Per recording and Details, including detector/source provenance. Saved results can be reopened without rerunning detection.
The 'Per recording' table lists every gathered point, but the plot may show fewer: log y drops non-positive values, and the details box counts what it dropped.
The Event plots window is a snapshot. Accepting or rejecting events in the inspector, gallery or table does not update the density map or the ensemble until you press Refresh in its toolbar.
'Log x' is ON by default in the density map, so its x-axis values are log10 values and any non-positive events are silently excluded from the binning.
Overriding the density map's X label or Y label removes the automatic '(log10)' hint — a renamed logged axis will not tell the reader it is logged.

Export current figure… exports the selected Event waveforms view. The event-count heatmap counts events; KDE probability density is a different analysis. Save/export never silently generates a new result from unapplied drafts.

With 'Normalize time' ticked (the default) the ensemble x axis is fractions of dwell, not seconds — events of very different durations are drawn the same width. 'Align' only does anything once you untick it.

Increasing ensemble padding can exclude events whose required window extends beyond the loaded trace; edge-skipped counts and other warnings are retained in Details/provenance, not added alongside clean plot artwork.
In the Open-pore baseline panel the buttons are never truly disabled — a dim button still takes the click and answers with the reason. Do not read 'greyed' as 'broken'.
'Base window' cannot be raised above 'Rough window'; if the spin box refuses to go higher, raise the rough window first.
Measuring proposes; it never applies. Nothing changes until you press 'Use these values'.

Confirmed reference settings are scoped to recording/channel. Returning to a stored result restores its recorded reference context; an unrun draft is not a saved analysis result. Check source and mode after switching targets.

There is no universal baseline setting. Automatic 0.5 / 0.1 s windows are defaults for an unseen recording, not a certified physical reference. Inspect the recording, compare candidate estimators, and use known current or demonstrably open intervals only when justified.
Changing the baseline windows after a detection has run does not re-measure the table; use Analysis ▸ Compare baseline estimators… first to see what would change, because it installs nothing.

The "Ranked:" rows judge each window on two numbers and the WORST single state is compared first: a baseline that follows more than 50% of any one state's excursion has ridden INTO that state and loses to any window that stays out, whatever the medians say — on the -600 mV apo file the 1 s / 300 ms window's median intrusion reads exactly 0.0 while its baseline rides into the 521 ms partial clog at t = 37.13 s, which then goes undetected while about thirty shallow events are invented on the collapsed local baseline, every health check green.

When a "Save image…" fails and a file of that name is already in the folder — in any of the five plotting windows — the dialog does not say the file was not created: it names that file as the EARLIER export, gives the date it was last written and warns that it is now older than the figure on screen, because an untouched stale PNG is exactly what a user mistakes for the image they just saved.
A live signal with fluctuations below float32's smallest representable magnitude is reported as a representation limit ("…not a quiet pore"), never as "Total RMS noise: 0".

Manual-reference Preview is noncommitting. To apply the reference press Detect: this can change residual-noise scale, automatic polarity, candidate boundaries and acceptance, not only reported amplitudes. Reviewed-table replacement is explicit and undoable.

Known and interval references require calibrated pA and a supported classical detector. Incompatible high-pass, normalization or runtime baseline-subtraction settings are refused; the application does not silently turn them off.

An automatic result and a known-current/specified-interval result answer different conditional questions. If intervals/current came from synthetic ground truth, disclose that as oracle assistance; it is not evidence available on a real recording.

controls.label: Noise spectrum…
controls.what_it_does: Opens the current-noise power spectrum for a recording's current channel: the log-log PSD that separates 1/f (flicker), the thermal/white floor and the high-frequency dielectric/capacitance rise, plus band-integrated RMS noise. Pore quality control on the RAW calibrated trace — no detection needed.
controls.notes: Disabled until at least one open recording has a live current channel and a known sample rate. Clicking the equivalent greyed launcher button posts the reason: 'Open a recording first — the noise spectrum needs a current channel with a known sample rate (no detection required).' or 'No open recording has a current channel with a known sample rate — the noise spectrum needs both.' Opening it points the window at whatever recording is currently selected in the Files panel.

controls.label: I-V / conductance…
controls.what_it_does: Gather (voltage, open-pore current) from every open recording, fit I vs V, and report the pore CONDUCTANCE (slope, in nS) with the leak and R². The classic pore-characterisation plot across your -1000..-200 mV runs.
controls.notes: Disabled until at least one open recording has BOTH a current channel and a known applied voltage (a live voltage channel, or a voltage in the file's metadata). Locked reason: 'No open recording has both a current channel and a known applied voltage (a voltage channel, or a voltage in the file's metadata).'

controls.label: Voltage dependence…
controls.what_it_does: Plot how an event metric (capture rate, dwell, depth, dI/I₀, count) varies with the applied voltage across your detected recordings, and fit the trend (linear or the A·exp(V/V₀) capture-rate model). The classic nanopore voltage series — batch-detect first, then open this.
controls.notes: Disabled until at least 2 recordings each have a known applied voltage AND a stored threshold (Schmitt) detection — one point is not a trend. The locked reason counts live: 'Needs at least 2 detected recordings with a known applied voltage — N so far. Open the voltage series and run Analysis ▸ Batch detect.'

controls.label: Event waveforms…
controls.what_it_does: The signature translocation plots for the current detection: the 2-D dwell-vs-blockage density map (with ECD / charge-deficit as a metric) and the event-ensemble overlay with its mean and median waveform. Needs at least one accepted event.
controls.notes: Disabled until the ACTIVE detection has at least one accepted event. Four different locked reasons, each naming the first real blocker: nothing open, nothing selected in the Files panel, no detection on the selected recording, or 'No accepted events yet — accept at least one in the Event inspector (or tick it in the event table) to fill the density map and the ensemble.'

controls.label: Compare baseline estimators…
controls.what_it_does: Shows what re-measuring this detection against the configured open-pore estimator would change: old vs new depth per event, the ratio distribution, and how many events have a stamped baseline that moves more than 10 pA. Nothing is re-measured until you say so.
controls.notes: Disabled until there is a stored detection. Refuses with a plain sentence if another analysis is running, if there is no detection, if the recording has no sample rate, or if the open-pore baseline controls are not set ('open the Preprocess tab and choose (or probe for) a window'). Opening the report installs nothing.

controls.label: Start
controls.what_it_does: Start of the analysed segment, in seconds.
controls.notes: Ranges over 0 … the primary recording's duration, 4 decimal places, 0.1 s steps. The group title is the instruction: pick a QUIET open-pore stretch — a segment full of translocations measures the events, not the pore.

controls.label: End
controls.what_it_does: End of the analysed segment, in seconds.
controls.notes: Same range and step as Start. A window holding fewer than 2 samples draws a message instead of a spectrum, naming the sample count.

controls.label: Use full trace
controls.what_it_does: Reset the segment to span the whole recording.
controls.notes: Sets Start to 0 and End to the recording's duration, then recomputes.

controls.label: (segment read-out, e.g. '3,000,000 samples · 60 s')
controls.what_it_does: Says how many samples the analysed window actually holds and how long it is, so you can see whether the window is long enough for the Welch segment length you chose.
controls.notes: Blank until a spectrum computes; blank again whenever the plot shows a message instead of a curve.

controls.label: Segment length
controls.what_it_does: Welch segment length (FFT size). Auto balances variance vs frequency resolution (≈8+ averaged segments). Longer = finer low-frequency detail.
controls.notes: Choices: Auto, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536. A value larger than the selected window is clipped to the window. The value actually used, the overlap, and the number of averaged segments are printed in Noise details.

controls.label: Window
controls.what_it_does: Taper applied to each segment before the FFT.
controls.notes: Choices: hann (the default), hamming, blackman, bartlett, blackmanharris, flattop, boxcar.

controls.label: Overlap
controls.what_it_does: Overlap between consecutive segments, as a percentage.
controls.notes: 0–95 %, default 50 %. More overlap averages more segments (smoother spectrum) out of the same data.

controls.label: Log-log axes
controls.what_it_does: Plot log10(PSD) vs log10(f) — the standard noise view.
controls.notes: On by default. Only redraws; it never re-runs the transform. On a log axis non-positive points are dropped, so an all-zero (flat) channel plots nothing — the window says so explicitly rather than blaming this toggle.

controls.label: Amplitude spectral density (√PSD)
controls.what_it_does: Plot the ASD √PSD in units/√Hz instead of the PSD in units²/Hz.
controls.notes: Off by default. Changes only the drawn quantity and the y-axis label (and the auto title's 'PSD'/'ASD' prefix); the numbers in Noise details stay in PSD units.

controls.label: f low
controls.what_it_does: Low edge of the RMS-noise integration band, in Hz.
controls.notes: Ranges 0 … the primary's Nyquist; defaults to 0 so the read-out starts as the TOTAL RMS. Changing it only re-integrates the stored spectrum — no recompute.

controls.label: f high
controls.what_it_does: High edge of the RMS-noise integration band, in Hz.
controls.notes: Defaults to the primary recording's Nyquist. Re-ranged whenever the primary Source changes.

controls.label: RMS in band
controls.what_it_does: The RMS current noise integrated over the chosen band, with the band restated in brackets — the single number you quote as 'this pore's noise'.
controls.notes: Shows '—' before anything is computed. With an overlay up it lists one line per curve, each in its OWN units — the values are never merged into one figure. A band that cannot be integrated reads 'unavailable', never 0.

controls.label: Title
controls.what_it_does: Override the plot title; blank uses the automatic title.
controls.notes: The automatic title is 'PSD — <recording>' (or 'ASD — …'), and with several curves it names every recording, e.g. 'PSD — A vs B', counting the rest past three.

controls.label: Data colour
controls.what_it_does: Colour of the spectrum curve. Clicking opens a colour picker; the button shows the chosen hex code on that colour.
controls.notes: Default #0072B2. Applies to the PRIMARY curve only — comparison curves keep their own assigned colours.

controls.label: Fit colour
controls.what_it_does: Colour of the fitted 1/f line. Clicking opens a colour picker.
controls.notes: Default #D55E00.

controls.label: Background
controls.what_it_does: Light gives a white canvas with dark ink for publication.
controls.notes: Choices: Dark (default), Light. Affects the exported PNG too.

controls.label: Export size
controls.what_it_does: Saved-PNG size in px (0 = native / follow aspect). Two boxes, width × height.
controls.notes: 0–20000 each. Setting only one keeps the aspect ratio; setting both forces exactly that size.

controls.label: Export current figure…
controls.what_it_does: Export the visible committed figure through the shared publication export dialog.
controls.notes: Choose native/physical dimensions and inspect the frozen preview; warning details stay in their own section and metadata. Export does not run a new analysis.

controls.label: Noise details
controls.what_it_does: The full noise report for the spectrum on screen: Total RMS noise; a Band RMS breakdown over <1 kHz, 1-10 kHz and 10 kHz-Nyquist; the White floor (median PSD over the mid decade, in units²/Hz, with the decade stated); the 1/f exponent α with its 1 Hz magnitude, R² and the fit band; and the acquisition line fs / Nyquist / Δf plus the Welch settings actually used (nperseg, noverlap, segments, window).
controls.notes: One block per curve, headed by the recording name, never merged. It prints 'unavailable' rather than a number when a quantity cannot be measured, and appends NOTE lines: a clipped time window, a curve that could not be computed, a recording that declares no units for its current channel (every magnitude in the block then reads '(units unknown)' and the NOTE says to set the units in Calibration), curves in DIFFERENT units (their heights are not comparable as drawn), and a CAUTION when the recordings' gains are not comparable — spectrum SHAPE is still comparable, absolute magnitude is not. If the whole spectrum is non-finite it explains that one NaN sample poisons every Welch bin, and names the channel's own calibration issues.

controls.label: Refresh
controls.what_it_does: Re-gather (V, I₀) from every open recording — pick up any opened since.
controls.notes: The window holds no other data controls: everything is read straight from the open documents.

controls.label: Export current figure…
controls.what_it_does: Export the visible committed figure through the shared publication export dialog.
controls.notes: Choose native/physical dimensions and inspect the frozen preview; warning details stay in their own section and metadata. Export does not run a new analysis.

controls.label: (conductance headline, e.g. 'G = 12.4 nS')
controls.what_it_does: The headline result — the pore conductance from the fitted slope, restated as the plot title alongside R².
controls.notes: Falls back to a slope in current-units per volt when a conductance cannot be named. Blank when there is nothing to fit.

controls.label: Fit details
controls.what_it_does: The fitted line, the leak/intercept, R² and how many recordings went into it.
controls.notes: Also where the 'Saved image → …' confirmation appears.

controls.label: Points:
controls.what_it_does: The list under Fit details naming every gathered (V, I₀) point — "  <recording>:  V = -600 mV,  I₀ = -34.79 (units unknown)  [measured]" — with "  — DROPPED, not in the fit" on any recording whose current units this window cannot convert. Recordings whose VOLTAGE units are undeclared are listed separately under "Excluded — voltage units undeclared (set them in Calibration):", each line carrying its own reason.
controls.notes: A dropped recording is still listed, because otherwise "I-V over N recording(s)" counts something the reader cannot see. When the drops leave a single usable point the details say what really happened instead of asking for another file: "Only one recording reached the fit: 3 of the 4 recordings with a (V, I₀) point were dropped for current units this window cannot convert — <names and their unit strings>. Declare their units in Calibration (pA / nA / uA / A), or open another recording at a different voltage." The plain "Only one recording — open another at a different voltage to fit a conductance." survives for the case where nothing was dropped.

controls.label: Metric
controls.what_it_does: Which per-recording event summary to plot against voltage.
controls.notes: Choices, in order: 'Capture rate (Hz)' (the default), 'Median dwell (s)', 'Median depth (pA)', 'Median dI/I₀', 'Event count'. Changing it re-gathers every point from the session and relabels the y axis and the table's third column.

controls.label: Fit
controls.what_it_does: Overlay a trend: a straight line, or the A·exp(V/V0) capture-rate model. "Press Apply fit to draw the one you have chosen." (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: SELECTING A TREND DOES NOT DRAW IT — press "Apply fit" beside the combo. Choices: none (default), linear, exponential. The fit runs on whatever x axis is currently drawn (|V| or signed V), so the curve always lands on the scatter. With fewer than 2 recordings the details box says 'Need >= 2 recordings at different voltages to fit a trend.'

controls.label: Apply fit
controls.what_it_does: Draws the trend chosen in the Fit combo beside it. The combo is a proposal; this is what puts the line on the plot.
controls.notes: Reads "Apply fit ●" while a chosen trend has not been drawn yet. The same gate the Plots window's histogram and scatter Fit combos carry, and it matters more here: every point is a whole recording, so a trend line that appeared the instant the dropdown opened would be a model asserted over the user's points before they asked for it.

controls.label: |V|
controls.what_it_does: Plot against the voltage MAGNITUDE |V| instead of signed V.
controls.notes: Off by default. It changes what the fit is fitted to as well as what is drawn — the reported slope or V₀ is in terms of whichever axis is showing, and the details line says which ('· |V|' vs '· V').

controls.label: Log y
controls.what_it_does: Log-scale the metric axis — an exponential capture rate reads as a line.
controls.notes: Non-positive points are dropped when it is on, and the details box counts them ('N non-positive point(s) dropped for log y.'). If nothing survives, the plot says 'No finite points to plot (check the log-y toggle).'

controls.label: Accepted only
controls.what_it_does: Summarise only the curated-in (accepted) events.
controls.notes: ON by default. Un-ticking it includes rejected events in every recording's metric, so the numbers here will no longer match what the curated event table reports. Toggling it re-gathers all points.

controls.label: (fit headline, e.g. 'V₀ = 0.0821 V' or 'slope = 34.7')
controls.what_it_does: The one number the fit is about, shown at the right of the controls row and repeated with R² as the plot title.
controls.notes: Blank when no fit is selected or none could be made.

controls.label: Refresh
controls.what_it_does: Re-gather (V, metric) from every open recording — pick up any detected since.
controls.notes: This is how a recording you have just batch-detected joins the plot; the window does not watch the session by itself.

controls.label: Export current figure…
controls.what_it_does: Export the visible committed figure through the shared publication export dialog.
controls.notes: Choose native/physical dimensions and inspect the frozen preview; warning details stay in their own section and metadata. Export does not run a new analysis.

controls.label: Fit details
controls.what_it_does: Names the metric and axis and the number of recordings, then spells out the fitted model — 'Exponential: value = A · exp(V / V0)' with A and V₀, or 'Linear: value = slope · V + intercept' — and closes with 'Goodness of fit: R² = … · n = N recording(s)'. Over two recordings that line adds the caveat that R² = 1 is exact by construction (both trends have two free parameters, so any two recordings score the same), and the short form '(exact by construction)' rides with the R² in the plot title. When the metric is identical across the pool the line reads instead 'Goodness of fit: R² undefined — the metric is identical across the pooled recording(s), so a trend explains nothing and no goodness-of-fit exists to report · n = N recording(s)'.
controls.notes: Also carries the log-y drop count and any 'Fit unavailable: …' message.

controls.label: Per recording
controls.what_it_does: One row per gathered recording, sorted by voltage: Recording name, V (mV), and the metric's value. This is where you check which file supplied which point.
controls.notes: Read-only. It lists EVERY gathered point even when the fit dropped some (e.g. non-positive values under log y), so the table can hold more rows than the plot shows points.

controls.label: Event-count heatmap
controls.what_it_does: Bin two event metrics into an event-count heatmap with marginal count histograms.
controls.notes: Counts are not a smoothed KDE probability density. The visible label is Event-count heatmap; Density remains an internal saved-workspace key.

controls.label: Ensemble
controls.what_it_does: Every accepted event resampled onto a common axis and overlaid faintly, with the bold mean (solid) and median (dashed) waveform drawn on top.
controls.notes: Its title line reports how many events were drawn and how many were 'edge-skipped'.

controls.label: Refresh
controls.what_it_does: Re-snapshot the active detection's accepted events.
controls.notes: Lives in the toolbar so both tabs share it. The window holds a snapshot: accepting or rejecting events elsewhere does NOT update these plots until you press this.

controls.label: X
controls.what_it_does: The X-axis event metric for the density map.
controls.notes: Choices: 'Dwell (s)' (default X), 'Depth', 'dI/I₀', 'ECD (charge deficit)'. Depth and ECD pick up the channel's units on the axis label ('Depth (pA)', 'ECD (pA·s)'). ECD is computed on demand from the calibrated signal, not read from the event table.

controls.label: Y
controls.what_it_does: The Y-axis event metric for the density map.
controls.notes: Same four choices; defaults to 'Depth'.

controls.label: Log x
controls.what_it_does: Bin the X metric in log space (drops non-positive values).
controls.notes: ON by default, because dwell reads on a log axis by convention. The axis label gains '(log10)' and the axis values ARE log10 values. If every event is dropped the plot says 'No events fall on these axes. Check the log toggles (non-positive values are dropped for a log axis).'

controls.label: Log y
controls.what_it_does: Bin the Y metric in log space (drops non-positive values).
controls.notes: Off by default. Watch this one with a signed depth metric — negative depths vanish silently apart from the empty-plot message.

controls.label: Bins
controls.what_it_does: Number of bins along each axis.
controls.notes: 4–400, default 40. The same count is used for X and Y and for the marginal histograms.

controls.label: Colormap
controls.what_it_does: Sequential colour map for the density (perceptually uniform).
controls.notes: Choices: viridis (default), magma, plasma, inferno, cividis. The colour bar re-inks with it.

controls.label: Title
controls.what_it_does: Overrides the density map's title; empty uses the automatic one.
controls.notes: Placeholder reads 'title (auto)'. The automatic title is '<Y metric> vs <X metric>   ·   n = N events'.

controls.label: X label
controls.what_it_does: Overrides the x-axis label; empty uses the metric's own name.
controls.notes: Placeholder 'x label (auto)'. Overriding it also removes the '(log10)' hint the automatic label adds — if you rename a logged axis, say so yourself.

controls.label: Y label
controls.what_it_does: Overrides the y-axis label; empty uses the metric's own name.
controls.notes: Placeholder 'y label (auto)'. Same '(log10)' caveat as X label.

controls.label: Export current figure…
controls.what_it_does: Export the visible committed figure through the shared publication export dialog.
controls.notes: Choose native/physical dimensions and inspect the frozen preview; warning details stay in their own section and metadata. Export does not run a new analysis.

controls.label: Normalize time
controls.what_it_does: Duration-normalize each event onto a common [0, 1] axis (align is then immaterial).
controls.notes: ON by default; the x axis reads 'Normalized time (dwell)'. Turning it off switches the x axis to real seconds AND enables the Align combo. With it on, a 0.2 ms event and a 5 ms event are drawn the same width — good for shape, useless for duration.

controls.label: Align
controls.what_it_does: Real-time alignment reference (used only when 'Normalize time' is off).
controls.notes: Choices: start, center. It is greyed out (genuinely disabled) whenever 'Normalize time' is ticked — un-tick that checkbox to enable it.

controls.label: Points
controls.what_it_does: Samples on the common axis each event is resampled to.
controls.notes: 8–4000, default 120. Too few and short events look square; too many and nothing is gained beyond the shortest event's real sample count.

controls.label: Pad %
controls.what_it_does: Pre/post padding as a percentage of each event's dwell — how much open-pore baseline is shown either side of the event.
controls.notes: 0–200, default 20. Larger padding pushes more events past the trace edge; those are excluded and counted as 'edge-skipped' in the title. If padding excludes every event the plot says 'Every accepted event is too close to the trace edge for this padding.'

controls.label: Title
controls.what_it_does: Overrides the ensemble title; empty uses the automatic one.
controls.notes: Placeholder 'title (auto)'. The automatic title is 'Ensemble of N event(s)   ·   M edge-skipped   —   mean (solid) + median (dashed)'.

controls.label: Export current figure…
controls.what_it_does: Export the visible committed figure through the shared publication export dialog.
controls.notes: Choose native/physical dimensions and inspect the frozen preview; warning details stay in their own section and metadata. Export does not run a new analysis.

controls.label: Event reference · open-pore baseline
controls.what_it_does: Configure how open-pore current is estimated or supplied for this recording/channel.
controls.notes: Preprocess section → Open-pore baseline; choose Automatic, Known open-pore current or Selected open-pore intervals. Automatic windows and the recording probe remain available in their appropriate context.

controls.label: Rough window
controls.what_it_does: Pass 1. Decides WHICH excursions count as events. It must be several times the longest state you want treated as an event — a rough window shorter than the state it is sitting in becomes that state, and nothing gets masked. (Measured on the -600 mV apo file: its 521 ms partial clog is 15% masked at 0.5 s and 99.96% masked at 2.0 s.)
controls.notes: Range 0.002–60 s, 3 decimals, 0.1 s step, app default 0.5 s. Lowering it drags the Base window down with it (Base window can never exceed it). Editing it by hand immediately restamps the source as 'set by hand'.

controls.label: Base window
controls.what_it_does: Pass 2. Decides how fast the baseline may follow the trace. It must be SHORTER than the shortest genuine conductance level dwell, or a gating pore's steps get smoothed into the baseline instead of being measured against it.
controls.notes: Range 0.001–30 s, 4 decimals, 0.05 s step, app default 0.1 s — but its live maximum is pinned to the Rough window's current value, so you cannot type a base window wider than the rough one. To raise it, raise Rough window first.

controls.label: Decimation
controls.what_it_does: Derived from the base window, never set by hand: the estimator's cost goes as 1/decimation squared, so it is the throttle rather than a quality knob. Shown here so the cost is visible.
controls.notes: Reads as 'N  (M taps)'. Shows 'auto (sample rate unknown)' when the selected recording has no sample rate, and plain 'auto' if the current value cannot be resolved mid-edit.

controls.label: These values: …
controls.what_it_does: Where the values above came from. This travels with the analysis, so a stored result says whether anyone ever looked at this recording.
controls.notes: One of six, verbatim (BaselinePanel._SOURCE_LABELS, in the order the module lists them): 'app default (this recording was not measured)', 'measured on this recording, and confirmed', 'set by hand', 'restored from the stored analysis', 'COPIED from the batch form: set for a DIFFERENT recording -- the one selected when the batch form was filled in -- and this recording was never measured', or 'restored from an older analysis whose estimator fell back on this trace (legacy stamp; the windows were not chosen by anyone)'. This is the whole staleness story in one line — a row still reading 'app default' was never looked at, the batch line means the numbers were confirmed for SOME OTHER recording, and the fall-back line is a legacy stamp only: a probe that cannot run on the trace today stamps 'app default' and the panel prints the CLAMPED line instead. When the windows in the form were accepted over a failing check the line turns amber and carries the standing mark '— ACCEPTED OVER N FAILED HEALTH CHECKS (<the checks>). Depths and dI/I0 measured with these windows are not certifiable — see Baseline health below.' That mark survives navigating to another recording and back; it ends when the windows themselves change (a hand edit, Back to default, or a clean re-proposal).

controls.label: Measure this recording
controls.what_it_does: Look at this recording and propose a rough and base window from its own timescales, then run the health checks on what it proposes. Usually a few seconds -- measured 2 s on a 3 M-sample recording and 6 s on 9 M samples (the button says Measuring... meanwhile; it has not missed the click). Nothing is applied until you press Use these values.
controls.notes: The column above is BaselinePanel.probe_button.toolTip() byte for byte, '--' and 'Measuring...' included — tests/gui/test_s7_fixup_docs_inventory_quotes_live_surfaces.py compares the two, because the string here was once written from a fix report rather than from the widget and quoted a tooltip the button never had. On the button itself the label changes to 'Measuring…' (an ellipsis, where the tooltip spells three dots) while the probe runs off-thread, and a second click is refused. The button is never Qt-disabled: when it cannot run it is dimmed and clicking it posts the reason in the amber line beneath — 'Select a current channel to measure its baseline.', 'Detection runs on CURRENT channels; this is a <kind> channel.', 'Sample rate unknown — dwell time is undefined without a time base, so detection is disabled for this recording.', or 'Still measuring this recording — one moment.'

controls.label: Use these values
controls.what_it_does: Accept the proposed windows. This is the confirmation step — the app never applies a measured parameter on its own. If the health block below condemns what was proposed, the first press explains what is wrong instead of applying it, and the second press accepts it anyway — with the panel saying so from then on. (Verbatim tooltip.)
controls.notes: Dimmed until a probe has produced a proposal; clicking it before then posts 'Nothing has been proposed yet. Press Measure this recording first, then this button applies what it found.' Over a condemned proposal the first click posts the REFUSED notice naming the checks that condemn it and arms the override; the button then relabels itself 'Use these values anyway' and turns amber, and the second click applies — after which the source line above carries the standing ACCEPTED OVER … FAILED HEALTH CHECKS mark. A new proposal disarms the override. Once applied, the values are marked confirmed and are protected from being overwritten when a stored detection is loaded — that protection ends only when you select a different recording/channel.

controls.label: Back to default
controls.what_it_does: Return to the app default (0.5 s / 0.1 s). A defensible floor for an unseen recording, and provably wrong for some — measure instead where you can.
controls.notes: Always active. It discards a confirmed measurement and resets the source line to 'app default (this recording was not measured)'.

controls.label: (amber gate line)
controls.what_it_does: Appears under the buttons to say why a click did nothing, always naming the FIRST thing you would have to fix rather than a downstream blocker.
controls.notes: Hidden until a blocked click, and hidden again as soon as the blocker clears.

controls.label: Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: The finished probe's findings, as a small table: 'Noise (robust sigma)', 'Longest state' (with a state count), 'Median state (base_s floor)' (the median state the base window is floored against, e.g. '20.7 ms -> base_s >= 100 ms'), 'Pore stepping (gating)' (yes/no with a ×noise score), 'Level dwell' when one was found, then 'Proposed rough window', 'Proposed base window' and 'Decimation (derived)'. Under those, one 'Ranked: <window>' row per window the probe actually ESTIMATED — each naming both criteria it was judged on, the MEDIAN share of each state's depth the baseline follows and the WORST single state it rides into — with the winner marked '— CHOSEN'. Then a plain-language reason that says why that window was taken and where the search stopped.
controls.notes: Hidden until a probe finishes, and cleared the moment you select a different recording — a proposal belongs to the recording it was measured on. If the probe could not measure, the reason line turns amber and is prefixed 'Could not measure -- '. Nothing here is applied until 'Use these values' is pressed.

controls.label: Baseline health
controls.what_it_does: Checks the reference implementation does not perform. They catch the regimes where this estimator fails SILENTLY — a mask that found nothing, a mask that swallowed the recording, drift faster than the rough window, and a trace too short for the two-pass structure.
controls.notes: Shown as soon as a probe returns — captioned 'These N checks were run on the windows PROPOSED above, before anything was measured with them. This is the evidence for the Apply click.' — and again after a detection, captioned 'These N checks describe the windows the detection on screen was measured under…'. The two are not interchangeable and the caption is the only thing that tells them apart. Bullets are colour-coded worst-first: refuse (red), warn (amber), info (grey), ok (green), with labels 'recording vs tracking window', 'recording vs rough window', 'mask fraction' (or 'mask fraction (floor)' / '(ceiling)'), 'mask vs a wide-window mask', 'base window vs state dwell', 'baseline vs the open pore beside each state', 'rough-pass sigma vs final noise', 'tracked level vs the recording's own histogram', 'overshoot' and 'trace vs tracking window'. Nine rows on all three reference recordings; the count is data-dependent, which is why the caption states it. It is rebuilt from stored provenance when a project is reopened, so an old suspect baseline never goes quiet.

controls.label: Recording
controls.what_it_does: The top box of the left-hand control column, holding Source, Compare with and Refresh. The recording chosen here is the PRIMARY one: it sets the segment window, the RMS band range and the y units of the whole plot.

controls.label: Segment (quiet open-pore baseline)
controls.what_it_does: The box that decides which slice of the trace the spectrum is computed from (Start, End, Use full trace and the samples/seconds read-out). Its name is the instruction: pick a quiet open-pore stretch, not one full of events.

controls.label: Welch estimate
controls.what_it_does: The FFT settings box (Segment length, Window, Overlap). Every overlaid comparison curve is computed with these same settings so the pores are compared like for like.

controls.label: Display
controls.what_it_does: The box holding Log-log axes and Amplitude spectral density. Changes here only redraw what is already computed, so they are instant and never re-run the FFT.

controls.label: RMS noise band
controls.what_it_does: The box holding f low, f high and the RMS in band read-out — the integrated noise figure over the frequency band you choose. Defaults to 0 Hz to Nyquist, i.e. the total RMS.

controls.label: Style
controls.what_it_does: The box holding Title, Data colour, Fit colour, Background and Export size — everything that changes how the saved figure looks rather than what it measures.

controls.label: Auto
controls.group: Noise spectrum ▸ Welch estimate ▸ Segment length
controls.what_it_does: The default Segment length entry: the app picks the FFT size that balances variance against frequency resolution (about 8 or more averaged segments). The other entries are the fixed sizes 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768 and 65536 — longer gives finer low-frequency detail but a noisier curve.

controls.label: hann
controls.what_it_does: The default taper applied to each segment before the FFT. The other choices are hamming, blackman, bartlett, blackmanharris, flattop and boxcar (boxcar = no taper).

controls.label: Light
controls.what_it_does: One of the two Background choices (the other, Dark, is the default): Light gives a white canvas with dark ink for publication, and the legend and axis ink re-colour with it.

controls.label: Capture rate (Hz)
controls.what_it_does: The default Metric: events per second in each recording, plotted against that recording's applied voltage. This is the one the exponential A·exp(V/V₀) fit is meant for.

controls.label: Median dwell (s)
controls.what_it_does: Plots each recording's median event duration in seconds against its applied voltage.

controls.label: Median depth (pA)
controls.what_it_does: Plots each recording's median blockage depth in pA (the median of the event table's depth_pA column) against its applied voltage.

controls.label: Median dI/I₀
controls.what_it_does: Plot the median recorded fractional depth against voltage.
controls.notes: Dimensionless does not guarantee comparability: review offset, reference construction and pore context.

controls.label: Event count
controls.what_it_does: Plots the raw number of events per recording against voltage (not divided by recording length, unlike Capture rate).

controls.label: none
controls.what_it_does: The default Fit entry: scatter only, no trend line, and the fit headline and fit parameters stay blank.

controls.label: linear
controls.what_it_does: Fits a straight line to the plotted points and reports slope and intercept; the headline then reads 'slope = …'. Needs at least 2 recordings at different voltages, otherwise the details box says so.

controls.label: exponential
controls.what_it_does: Fits the A·exp(V/V₀) capture-rate model and reports A and V₀; the headline then reads 'V₀ = … V'. The fit is run on whichever x-axis is showing, so it follows the |V| toggle.

controls.label: V (mV)
controls.what_it_does: The middle column of the Per recording table, giving each recording's applied voltage in millivolts; the first column is 'Recording' and the third takes the name of the selected metric (it reads 'metric' until points exist). Rows are sorted by voltage, are read-only, and list every gathered point even when no fit could be made.

controls.label: Dwell (s)
controls.group: Event waveforms ▸ Event-count heatmap ▸ X and Y
controls.what_it_does: Event duration in seconds — the default X metric, and the one Log x is on for by default.

controls.label: Depth
controls.group: Event waveforms ▸ Event-count heatmap ▸ X and Y
controls.what_it_does: Blockage depth — the default Y metric. The axis label picks up the channel's units, so it prints as 'Depth (pA)' on a pA channel.

controls.label: dI/I₀
controls.group: Event waveforms ▸ Event-count heatmap ▸ X and Y
controls.what_it_does: Use the recorded fractional event depth as a heatmap metric.
controls.notes: Physical interpretation depends on the recorded open-pore reference; it is not universally gain/calibration independent.

controls.label: ECD (charge deficit)
controls.group: Event waveforms ▸ Event-count heatmap ▸ X and Y
controls.what_it_does: Equivalent charge deficit — the area of each blockage, computed on demand from the trace rather than read from the event table. Its axis prints with the channel units, e.g. 'ECD (pA·s)'.

controls.label: center
controls.what_it_does: Lines the events up on their midpoints instead of their starts, which is the better view for events of unequal length. Only selectable when Normalize time is off.

controls.label: viridis
controls.what_it_does: The default density colour map; the other entries are magma, plasma, inferno and cividis. All five are perceptually uniform, and the colour bar beside the map follows the choice.

controls.label: title (auto)
controls.group: Event waveforms ▸ Event-count heatmap and Ensemble
controls.what_it_does: The grey hint inside the Title box: leave it empty and the plot titles itself (density: 'Y vs X · n = … events'; ensemble: 'Ensemble of N event(s) — mean (solid) + median (dashed)'). The X label and Y label boxes hint 'x label (auto)' and 'y label (auto)' the same way.

controls.label: Measuring…
controls.what_it_does: What the Measure this recording button renames itself to while the probe is running. It stays clickable, but a second click is refused with 'Still measuring this recording — one moment.' in the amber line; the button reverts once the proposal arrives.

controls.label: Noise (robust sigma)
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: First row of the proposal table: the noise level the probe measured on this trace, in pA (or 'n/a' when it could not be measured).

controls.label: Longest state
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: The longest steady non-open-pore state the probe found, in milliseconds, with how many states it saw — this is what the rough window has to be several times longer than. Reads 'none found' on a clean trace.

controls.label: Pore stepping (gating)
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: Whether the pore looks like it is gating (stepping between conductance levels), given as 'yes -- N x noise' or 'no -- N x noise'. A gating pore needs much shorter windows than a quiet one.

controls.label: Level dwell
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: How long the pore sits at one conductance level, in milliseconds. Only shown when the probe found stepping; the base window must stay shorter than this.

controls.label: Proposed rough window
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: The pass-1 window the probe suggests, in seconds. Nothing changes in the form until you press Use these values.

controls.label: Proposed base window
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: The pass-2 window the probe suggests, shown in milliseconds (the Base window spin box above shows the same number in seconds).

controls.label: Decimation (derived)
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: The decimation the proposed base window implies, or 'auto' when the sample rate is not known. It is never set by hand — it is shown so the cost of the settings is visible.

controls.label: Could not measure --
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: The prefix put in front of the explanation line under the proposal table when the probe could not measure the recording; the whole line turns amber. Without the prefix the same line, in grey, is the plain-English reason the confident proposal was made.

controls.label: Ranked: <rough> s / <base> ms
controls.group: Open-pore baseline ▸ Proposed for this recording
controls.what_it_does: One row per window the probe actually ESTIMATED, carrying BOTH criteria the ranking decides on: the MEDIAN share of each state's own depth the tracked baseline follows ("baseline follows N% of the state depth (M states; worst single state K%)", or "follows NONE of the state depth" when the reading is at or below zero), and the worst single state beside it. A window whose baseline followed more than 50% of any ONE state's excursion reads "… but RIDES INTO a <N> ms state at t = <T> s, <K>% of its excursion followed" and loses to any window that stays out, before the medians are compared at all. The winner is marked "— CHOSEN"; a rung that could not be measured reads "not measurable here".
controls.notes: Rows exist only for rungs the search estimated — the reason paragraph underneath counts and names the ones it stopped short of and never claims a reading for them. Ties go to the SHORTEST window, because a longer one tracks slower drift less well. When the ranking overrides the window the rule derived, the reason paragraph says so in capitals before any of its evidence ("THE <window> DERIVED ABOVE IS THE RULE'S WINDOW AND NOT WHAT THE APP OFFERS … the ranking that follows SUPERSEDES it with <window>."), so the numbers earlier in that explanation are not always the ones being offered.

controls.label: Reference mode
controls.what_it_does: Choose Automatic (existing estimator), Known open-pore current, or Selected open-pore intervals.
controls.notes: Recording/channel-specific; changing the draft alone leaves existing events unchanged. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Open-pore current (pA)
controls.what_it_does: Enter the signed known current.
controls.notes: Enter the signed, calibrated current justified for THIS recording/channel; −120 pA is not interchangeable with +120 pA. This supplies a constant reference rather than subtracting a baseline from the source trace. It can still change residual-noise estimation, automatic polarity, event boundaries, counts and measurements when Detect is run. It does not make those results independent of the recording. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; nanoscope/analysis/open_pore_reference.py.

controls.label: Start (s) / End (s)
controls.what_it_does: Edit recording-relative half-open [start, end) open-pore intervals.
controls.notes: These are seconds, not absolute instrument times or sample indices. Intervals must be ordered, non-overlapping, within the trace and contain at least five samples; that minimum is validation, not proof the pore was open. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Add current trace selection
controls.what_it_does: Add the Measure selection as an open-pore interval.
controls.notes: Transfers sample-based selection to recording-relative seconds; ensure the selected span is genuinely open pore. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Add interval
controls.what_it_does: Append an interval row for direct editing.
controls.notes: A blank/new interval is invalid until valid bounds are supplied. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Remove selected
controls.what_it_does: Remove selected interval rows from the reference draft.
controls.notes: Does not delete raw samples or automatically rerun detection. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Constant reference (stable recording)
controls.what_it_does: Use the pooled median of samples from the selected open intervals.
controls.notes: Longer intervals contribute more samples; not an unweighted mean of interval medians. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Linear between interval anchors (drift)
controls.what_it_does: Interpolate between interval median levels at their sampled centers.
controls.notes: Needs at least two intervals. Holds endpoint levels outside the anchor range, rather than extrapolating. Sparse anchors can perform worse on curved drift. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Optional source / notes (saved with analysis)
controls.what_it_does: Record why the current or selected intervals represent open pore.
controls.notes: Include external measurement provenance or explain interval selection. A note is not scientific validation. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Preview reference and detection…
controls.what_it_does: Preview a supported manual reference and its detector result without committing.
controls.notes: Uses the configured detector on full-resolution arrays. Display decimation is min/max presentation only. Candidate count and accepted count differ; inspect Details and warnings. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Show this baseline on the trace
controls.what_it_does: Show the configured baseline as a trace overlay.
controls.notes: Visualization is not a new detection. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Subtract baseline (display only)
controls.what_it_does: Show a baseline-subtracted display.
controls.notes: Not the runtime Baseline drift preprocessing stage and not a new analysis result. Source: nanoscope/gui/baseline_panel.py; open_pore_preview.py; nanoscope/analysis/baseline.py.

controls.label: Show
controls.what_it_does: Choose Welch PSD, FFT, Spectrogram or All-points histogram.
controls.notes: All views use the same selected span of the raw calibrated recording, not the detector conditioning chain. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: FFT
controls.what_it_does: Show one tapered transform of the whole span.
controls.notes: Uses the Window control; Welch Segment length and Overlap do not apply. Full 1/T resolution is not inherently a better noise estimate. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Spectrogram
controls.what_it_does: Show log-power across time and frequency.
controls.notes: Choose Time resolution; a short segment improves time resolution while worsening frequency resolution. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Time resolution
controls.what_it_does: Choose spectrogram samples per time column.
controls.notes: Auto targets roughly 400 columns, unlike Welch Auto targeting roughly eight averages. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: All-points histogram
controls.what_it_does: Count raw calibrated samples by current level.
controls.notes: Populated modes do not prove which level is open pore. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Bins
controls.what_it_does: Choose amplitude-bin resolution for the all-points histogram.
controls.notes: More bins resolve nearby modes but also more counting noise. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Clip outliers (0.01–99.99%)
controls.what_it_does: Restrict the drawn current range to these quantiles.
controls.notes: Excluded samples are counted in the details; not silently discarded from the source recording. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Mark the populated levels
controls.what_it_does: Overlay estimated occupied histogram modes.
controls.notes: These are occupied levels, not automatic certification of open pore or event identity. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Export data (CSV)…
controls.what_it_does: Export numerical data for the selected noise view.
controls.notes: Retain source/span, units, window and estimator metadata with the figure. Source: nanoscope/gui/psd_panel.py.

controls.label: Analyze…
controls.what_it_does: Open the explicit Subpopulations analysis workflow.
controls.notes: Section and appearance changes never rerun feature extraction, PCA, clustering or mixture analysis. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.

controls.label: Embedding / Colour by
controls.what_it_does: Choose the displayed captured embedding and grouping.
controls.notes: Exploratory visual comparison, not independent confirmation of molecular species. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.

controls.label: Export report and tables…
controls.what_it_does: Export report text, JSON settings/caveats and numerical tables.
controls.notes: Includes event membership/posteriors, population summaries and available embedding/waveform data; does not merely save a screenshot. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.

controls.label: Copy report
controls.what_it_does: Copy the whole report including caveats.
controls.notes: Keep caveats when circulating clean figure artwork. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.

controls.label: Event gallery…
controls.what_it_does: Review report-linked event tiles and subpopulation classes.
controls.notes: A statistical assignment is not an accept/reject decision or an identified analyte. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.

controls.label: Colour the trace
controls.what_it_does: Shade the main trace with the report class colors.
controls.notes: Presentation only; original detector classifications and measurements are not replaced. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.

controls.label: Caveats
controls.what_it_does: Read the persistent caveat summary and expandable report details.
controls.notes: Caveats stay outside plot artwork and travel with report/provenance exports. Source: nanoscope/gui/subpop_window.py; main_window.py.
